distance-running.title: Class 1
distance-running.effort: Build repeatable ankle spring and leg-force reserve for controlled single-leg support during distance running.

exercises.name: Stationary Bilateral Ankle Pogo
exercises.dose: 2 × 8 hops, bodyweight; 60 s after each set
exercises.description: Main repeated ankle-spring practice. Hands on hips; make small two-foot bounces in place, with soft knees and ankles moving freely. Record the quality marker. End the set if rhythm/position deteriorates; use lower amplitude instead of chasing height.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Pogo in Place
exercises.dose: 1 × 4 hops per leg; 90 s between legs and after the second leg
exercises.description: Apply spring-like ankle force while one leg supports the pelvis. Hands on hips; stay over the foot and finish balanced. Reduce amplitude for drift; if needed, use light fingertip support on a stable bench instead of unsupported execution, with the same dose. Do not change this to alternating jogging.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Forward Hop to Stick
exercises.dose: 1 × 3 per leg; 12–15 s between reps, 90 s between legs and afterward
exercises.description: Quick single-leg push followed by controlled forward weight acceptance. Take off and land on the same leg over a short, self-selected distance, no more than one of the athlete's foot lengths today. Hold 2 s, then walk back and reset. Use a shorter distance instead of a farther unstable landing; stop for repeated extra balance steps.

exercises.name: Squat Jump — paused, hands on hips
exercises.sourceName: Squat Jump — paused, hands on hips
exercises.dose: 1 × 3; 12–15 s between reps, 90 s afterward
exercises.description: Express hip/knee extension quickly from stillness, complementing the ankle-dominant anchor. Hold a comfortable quarter-to-half squat for 2 s, jump vertically without another dip, then absorb and hold the two-foot landing for 2 s. Lower jump height for a hard landing; repeated re-dipping ends the task.

exercises.name: Split-Squat Jump to Stick — no leg switch
exercises.sourceName: Split-Squat Jump to Stick — no leg switch
exercises.dose: 1 × 3 per lead leg; 12–15 s between reps, 90 s between sides and afterward
exercises.description: Produce quick force from an asymmetric stance while keeping the pelvis facing forward. From a comfortable floor split stance, dip shallowly, jump a small height and land in the same stance, holding 2 s. Both feet participate: this is not a single-leg landing. Use a shallower dip/lower flight instead of switching legs or losing alignment.

exercises.name: Two-hand Kettlebell Swing
exercises.dose: 2 × 5 swings; light-to-moderate bell selected for crisp speed; 90 s after each set
exercises.description: Rapid hip extension against an external load, with no additional jump landing. Hinge, snap hips tall and let the bell float to no higher than chest height; feet stay planted. Park under control after rep five. Reduce the bell load for arm lifting, back extension or slowing; stop if the hinge cannot stay controlled.

exercises.description: Strengthen active arch control for a stable contact platform. Stand on both feet; gently draw the target forefoot toward its heel without curling toes or raising the heel. Only one foot is targeted at a time. Use seated execution instead of standing if toe gripping or cramping appears.

exercises.description: Main bent-knee plantarflexor strength exposure for the ankle's stance-support role. Sit on a stable bench, knees near 90°, DBs secured by hands on lower thighs above the knees. From the floor, rise for 1 s, hold 1 s, lower 2 s; no bounce. Reduce load for lost heel height or discomfort at the implement contact.

Rise 1 s, hold 1 s, lower 2 s; do not lock the knee or roll the ankle. Reduce load for lost range; use both legs instead of one at 1 × 8 if a unilateral bodyweight set is already too hard.

exercises.name: Glute Bridge Walkout
exercises.dose: 1 × 4 complete cycles; 90 s afterward
exercises.description: Challenge hamstrings as the knee opens and closes while the pelvis stays supported, distinct from P2's loaded hip hinge. From a floor bridge, take four small alternating heel steps out, then four back: 8 steps = 1 rep. About 1 s per step; keep breathing and hips level. Choose heel reach to make four cycles challenging with 2–3 sound cycles available. Shorten reach for pelvic sag or cramping; no extra cycles.

exercises.name: Supine Band-resisted Hip Flexion
exercises.dose: 1 × 6 per leg; 2 s up, 1 s hold, 2 s down; 60 s between legs, 90 s afterward
exercises.description: Load the hip flexors' leg-recovery action while the trunk/pelvis stay quiet. A suitable closed-loop band surrounds both forefeet: keep the nonworking leg extended with heel grounded, bend/lift the working thigh toward vertical, then return without arching or moving the anchor foot. Choose band tension for 2–3 RIR; reduce tension/range for pelvic tilt or foot slippage.

distance-running.quality: Within E1's two scheduled eight-hop sets, record clean landings out of attempts: centred contacts, similar low height/rhythm, and no progressive deep knee bend or trunk drift. Record the reason for any stop. These observations do not measure running economy or ground-contact time. Keep surface, shoes, hand position and intent consistent for later comparison.
distance-running.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1. Reference only; its contents and duration are not supplied and are not created or modified here. The existing sequence used must already respect the no-running requirement; if it does not, that preparation conflict needs resolving before delivery. No alternative sequence is authored here.
distance-running.explosiveNotes: E1 is the primary repeatability anchor. Quick force expression matters; maximum height, distance and exhaustion do not. Start each set recovered. The modest supporting doses preserve quality for the later strength work.

distance-running.title: Class 2
distance-running.effort: Keep ankle return centred while the support position changes slightly, preserving leg-force reserve for repeated stance.
distance-running.delivery: Allow about 72–82 min beyond Access & Prepare 1 for one coached athlete or an efficiently equipped small wave, including stated recovery, lift preparation, handling and notes. The full class duration is unresolved. Maintain this exercise order; no timed circuit. Use separate cleared bays within the three separate 10 m lanes; check width, queues and equipment quantities onsite. Rest after the last set may include the next setup once, not twice. Bigger groups, scarce implements or extra instruction extend the clock. Check any 60/90-minute booking against actual preparation and group flow rather than borrowing another program’s timetable. Timing and audit.

exercises.description: Main accuracy task: produce a quick ankle return while controlling very small fore-aft displacement. Use a floor seam or two positions indicated by cones outside the landing area, less than one foot length apart. Jump across and back with both feet together, low height and soft knees. Shorten travel for drift; end a set if it becomes a squat-jump pattern.

distance-running.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1; reference only, do not create or modify it. Its content, load, duration and no-running compatibility remain unverified. The existing sequence selected must already meet the no-running constraint; resolve any mismatch before delivery. distance-running.explosiveNotes: E1 is first with two sets; the more demanding nominated-leg receiving follows a shared raised landing task while fresh. The final three tasks have small doses and full resets; no long horizontal or switching-lunge circuit. Bodyweight unless a light implement/band is specified. Ballistic loads must permit crisp acceleration without grinding.

distance-running.title: Class 9
distance-running.effort: Express leg force rapidly against manageable external resistance while keeping the foot and pelvis organized.
distance-running.delivery: Allow about 67–77 min beyond Access & Prepare 1 for one coached athlete or an efficiently equipped small wave, including stated recovery, lift preparation, handling and notes. The full class duration is unresolved. Maintain this exercise order; no timed circuit. Use separate cleared bays within the three separate 10 m lanes; check width, queues and equipment quantities onsite. Rest after the last set may include the next setup once, not twice. Bigger groups, scarce implements or extra instruction extend the clock. Check any 60/90-minute booking against actual preparation and group flow rather than borrowing another program’s timetable. Timing and audit.

Timing and audit.

sprinting.title: Class 3
sprinting.effort: Direct each leg's push into forward projection and transfer to the next support without pelvic rotation or reaching. Pair that work with rapid free-leg recovery and targeted strength.

exercises.name: Three-Point Start Acceleration — first two steps
exercises.sourceName: Three-Point Start Acceleration — first two steps
exercises.dose: 2 × 2 starts, one with each front leg per pair. Front toes at 1 m; fit the entire starting body inside 0–2 m. At most 2 driving strikes or 3 m of drive, ending by 4 m; progressively slow and stop by 9 m. 75 s between starts; 120 s between pairs.
exercises.description: Main launch task: coordinate release of hand support with the legs' forward push. Use staggered feet and the hand opposite the front leg on the floor; choose comfortable spacing that allows both feet to push without a cramped crouch. Hold still briefly, then release and drive without twisting. First pair uses controlled fast intent to establish stopping; second pair uses the fastest clean intent that preserves it. No blocks or maximal-load test.

exercises.rest: See prescribed recovery

exercises.name: Rapid Step-Up to Knee Drive — no flight
exercises.sourceName: Rapid Step-Up to Knee Drive — no flight
exercises.dose: 1 × 3 per working leg, bodyweight; rapid rise, 1 s tall finish, 2 s controlled lower. 10 s reset between reps; 45 s between legs.
exercises.description: Make the elevated leg supply most of the upward push while the other thigh recovers. Whole working foot on a stable low box; front knee below hip level at the start. Rise quickly without bouncing off the floor leg, hopping off the box or lifting the working heel. The free knee rises naturally as the body comes up; return that foot gently to the floor, keeping the working foot on the box. Lower the box height for pelvic hitching or loss of forceful ascent.

exercises.name: Forward Bound to Opposite-Leg Stick
exercises.dose: 1 × 2 per takeoff leg; modest distance, natural arms. 20 s between same-takeoff reps; 45 s between legs.
exercises.description: Transfer a forward push from one leg into controlled support on the other, rather than receiving every projection on two feet. From one-leg support, use a small dip, bound forward and hold the opposite-leg landing 2 s before setting the free foot down. Keep the pelvis facing forward; shorten distance for reaching, trunk rotation or an unstable receiver. No linked bounds.

exercises.name: Broad Jump to Stick — countermovement and arm swing
exercises.sourceName: Broad Jump to Stick — countermovement and arm swing
exercises.dose: 2 × 2; natural arms, one smooth dip and immediate forward jump. 20 s between reps; 90 s between sets.
exercises.description: Integrate arm action and a dynamic leg drive into horizontal projection. This differs from Class 1's paused, hands-on-hips jump: there is no held squat or deliberate interruption of the dip. Land on both feet and hold 2 s; select a distance that permits control rather than chasing a record.

exercises.name: Standing Single-Leg Cycle and Strike
exercises.dose: 1 × 3 cycles per moving leg. One compact recovery cycle followed by a quick target-foot strike; 10 s reset between reps, 45 s between legs.
exercises.description: Rehearse returning the free foot beneath the pelvis while the other leg provides stable support. Keep the support foot planted. Recover the moving heel beneath the hip, bring the thigh forward through a comfortable range, let the lower leg unfold without kicking, then place the foot quickly beside the support foot. No running travel or hopping on the support leg. Reduce cycle height/range for leaning, a long backswing or an ahead-of-body strike. A rep is one complete recovery-and-strike cycle.

exercises.name: Supine Banded Knee Drive — opposite heel grounded
exercises.sourceName: Supine Banded Knee Drive — opposite heel grounded
exercises.dose: 1 × 3 per moving leg, very light band. Quick knee drive, 1 s finish, 2 s controlled lower; 10 s reset between reps, 45 s between legs.
exercises.description: Express rapid thigh recovery against light elastic resistance while the pelvis is supported, complementing E5's placement task. Lie with both legs comfortably long and heels on the floor, a suitable closed band around both shoe midfeet. Keep the nonmoving leg long, heel grounded and foot secure; quickly bend/lift the moving knee toward the torso as the band stretches, then lower under control. Stop the lift before pelvic movement or the band's stretch limit. The grounded heel must not slide or lift. The band must oppose the knee drive, not assist it; do not start with the opposite thigh raised. Use lighter resistance/shorter range for a slowed drive, rolling band or loss of pelvic control.

exercises.description: Maintain heel and both forefoot bases while gently raising the working arch, supporting the foot used to push and the opposite foot receiving the bound. Keep toes long; reduce effort or use seated foot doming instead of standing for clawing or rolling.

exercises.description: Give the lateral hip a small strengthening dose for keeping the pelvis level/directed forward during step-up, bound reception and the planted-leg cycle. Bottom knee bent, top leg aligned with torso, toes forward; reduce range if the pelvis rolls or the thigh moves forward.

exercises.description: Main strength anchor: load lead-leg knee/hip extension in a split base while preserving pelvis direction. Both feet remain on the floor; modest whole-trunk inclination without rounding. Reduce depth/load for knee collapse, rotation or rear-leg hopping.

exercises.name: Seated Dumbbell Hip Flexion

exercises.description: Build force for lifting the thigh through a stable seated range, complementary to E6's light rapid drive from a longer-leg starting position. Secure a DB across the distal thigh above the knee with both hands; lift the knee a few centimetres without hand assistance or leaning, then return the foot gently. Use a stable fitted seat with foot supported and knee initially near a right angle. Reduce load/range for pinching, tipping or shifting load.

exercises.name: Glute Bridge Walkout

Keep pelvis raised and knees soft at the far endpoint; return to original heel positions. Shorten steps for sag/cramp; do not lengthen them just to compensate for the lower rep count. Stop if control cannot be restored.

sprinting.explosiveNotes: E1 is the primary performance task. Complete the exercises in order, with quick, clean intent and modest supporting doses. Rapid force expression does not require every exercise to include flight.

sprinting.title: Class 4
sprinting.effort: Keep the pelvis and trunk organized over the supporting leg while the other leg returns quickly to a nearby foot placement. Train upright support and rapid limb action within a stationary gym footprint.

exercises.name: Stationary A-Run — alternating high-knee exchanges
exercises.dose: 2 × 6 alternating foot contacts, 3/foot/set; 90 s between sets. Bodyweight; quick rhythm without chasing cadence. Start the sets on opposite support legs.
exercises.description: Main task: alternate a bent-knee thigh recovery and rapid support exchange while staying tall. Begin on one foot with the other knee comfortably raised; make small airborne exchanges, landing the incoming foot close to its normal standing position as the opposite thigh lifts. No extra bounce between exchanges, forced hip-height target, backward lean or deliberate clawing. Finish on contact six, stabilize, then set the other foot down. Reduce knee height/cadence for drift, reaching or loss of posture.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Vertical Jump to Same-Leg Stick
exercises.sourceName: Single-Leg Vertical Jump to Same-Leg Stick
exercises.dose: 1 × 2 per leg, bodyweight, natural arms; modest height with forceful takeoff. 20 s between same-leg reps; 45 s between legs.
exercises.description: Produce an upward push and receive it over the same foot, separating vertical support from the earlier forward bounds. Use one small countermovement, jump upward and hold the same-leg landing 2 s before the free foot touches down. Keep the pelvis facing forward and knee tracking with the foot. Lower height for reaching, rotation or a second hop; do not add a rebound.

exercises.name: Straight-Leg Scissor Bounce in Place
exercises.dose: 1 × 6 alternating landing contacts, 3/foot; bodyweight, very low flight.
exercises.description: Repeatedly exchange support through the ankles with the knees nearly straight, unlike E1's bent-knee recovery and E2's larger leg drive. Start on one foot; use a tiny forward/backward leg exchange in flight and receive the next foot near the standing position. Knees stay soft, not locked; no high kicks, long reach, double bounce or forward travel. Finish contact six under control, then set the other foot down. Reduce amplitude/speed for hard contacts or lost rhythm.

exercises.dose: 1 × 3 per moving leg; bodyweight. Quick floor tap/return, 1 s balanced finish; 10 s reset between reps, 45 s between legs.
exercises.description: Maintain a level pelvis as the free foot moves between a raised-knee position and a lower contact surface. Keep the entire support foot on a stable platform approximately 10 cm high; begin with the other thigh comfortably raised. Quickly lower that free foot to a light floor touch beside the platform and return the knee, allowing a small support-knee bend as needed. Switch the arms with the free leg. The support foot stays on the platform: this is not a jumping box exchange or a step-up. Reduce knee range/speed for a hip hitch, forceful floor push or trunk tilt.

exercises.name: Arm Action Drill — seated fast exchanges
exercises.sourceName: Arm Action Drill — seated fast exchanges
exercises.dose: 2 × 4 continuous arm exchanges, bodyweight; 75 s between sets. One rep switches both arms from their opposing positions to the other positions; 8 total exchanges.
exercises.description: Practice quick opposing arm action while the torso stays organized, without adding another ankle-impact task. Sit tall on a fitted stable bench, feet on the floor, no backrest assistance. Move relaxed bent arms forward/backward from the shoulders within a comfortable sprint-like range. Hands do not cross the trunk or strike the seat; avoid shrugging or exaggerated rocking. Use the fastest relaxed exchanges that preserve posture; reduce speed/range if the trunk supplies the movement. This isolates arm action, not complete arm–leg timing.

exercises.sourceName: Single-Leg Glute Bridge — rapid hip drive

exercises.description: Express hip-extension force rapidly as the hip approaches neutral, supporting the upright position without another landing. Lie with the working foot flat, knee bent; hold the free thigh comfortably toward the torso. Drive the pelvis up quickly until the working thigh and trunk align, then lower under control. Keep the pelvis level, heel down and ribs settled; no lumbar arch, foot launch or maximal bridge height. Shorten the rise for twisting or cramp; if a single-leg drive cannot remain crisp, use the stated replacement.

exercises.name: Stationary Single-Leg High-Knee Run
exercises.dose: 1 × 3 cycles per target leg; 90 s between target legs. One cycle = target-foot running contact plus opposite-foot running contact: 12 total contacts, 6/foot.
exercises.description: Main task: repeatedly recover one thigh while the other leg uses a low, compact running step. Begin supported on the opposite leg with target thigh comfortably raised. Exchange onto the target foot, then onto the opposite foot as the target heel folds beneath the hip and its thigh rises again. Repeat this asymmetric rhythm without a full cycle on the low-step leg. Use small flight, natural arms and nearby foot contacts; do not hop twice on one foot. Finish the third cycle under control. Lower knee height/speed for long backswing, drift, reaching or backward lean.

sprinting.effort: Initiate a strong forward push from a settled position, expressing hip/leg force without a preceding approach or repeated rebound. Support the push with a stable body line and rapid free-thigh recovery.

exercises.name: Seated Sprint Start — first two steps
exercises.sourceName: Seated Sprint Start — first two steps
exercises.dose: 2 × 2 starts, one with each first stepping foot per pair. Start with feet at the 1 m line; at most 2 driving strikes or 3 m of drive, ending by the 4 m line. Progressively slow and stop by 9 m. 75 s between starts; 120 s between pairs.
exercises.description: Main task: transfer support from the seat to the feet and initiate forward travel without backward rocking. Sit at the front of a stable fitted bench/box, both feet flat near hip width, knees comfortably bent and trunk slightly inclined forward. Settle for 2 s, then push up/forward through the legs and take the selected first step; arms assist naturally but hands do not push the seat. First pair uses controlled fast intent to establish stopping; second uses the fastest clean intent that preserves it. No jump off the seat.

exercises.description: Rehearse rapid force onset through the legs while the body line remains fixed. With both palms on a verified immovable wall near shoulder height, take a comfortable split stance and shallow forward lean. Front foot stays fully planted, rear forefoot supports; quickly push the floor back through the front leg while the hands transmit pressure to the wall. No arm pressing motion, heel pop, rocking, breath-holding or maximal strain. Step out of the lean during recovery. Reduce pressure/lean for lost position; no measured rate-of-force-development claim is made.

sprinting.effort: Leave a stable crouched start with consecutive forward pushes, recovering the free leg promptly while maintaining a useful support line.

exercises.sourceName: Four-Point Crouch Start — first two steps, no blocks
exercises.dose: 2 × 2 starts, one with each leg forward per pair. Front toes at 1 m; at most 2 driving strikes or 3 m of drive, ending by 4 m. Progressively slow and stop by 9 m. 75 s between starts; 120 s between pairs.
exercises.description: Main task: coordinate release from two-hand support into successive leg pushes. Use a comfortable staggered crouch, both hands shoulder-width on the floor just ahead of the front foot, shoulders near the hands, knees clear and spine/head comfortably aligned. Fit the entire starting stance inside 0–2 m. Settle 2 s, push through both feet and release both hands into natural opposing arm action; no preliminary hop or forced head-down posture. First pair is controlled-fast to establish stopping; use faster intent in the second only while control remains.

exercises.name: Repeated Broad Jump — two consecutive jumps, final stick
exercises.sourceName: Repeated Broad Jump — two consecutive jumps, final stick
exercises.dose: 2 × 2 consecutive jumps, bodyweight, natural arms; 120 s between two-jump bouts. Modest distances, no approach.
exercises.description: Accept the first forward landing and use it for another forward push without a deliberate pause. Start with parallel feet and a comfortable dip; make two small broad jumps, then hold the second landing 2 s. sprinting.title: Class 12
sprinting.effort: Maintain upright support while the legs recover promptly and the feet return nearby; finish with repeatable observations that can guide the next training decision.

exercises.name: Stationary A-Run — alternating high-knee exchanges
exercises.dose: 2 × 6 alternating foot contacts, 3/foot/set; 90 s between sets. Bodyweight; quick rhythm without chasing cadence. Start the sets on opposite support legs.
exercises.description: Main task; intentional Class 4 repeat: alternate compact bent-knee recovery and rapid support while staying tall. Begin on one foot, other knee comfortably raised; use small airborne exchanges and natural opposing arms. Place each foot near its standing position without extra bounce, forced knee height, backward lean or clawing. After contact six, stabilize and gently set the free foot down: two finish set-downs total. Reduce knee height/cadence for drift, reaching or lost posture.

exercises.description: Convert a small rearward load into forward hip-driven projection. From standing, take one short backward step then step forward to gather both feet and immediately jump forward with natural arms; hold the bilateral landing 2 s. Regress/stop: Shorten and slow the entry; stop for extra shuffles or an uncontrolled forward pitch.

Regress/stop: Reduce ball load and hinge; do not throw unless the full overhead trajectory and landing/roll fit the verified area.

Regress/stop: Lower the step and rebound height; stop if impact control or alignment deteriorates.

exercises.name: Seated Single-leg Jump onto a Low Box
exercises.sourceName: Seated Single-leg Jump onto a Low Box
exercises.dose: 1 × 1 per side = 2 reps. Fast takeoff with controlled travel. 30 s between reps; 90 s between set/side bouts; 90 s before the next row/section.
exercises.description: Supply a controlled one-leg initial impulse into a two-foot elevated finish. Sit still with one foot flat and the other free; push from the supported leg and swing arms to land both feet fully on a very low nearby box; hold and step down. Regress/stop: Raise the seat or lower/bring the landing box closer while keeping the same task; stop for rocking, twisting or incomplete foot placement. Entry: Demonstrated single-leg seated takeoff and box landing; no attempt to force height.

jumps-horizontal.title: Class 12
jumps-horizontal.effort: Integrate same-leg and opposite-leg contacts into a controlled horizontal finish.

exercises.name: Stationary Single-leg Hop–Step–Jump
exercises.dose: 2 × 1 = 2 reps. Fast takeoff with controlled travel. continuous reps within the short set; 120 s between set/side bouts; 90 s before the next row/section. Two integrated sequences = six landings: four unilateral and two bilateral. No running approach; not three bilateral broad jumps.
exercises.description: Integrate same-leg reuse, opposite-leg transfer and a bilateral final reception into one defined horizontal foot sequence. From one foot, hop to the same foot, step-bound to the opposite foot, then jump from that foot to both feet; hold the final landing. Start the other set on the opposite leg. Regress/stop: Shorten each segment and slow entry intent while keeping the sequence; stop for a collapsing intermediate contact or incorrect foot order.

exercises.description: Redirect a small lateral entry into a straight-ahead two-foot push. Take one short lateral step into a parallel two-foot gather, square the pelvis to the forward lane and jump forward; hold the landing 2 s. Regress/stop: Shorten/slow the lateral step; stop if the jump drifts sideways or the pelvis rotates through landing.

jumps-vertical.title: Class 4
jumps-vertical.effort: Direct a controlled dip or short entry into decisive upward leg drive. Box Jump — standing countermovement is the main performance drill. Supporting work practices redirecting a lateral entry upward, single-leg upward projection, low ankle-return rhythm and rapid leg extension against external load.

Land on two feet near the takeoff area and hold 2 s. Use a walking entry over at most 1 m; slow/shorten it for sideways drift or knee/pelvis loss. exercises.sourceName: Power Skip for Height — isolated step-hop cycle — proposed exact execution

Take one walking step onto the takeoff foot, make one modest upward hop with opposite knee drive, land on that same foot, absorb under control, then place the free foot down and walk clear. jumps-vertical.explosiveNotes: Follow this order, with full resets except the small continuous rope bout. E1–E4 are bodyweight. Strong upward intent must remain compatible with the specified landing; E3 stays modest because its same-leg landing is a new demand. E5–E6 use light, readily controlled loads, not strength-set effort.

jumps-vertical.title: Class 5
jumps-vertical.effort: Produce decisive upward force through each takeoff leg while keeping the foot, knee and pelvis organized. Single-Leg Takeoff to Two-Foot Box Landing is the primary drill. Supporting work uses a staggered push, low ankle rebound, a deeper supported start, rapid hip extension and a leg-driven ball release. The supporting staggered tasks use both feet; they are not falsely counted as isolated single-leg force.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Takeoff to Two-Foot Box Landing
exercises.sourceName: Single-Leg Takeoff to Two-Foot Box Landing
exercises.dose: 1 × 3 per takeoff leg = 6 jumps. 30 s after step-down/return between same-leg attempts; 90 s between legs; 120 s before E2.
exercises.description: Main task: direct one leg's dip-to-drive force upward. Start stationary on one foot, free foot clear; no approach or repeated hop. Swing the arms, extend the stance leg and land on a low stable box with both whole feet. Hold 2 s, stand and step down. Choose a small gap and easily controlled target, not a height challenge. Lower box/intent or use the floor replacement for knee collapse, pelvic rotation, deep tuck or edge contact.

jumps-vertical.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1 sequence, supplied separately, without creating or modifying it. Its content, duration and impacts/lifting are unknown here. Include its actual exposure and the athlete's current readiness in the delivery decision.
jumps-vertical.explosiveNotes: Use this order. E1 receives six primary attempts; E2 is a small supporting jump dose, and E3 is only low ankle rebound. E4–E6 express force rapidly without intended athlete flight. All bodyweight work stays unloaded; ball/bell loads must allow crisp, controlled motion. For side-based work, begin left then right unless a known actual prior order justifies reversing it; record the chosen order.

jumps-vertical.title: Class 6
jumps-vertical.effort: Convert a short entry into an organized plant and upward drive. Approach Box Jump — two-step entry, two-foot takeoff is the primary drill. The supporting jobs are a single-leg entry plant, low ankle return across a small displacement, rapid drive after placing a foot on a step, leg-to-arm vertical load transfer and an upward ball release after gathering the feet.

jumps-vertical.explosiveNotes: Use this order. E1 receives six primary attempts; E2 contributes four supporting flights and E3 six low contacts. E4–E6 express force rapidly without intended athlete flight. Bodyweight drills remain unloaded; dumbbells and ball must permit crisp, controlled action. In E1, each set has one left-leading entry then one right-leading entry. In other side-based slots, begin left then right unless a known actual record supports reversing order; record it.

jumps-vertical.title: Class 7
jumps-vertical.effort: Absorb a self-generated landing and turn it into a prompt, organized second vertical takeoff. Countermovement Jump Rebound is the primary drill: one floor jump linked to exactly one rebound. Supporting work addresses leg-led dip reversal, low ankle return under slight lateral displacement, lead-leg lowering-to-drive, rapid hip reversal under a one-hand load and leg-driven upward ball release.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump Rebound — one linked rebound
exercises.sourceName: Countermovement Jump Rebound — one linked rebound
exercises.dose: 3 × 1 two-flight bout = 6 jumps/landings, with one rebound transition per bout. 120 s between bouts and before E2.
exercises.description: Main task: accept a self-generated floor landing and redirect force upward. Start stationary on two feet with natural arms, make a controlled vertical CMJ, land on both feet and use one smooth yielding action for the second jump. Land again on both feet, hold 2 s and reset. Keep both flights modest initially, with no obstacle or external drop. End after the first landing if symmetry/control is lost; do not force the rebound to finish a count. Reduce intent or use isolated jumps if pausing, deep collapse, knee loss, drift or an unwanted third jump appears.

jumps-vertical.title: Class 8
jumps-vertical.effort: Consolidate leg-led upward projection with a repeatable dip and organized landing. No-Arm-Swing Box Jump is the primary task. Brief support work changes the split-stance landing, ankle impulse, seated start and loaded hip start while preserving upward force as the job. A simple vertical scoop toss recurs to retain leg-to-arm release practice without adding another new throw constraint.

exercises.name: No-Arm-Swing Box Jump
exercises.dose: 3 × 2 = 6 jumps. 20 s after step-down/return between reps; 120 s between sets and before E2.
exercises.description: Main task: direct leg-driven extension upward with arm assistance removed at takeoff. Start stationary, feet parallel, hands at hips; make one comfortable dip and jump to a low stable box with a small gap. Land with both whole feet, hold 2 s, stand, step down and reset. Keep the target easily controlled, without deep knee tuck or a forward dive. Lower target/intent or use the floor replacement for edge contact, drift, knee loss or arm-assisted takeoff.

exercises.name: Lunge Switch Jump — isolated, opposite-lead landing
exercises.sourceName: Lunge Switch Jump — isolated, opposite-lead landing
exercises.dose: 1 × 1 per starting lead leg = 2 jumps. Start left lead for the first, right lead for the second. 60 s between starting leads; 90 s before E3.
exercises.description: Preserve upward projection while the feet exchange lead in flight. jumps-vertical.effort: Express rapid upward force against a modest held load while preserving a controlled takeoff and landing. Dumbbell Countermovement Jump is the primary task, using two scheduled bodyweight attempts before up to four lightly loaded attempts. Supporting work separates static-start arm-assisted force, brief ankle rebounds, a tall-start ball preload, a floor-start loaded pull and supported lead-leg extension.

jumps-vertical.explosiveNotes: Use this order. The full prescription has fourteen jump landings: E1 six, E2 four and E3 four. Under the conditional loading plan, ten are bodyweight and at most four carry dumbbells. E4–E6 have no intended athlete flight. The two E1 bodyweight checks are part of its six-attempt budget, not additional preparation jumps or primary-strength preparation reps.

jumps-vertical.title: Class 10
jumps-vertical.effort: Organize a short walking entry into a stable two-foot base, then express a clean vertical takeoff. Gather-and-Hold Vertical Jump is the primary task: two foot placements, a two-second tall settle, then one countermovement jump. The settle intentionally removes immediate approach momentum; this is an entry-to-standing integration task, not a fast approach-jump test.

exercises.name: Gather-and-Hold Vertical Jump — two walking placements, tall settle — proposed execution
exercises.sourceName: Gather-and-Hold Vertical Jump — two walking placements, tall settle — proposed execution
exercises.dose: 3 × 2 = 6 jumps, one left-first and one right-first entry each set. 2 s tall settle before the dip; 2 s landing hold. 20 s after walking return/reset between reps; 120 s between sets and before E2.
exercises.description: Main task: establish a square, balanced takeoff base after movement, then direct force upward. Start tall; take a short walking step, bring the other foot alongside to comfortable jumping width, settle with arms relaxed, then use one natural dip/arm swing and jump. No extra shuffle, running, pre-hop, squat hold or immediate rebound. Entry is at most 2 m within the inspected zone. Use a shorter/slower entry if the base needs adjustment; use stationary CMJ instead if it still cannot be organized.

jumps-vertical.title: Class 11
jumps-vertical.effort: Produce a repeatable standing vertical jump with coordinated dip, leg extension and natural arm swing. Countermovement Jump deliberately returns as the primary performance anchor. Establish usable assessment conditions within its six attempts while reducing unnecessary support volume.

exercises.sourceName: Countermovement Jump — natural arm swing, stick landing — deliberately recurring
exercises.dose: 3 × 2 = 6 jumps. Set 1: two controlled execution checks; sets 2–3: up to four candidate jumps with maximum-height intent only while control/readiness permit. 30 s after landing/reset between reps; 120 s between sets and before E2.
exercises.description: Main performance task: coordinate a natural dip and arm swing into direct upward propulsion. Start stationary with the same comfortable stance, use one self-selected dip, jump upward and hold the bilateral landing 2 s. No approach, pre-hop, pause in the squat, loaded implement or rebound. Keep the declared cue/arm/stance protocol stable in sets 2–3. Reduce intent or stop for uncontrolled drift/landing; record modified work without treating it as comparable maximal output.

exercises.dose: 1 × 3 = 3 jumps. Sit still 2 s before each, hold the floor landing 2 s, then walk back and reseat between jumps; after the final landing, clear the zone. 20 s after reseating/reset between reps; 90 s before E3.
exercises.description: Express leg force from a supported stationary start without arm-swing assistance, separating initiation from E1's active dip. jumps-vertical.explosiveNotes: Use this order. E1's observation precedes all supporting work. Six E1, two E2 and four E3 jumps total twelve bodyweight bilateral floor landings. E4–E6 have no intended athlete flight. First scheduled work checks each task's execution; no additional practice, tests or compensating work.

jumps-rebound.title: Class 1
jumps-rebound.effort: Receive a self-generated jump landing with control, then use that landing to produce a prompt, organized second takeoff. Today establishes the difference between stopping a landing and rebounding from it.

Rest durations begin after the previous effort finishes and include no extra exercises.

Keep pressure centered over both feet. Reduce height if the landing needs a step or the trunk folds; stop if control is not restored.

jumps-rebound.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1 sequence. It is supplied separately and is not created or modified here. Its exact content and duration have not been established for this curriculum. The coach must account for any jumps, loaded work or fatigue already present in it. All totals and time estimates below exclude that sequence.
jumps-rebound.explosiveNotes: Perform in table order, with bodyweight and purposeful quick takeoffs. Control the indicated amplitude rather than chasing height or distance. Rest is recovery, without other exercise work. An ongoing connected sequence is one exercise, not separate drills; stop and settle its final landing.

agility-mobility.explosiveNotes: Use E1–E6 in order. Routes/directions are known before starting; this is directional practice, not reactive anticipation. E2 receives the main practice allocation. A continuous route or flight-to-exit is one drill, not a circuit of additional exercises.

upper-body-force.title: Class 1
upper-body-force.effort: Produce forceful horizontal pushes and pulls with a steady trunk; express the pushing action in a fast, straight-ahead chest-pass release.
upper-body-force.delivery: Timing and scheduling: Allow approximately 65–75 minutes after Access & Prepare 1, including listed resets, rest, load-preparation sets, demonstrations and equipment changes for an athlete with equipment access. Group queues and extra coaching can add time. The existing preparation duration and actual booking are unknown, so the complete session duration is unresolved; this is not a 60-minute total-session claim. Match the class to actual sport, lifting, throwing, contact and tumbling exposure. Initially plan a nonconsecutive demanding upper-body exposure, commonly about 48–72 hours later, then adjust to actual symptoms, fatigue and schedule; elapsed time alone does not establish recovery. No separate body-control work is prescribed here.

upper-body-force.quality: Quality marker, inside E1: Record valid releases out of the nine prescribed attempts. A valid attempt starts with a one-second still chest hold, uses simultaneous hand release, sends the ball through the declared forward corridor and finishes with ribs over pelvis and both feet planted. Record ball mass/type, stance, target arrangement and misses; a miss still consumes an attempt. This is a technique record, not a validated power test. No extra test throws and no fabricated speed or distance results.
upper-body-force.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1 sequence, supplied separately. Its contents and duration were not provided; do not create, modify or infer them. Check its actual shoulder, elbow and wrist loading before continuing.
upper-body-force.explosiveNotes: Baseline: Ages 12–14 with established basic lifting technique, under qualified supervision. This is a first curriculum exposure, not automatically a first lifting session. Select resistance from demonstrated control and speed. Attendance, recent loading, individual restrictions and response are unknown. Daily stimulus brief: Train a decisive forward release and a strong backward draw without substituting torso rotation or lumbar extension. The stationary Medicine Ball Chest Pass is the performance anchor. Supporting jobs are rapid pulling from a pause, brief hand push-off and force acceptance, a small preload into projection, pulling through rising resistance, and independent arm projection. Light scapular and shoulder control precede challenging press, row and elbow-strength work.

E: Use light resistance that allows a visibly quick effort with control; ball mass is athlete-specific, not a universal age-based weight. Start with E1 while fresh. These are discrete efforts, not a timed circuit.

Between exercises: Rest 90 seconds after the last effort before the next exercise; setup time may supply this rest only if the athlete is actually resting. Extend explosive set/transition recovery to 2–3 minutes when speed or attention has not returned. Rest 90 seconds after E6 before Section 3. Never shorten recovery to finish a clock.

Throwing and quality: Use an inspected throw-rated wall with a clear rebound zone, or an open release corridor that contains the flight, bounce and roll. Select and record the target before E1; use the same target arrangement for repeat comparisons. Lane length alone does not establish containment. Athletes do not catch returning balls. Retrieve only after the ball stops and the coach clears entry. No athlete waits downrange. Finish a set when speed plainly falls, hands release unevenly, the torso substitutes for the arms, or E3 hand landing becomes hard/asymmetric. Rest and use an easier replacement for remaining prescribed work only if quality returns; otherwise stop that exercise and record the shortfall. Do not make up failed attempts.
S: Keep these light, smooth and well short of fatigue, with at least 5 clean repetitions in reserve. They should leave the athlete ready to lift.

Rest 45 seconds between these exercises and 60 seconds after S2 before strength preparation. Reduce band tension or quadruped loading if the reserve disappears; do not turn this section into a burn or mobility sequence.
P: The table lists working sets. Every working set should finish with about 2–3 technically sound repetitions in reserve. Use controlled lowering and a decisive lifting intent; no grinding, forced reps or maximal tests. This is strength work, not a rotation against the clock. Work in the listed order.

Preparation sets, separate from working sets: P1: 1 × 6 very light, then 1 × 3 intermediate, resting 60 seconds between them and 90 seconds before working sets. P2: 1 × 5 per arm light, 30 seconds between arms and 90 seconds before work. P3: 1 × 3 at an easier leverage/resistance. P4, P5 and P6: 1 × 5 light each. Rest 60 seconds after each of the P3–P6 preparation sets. All preparation stays at least 5 reps from technical failure. These total 37 repetitions, 7 set rounds / 8 side-specific bouts, all of listed exercises. Any extra load-finding reps must be recorded and add time; do not improvise extra exercises.

Between strength exercises: Rest 2 minutes after P1, P2 and P3; 90 seconds after P4 and P5, before the next exercise's preparation. If a working load would leave fewer than 2 clean reps, reduce it. If it leaves clearly more than 3, adjust the next available prescribed set or future exposure; do not add bonus sets. Stop for pain, loss of control or persistent compensation, even if work remains. P3 and P4 are distinct strengthening tasks, not hidden explosive or stabilization sets.

Replacement rules: Replacements occupy the same slot and remaining dose; never add them to the session. Raise E3's hand support if needed; if even a small hand release is unsuitable, use a fast incline push-up with hands staying down instead of E3, recording zero hand-landing events. If the minimum landmine load is too slow or its sleeve cannot be gripped securely, use a light two-hand kettlebell row from the same paused hinge instead of E2, 2 × 3 with identical recovery. If E5's seated band setup slips, use a bent-over band row with the band securely under both feet instead of E5, 1 × 4 at the same tempo; record the changed resistance direction. Use thigh-supported One-Arm Row instead of P2 if no suitable bench support fits, preserving side dose and trunk control. Use lighter implements/resistance and suitable range for other rows, not extra repetitions.

Unconfirmed release area or one-arm ball fit: Use the specific replacement-only band presses in the delivery audit if a throwing slot cannot be delivered. They preserve rapid pushing practice but remove that slot's free-release practice; record the direct-practice gap and changed throw totals. If no suitable replacement can preserve controlled, meaningful work, do not represent an interrupted class as fully delivered.

upper-body-force.setup: Base equipment actually needed: suitable medicine balls; a secured landmine, suitably light bar and compatible plates if needed; dumbbells; bands; one stable elevated hand support and one usable row support (a suitable bench may serve sequentially); a clear floor and inspected throwing arrangement. Equipment categories are confirmed; individual fit, condition and counts are not. No three-simultaneous-station claim is made. Layout: Reserve one contained throwing corridor or a throw-rated wall lane, with the waiting area behind the thrower and beyond the possible rebound path. The thrower's line, target, rebound/bounce zone and retrieval route must fit the inspected site. Three 10 m lanes are not one 30 m space. Keep all lifting, band and push-up work outside flight/rebound zones; with one coach and one throwing bay, run the explosive exercises sequentially so coaching attention and clearance are not split. Do not operate a row station in a live throwing lane. No catches, run-ups or step-throughs are required. Throw replacements: If the wall/open release area cannot contain throws, use a self-anchored two-hand Band Speed Chest Press from a pause instead of E1, 3 × 3; use a shallow-countermovement Band Speed Chest Press instead of E4, 1 × 3; use a forward-facing Single-Arm Band Speed Press instead of E6, 1 × 2 per arm. These are proposed exact executions, not claimed library variants. Place an intact manufacturer-suitable band across the upper back below the neck; for bilateral work secure it in both hands, and for unilateral work secure the nonworking end against the torso with the other hand. No external anchor or band release. Feet stay planted; press quickly, keep the ribs quiet, return under control. Retain each slot's listed inter-rep, inter-set and side recovery. Reduce resistance if tension cannot be controlled. Unilateral pressing also replaces E6 alone if no ball can be securely controlled by one hand. Never perform both versions. These replacements are rapid resisted pushing, not throws, and cannot establish chest-pass release performance. Record E1 as a different anchor, throw totals as 0 if all three are replaced (12 if only E6 is replaced), and an unresolved free-release practice gap. Do not compare band performance with ball performance. If no valid band fit is available either, the session is not fully deliverable under current conditions; resolve the setup rather than hiding a zero-dose slot. The finalized base prescription remains the ball-release class, conditional on verified containment. Other replacements: E2 can use a light two-hand kettlebell paused row if minimum bar mass or grip prevents a fast pull; E3 can use a higher stable support or a non-flight fast incline press; E5 can use a band secured under both feet in a fixed hinge instead of seated foot anchoring; P2 can use a stable thigh-supported row instead of bench support. All retain their slot's remaining sets/reps and rest, and changes must be logged. A change to seated/standing resistance direction invalidates a like-for-like E5 comparison. P4's hinge must remain technically established; use a supported chest-down version instead of P4 only if a bench actually permits the arm path and clearance, with the same 1 × 8 and effort. Do not assume an adjustable incline bench. Group time model: Let A be actual Access & Prepare 1 minutes and Q be additional queue, supervision and individual load-finding time beyond the base allowance. Full delivery is approximately A + 65–75 + Q minutes. For N athletes sharing one bay, each three-throw turn consumes roughly 45–60 seconds including clearance/reset. Return to a station only after that athlete's required recovery; compute waiting as `max(required recovery, actual waiting)` rather than adding both. This example describes turn occupancy, not a confirmed group size or proof of overall fit. Observe the actual flow before promising a booked duration.
upper-body-force.progression: Progression note: There is no prior prescription for this focus and no observed response. E1 is this class's quality marker; P1 and P2 may recur as strength anchors. Under the owner's updated preference, Class 2 should consolidate straight-ahead release and push/pull positions through unique, directly relevant drills, checking prior drill use first. A repeated drill needs a specific justification; new names or cosmetic changes do not count as unique. With absent feedback, keep readiness conditional and do not infer earned increases in load, volume or complexity. Consider one small strength-load adjustment only after reported completion at the stated technique/reserve and satisfactory recovery. Compare a drill's performance only when its execution, ball and setup match; do not compare unlike drills as a power test.

upper-body-force.title: Class 2
upper-body-force.effort: Accelerate the arms in pushing and pulling while the trunk supplies a stable base; retain a straight-ahead release.
upper-body-force.delivery: Workload and timing: 6 throw bilateral; 6 rapid press unilateral; 8 alternating rope pull; 7 rapid pull bilateral; 4 rapid press bilateral. Primary work totals 68 task repetitions in 8 rounds / 10 bouts; resilience totals 16 task repetitions. Bilateral cycles count once; unilateral doses count both arms. These exposure types are not equivalent stress units. No lower-body jumping, sprinting or rotational throw work is added. Estimate 60–69 minutes after Access & Prepare 1, including listed work, resets, recovery, preparation and instruction; additional group queues or extra coaching add time. Complete session length is unresolved. Match the actual booking rather than compressing recovery. Scheduling: Review recent/upcoming throwing, contact sport, lifting and hand-supported tumbling. Plan the next demanding upper-body exposure on a nonconsecutive occasion, commonly 48–72 hours later initially, then adjust to actual recovery and schedule. Elapsed time is not proof of readiness. Body control remains separate.

upper-body-force.quality: Quality marker, within E1: In E1, record controlled forward releases out of 6 attempts: both knees remain down, hips remain tall, ribs do not flare and the ball exits symmetrically. Record ball and target. This kneeling task is not directly comparable with Class 1 standing throws. Record valid attempts and actual work, including misses; an invalid attempt consumes a rep. No bonus test attempts. Do not compare measurements from different drills as the same test.
upper-body-force.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1, supplied separately. Do not create or modify it. Its duration and workload are unknown; check its actual upper-body demand before proceeding.
upper-body-force.explosiveNotes: Baseline and current evidence: Ages 12–14 with established basic lifting technique and qualified supervision. Reviewed Class 1, saved workload/progression, drill use and available feedback before this prescription. No athlete completion, symptoms, load tolerance or improvement has been reported. This is a conditional planned class, not the next calendar day. New tasks require demonstrated control in the first prescribed attempts; no separate readiness test is added. Daily stimulus brief: Remove leg contribution from the main release, then practice distinct arm-force tasks: guided unilateral pressing, sequential grip-to-pull transfer, assisted vertical pulling, elastic press acceleration and shoulder-only downward pulling. The last two pulling tasks support the requested Pulling subcategory; they are not presented as horizontal chest-pass tests.

E: Light resistance, rapid purposeful effort and controlled resets. Use the least assistance/load needed to preserve speed and position; no generic age-based weight. No failure sets or conditioning circuit.

Recovery and quality: Rest 90 seconds between exercises, including after E6 before Section 3; extend to 2–3 minutes if control, attention or speed has not returned. Returns are controlled, not explosive, unless the row explicitly describes a linked action. Stop the set for pain, jerking, unwanted rotation, hard/asymmetric hand reception or clear loss of speed; reduce load/complexity for remaining work only if control returns. Otherwise stop and record the shortfall. Do not make up missed reps or count a non-flight press as a hand landing.

Delivery: Use a single supervised throwing bay first, then move to a separate landmine/floor area and an inspected bar/band attachment. Bar and band stations must not lie in the throwing or rope-retrieval path. Rope length/diameter and box/bar fit are not assumed; use the listed same-slot replacement when unsuitable. Ball releases require an inspected throw-rated wall with a protected rebound area, or a clear open corridor containing flight, bounce and roll. No rebound catches unless explicitly prescribed in a row. Retrieve stopped balls on the coach's signal; nobody waits downrange. Three separate 10 m lanes do not confirm throwing containment or extra run-off. Equipment quantities, ball mass/size, anchor ratings, bar minimum load and support dimensions remain unconfirmed. Every replacement occupies its original slot only; a resisted press replacing a throw removes that release exposure and cannot supply the same assessment.
S: Light, controlled strengthening; keep at least 5 technically sound repetitions in reserve. These sets should not tire the athlete before primary lifting.

Rest 45 seconds between exercises and 60 seconds after S2 before strength preparation. Use lighter resistance or shorter comfortable range if control fades. Stop for symptoms rather than completing a nominal count.
P: These are working sets, each finishing with approximately 2–3 technically sound repetitions in reserve. Select challenging loads/assistance individually; a small set count does not mean a light effort. No forced reps, maximum testing, unstable supports or timed rotation. Work in order.

Load-preparation sets of these same listed lifts: P1: 1 × 6 then 1 × 3; P2: 1 × 5 per arm; P3: 1 × 3; P4: 1 × 5; P5: 1 × 5; P6: 1 × 5. Use very light resistance; where two preparation sets are listed, the second is intermediate. Keep at least 5 technical reps in reserve. Rest 60 seconds between preparation rounds, 30 seconds between arms within a preparation round, then 90 seconds before P1/P2 working sets or 60 seconds before P3–P6 work. Preparation totals 37 repetitions, 7 rounds / 8 bouts. Extra load-finding reps add actual workload and time; never add an exercise.

Strength transitions: Rest 2 minutes after P1, P2 and P3, and 90 seconds after P4 and P5, before preparing the next lift. Increase load only when an available prescribed set can remain at the stated range, tempo and reserve; if the next increment is too large, hold the load. All symptom, speed and technique stops take precedence over the planned count.

upper-body-force.progression: Progression note: Class 1 main Floor Press 2 × 6 and One-Arm Row 2 × 6 per arm → same doses here because no completion or recovery is reported. P3/P5/P6 also retain their direct strength roles and doses; P4 changes from wide-elbow row to 1 × 8 Band Lat Pulldown to support today's overhead draw. Next exposure: hold these strength loads unless actual controlled completion at 2–3 RIR and satisfactory recovery supports one small relevant change.

upper-body-force.title: Class 3
upper-body-force.effort: Initiate and complete a rapid downward or backward arm draw without trunk heaving.
upper-body-force.delivery: Workload and timing: 9 throw bilateral; 6 rapid pull unilateral; 8 rapid pull bilateral; 4 rapid scapular pull bilateral. Primary work totals 66 task repetitions in 8 rounds / 10 bouts; resilience totals 18 task repetitions. Bilateral cycles count once; unilateral doses count both arms. These exposure types are not equivalent stress units. No lower-body jumping, sprinting or rotational throw work is added. Estimate 60–69 minutes after Access & Prepare 1, including listed work, resets, recovery, preparation and instruction; additional group queues or extra coaching add time. Complete session length is unresolved. Match the actual booking rather than compressing recovery. Scheduling: Review recent/upcoming throwing, contact sport, lifting and hand-supported tumbling. Plan the next demanding upper-body exposure on a nonconsecutive occasion, commonly 48–72 hours later initially, then adjust to actual recovery and schedule. Elapsed time is not proof of readiness. Body control remains separate.

upper-body-force.explosiveNotes: Baseline and current evidence: Ages 12–14 with established basic lifting technique and qualified supervision. Reviewed Class 2, saved workload/progression, drill use and available feedback before this prescription. No athlete completion, symptoms, load tolerance or improvement has been reported. This is a conditional planned class, not the next calendar day. New tasks require demonstrated control in the first prescribed attempts; no separate readiness test is added. Daily stimulus brief: The main task is a tall-kneeling slam driven by the arms. Supporting pulls separate upper-arm drive, reversal into a row, elbow-flexion acceleration and initial scapular control. One small familiar forward-release dose retains the requested projection component without competing with the pulling emphasis.

E: Light resistance, rapid purposeful effort and controlled resets. Use the least assistance/load needed to preserve speed and position; no generic age-based weight. No failure sets or conditioning circuit.

Recovery and quality: Rest 90 seconds between exercises, including after E6 before Section 3; extend to 2–3 minutes if control, attention or speed has not returned. Returns are controlled, not explosive, unless the row explicitly describes a linked action. Stop the set for pain, jerking, unwanted rotation, hard/asymmetric hand reception or clear loss of speed; reduce load/complexity for remaining work only if control returns. Otherwise stop and record the shortfall. Do not make up missed reps or count a non-flight press as a hand landing.

Delivery: Run the slam station separately from the forward-release corridor. Both need inspected surfaces and clear ball travel; a slam is not permission to use a rebounding ball beneath the face. Place the overhead-band/bar station outside both ball zones. Unsupported bands or improvised bar supports are not acceptable substitutes. Ball releases require an inspected throw-rated wall with a protected rebound area, or a clear open corridor containing flight, bounce and roll. No rebound catches unless explicitly prescribed in a row. Retrieve stopped balls on the coach's signal; nobody waits downrange. Three separate 10 m lanes do not confirm throwing containment or extra run-off. Equipment quantities, ball mass/size, anchor ratings, bar minimum load and support dimensions remain unconfirmed. Every replacement occupies its original slot only; a resisted press replacing a throw removes that release exposure and cannot supply the same assessment.
S: Light, controlled strengthening; keep at least 5 technically sound repetitions in reserve. These sets should not tire the athlete before primary lifting.

Rest 45 seconds between exercises and 60 seconds after S2 before strength preparation. Use lighter resistance or shorter comfortable range if control fades. Stop for symptoms rather than completing a nominal count.
P: These are working sets, each finishing with approximately 2–3 technically sound repetitions in reserve. Select challenging loads/assistance individually; a small set count does not mean a light effort. No forced reps, maximum testing, unstable supports or timed rotation. Work in order.

Load-preparation sets of these same listed lifts: P1: 1 × 5 per arm; P2: 1 × 5; P3: 1 × 5; P4: 1 × 5; P5: 1 × 5; P6: 1 × 5. Use very light resistance; where two preparation sets are listed, the second is intermediate. Keep at least 5 technical reps in reserve. Rest 60 seconds between preparation rounds, 30 seconds between arms within a preparation round, then 90 seconds before P1/P2 working sets or 60 seconds before P3–P6 work. Preparation totals 35 repetitions, 6 rounds / 7 bouts. Extra load-finding reps add actual workload and time; never add an exercise.

Strength transitions: Rest 2 minutes after P1, P2 and P3, and 90 seconds after P4 and P5, before preparing the next lift. Increase load only when an available prescribed set can remain at the stated range, tempo and reserve; if the next increment is too large, hold the load. All symptom, speed and technique stops take precedence over the planned count.

upper-body-force.progression: Progression note: Class 2 used 2 × 6 Floor Press and 1 × 8 Band Lat Pulldown. Here the press falls to 1 × 6 and the pulldown becomes 2 × 6, retaining eight total primary set rounds while giving the main pulling task more practice; total primary task reps change from 68 to 66. One-Arm Row remains 2 × 6 per arm. This planned redistribution is not evidence of improved capacity. Use familiar manageable loads; hold or reduce the pulldown if actual readiness or first-set technique does not support the extra set. Before later load advancement require reported controlled completion, stated reserve and recovery.

upper-body-force.title: Class 4
upper-body-force.effort: Express a fast forward press from a settled start and control the finish.
upper-body-force.delivery: Workload and timing: 6 hand landing bilateral; 8 rapid press bilateral; 3 throw bilateral; 4 rapid press unilateral; 3 rapid pull bilateral. Primary work totals 60 task repetitions in 8 rounds / 9 bouts; resilience totals 16 task repetitions. Bilateral cycles count once; unilateral doses count both arms. These exposure types are not equivalent stress units. No lower-body jumping, sprinting or rotational throw work is added. Estimate 59–68 minutes after Access & Prepare 1, including listed work, resets, recovery, preparation and instruction; additional group queues or extra coaching add time. Complete session length is unresolved. Match the actual booking rather than compressing recovery. Scheduling: Review recent/upcoming throwing, contact sport, lifting and hand-supported tumbling. Plan the next demanding upper-body exposure on a nonconsecutive occasion, commonly 48–72 hours later initially, then adjust to actual recovery and schedule. Elapsed time is not proof of readiness. Body control remains separate.

No bonus test attempts. Do not compare measurements from different drills as the same test.
upper-body-force.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1, supplied separately. Do not create or modify it. Its duration and workload are unknown; check its actual upper-body demand before proceeding.
upper-body-force.explosiveNotes: Baseline and current evidence: Ages 12–14 with established basic lifting technique and qualified supervision. Reviewed Class 3, saved workload/progression, drill use and available feedback before this prescription. No athlete completion, symptoms, load tolerance or improvement has been reported. This is a conditional planned class, not the next calendar day. New tasks require demonstrated control in the first prescribed attempts; no separate readiness test is added. Daily stimulus brief: The paused-start plyometric push-up is primary. Small supporting doses distinguish elbow extension, receive-then-set force production, external-load acceleration and independent arm timing; one familiar pull maintains the requested pulling component. Shoulder and elbow overlap is limited by keeping supports to one short set.

E: Light resistance, rapid purposeful effort and controlled resets. Use the least assistance/load needed to preserve speed and position; no generic age-based weight. No failure sets or conditioning circuit.

Recovery and quality: Rest 90 seconds between exercises, including after E6 before Section 3; extend to 2–3 minutes if control, attention or speed has not returned. Returns are controlled, not explosive, unless the row explicitly describes a linked action. Stop the set for pain, jerking, unwanted rotation, hard/asymmetric hand reception or clear loss of speed; reduce load/complexity for remaining work only if control returns. Otherwise stop and record the shortfall. Do not make up missed reps or count a non-flight press as a hand landing.

Delivery: Use one inspected hand support with room for both hand receptions. Keep the coach-fed pass separate from other activity; the coach controls both feed and retrieval so the receiving athlete is never surprised. Ball size, rebound/flight containment and receiving competence are unconfirmed. Keep the band and floor-press stations outside the ball corridor. Ball releases require an inspected throw-rated wall with a protected rebound area, or a clear open corridor containing flight, bounce and roll. No rebound catches unless explicitly prescribed in a row. Retrieve stopped balls on the coach's signal; nobody waits downrange. Three separate 10 m lanes do not confirm throwing containment or extra run-off. Equipment quantities, ball mass/size, anchor ratings, bar minimum load and support dimensions remain unconfirmed. Every replacement occupies its original slot only; a resisted press replacing a throw removes that release exposure and cannot supply the same assessment.
S: Light, controlled strengthening; keep at least 5 technically sound repetitions in reserve. These sets should not tire the athlete before primary lifting.

Rest 45 seconds between exercises and 60 seconds after S2 before strength preparation. Use lighter resistance or shorter comfortable range if control fades. Stop for symptoms rather than completing a nominal count.
P: These are working sets, each finishing with approximately 2–3 technically sound repetitions in reserve. Select challenging loads/assistance individually; a small set count does not mean a light effort. No forced reps, maximum testing, unstable supports or timed rotation. Work in order.

Load-preparation sets of these same listed lifts: P1: 1 × 6 then 1 × 3; P2: 1 × 5 per arm; P3: 1 × 3; P4: 1 × 5; P5: 1 × 5; P6: 1 × 5. Use very light resistance; where two preparation sets are listed, the second is intermediate. Keep at least 5 technical reps in reserve. Rest 60 seconds between preparation rounds, 30 seconds between arms within a preparation round, then 90 seconds before P1/P2 working sets or 60 seconds before P3–P6 work. Preparation totals 37 repetitions, 7 rounds / 8 bouts. Extra load-finding reps add actual workload and time; never add an exercise.

Strength transitions: Rest 2 minutes after P1, P2 and P3, and 90 seconds after P4 and P5, before preparing the next lift. Increase load only when an available prescribed set can remain at the stated range, tempo and reserve; if the next increment is too large, hold the load. All symptom, speed and technique stops take precedence over the planned count.

upper-body-force.progression: Progression note: Class 3 emphasized pulling with Floor Press 1 × 6 and two main pulling lifts. Here Floor Press returns to its already prescribed Class 1/2 dose of 2 × 6, One-Arm Row drops to 1 × 6 per arm, and controlled Push-Up receives 2 × 6 instead of Class 2's 1 × 8. Eight primary rounds are retained, with 60 task reps rather than Class 3's 66. This is focus-based redistribution, not an earned increase. Hold loads at demonstrated 2–3 RIR; the added receiving/hand-flight demands can require same-slot regression or stopped work. Next progression needs actual controlled completion and recovery.

upper-body-force.title: Class 5
upper-body-force.effort: Convert a small preload or received load into a straight-ahead upper-body release.
upper-body-force.delivery: Workload and timing: 9 throw bilateral; 3 rapid press bilateral; 4 throw unilateral; 4 rapid pull bilateral; 4 hand landing bilateral. Primary work totals 64 task repetitions in 8 rounds / 10 bouts; resilience totals 20 task repetitions. Bilateral cycles count once; unilateral doses count both arms. These exposure types are not equivalent stress units. No lower-body jumping, sprinting or rotational throw work is added. Estimate 62–71 minutes after Access & Prepare 1, including listed work, resets, recovery, preparation and instruction; additional group queues or extra coaching add time. Complete session length is unresolved. Match the actual booking rather than compressing recovery. Scheduling: Review recent/upcoming throwing, contact sport, lifting and hand-supported tumbling. Plan the next demanding upper-body exposure on a nonconsecutive occasion, commonly 48–72 hours later initially, then adjust to actual recovery and schedule. Elapsed time is not proof of readiness. Body control remains separate.

upper-body-force.explosiveNotes: Baseline and current evidence: Ages 12–14 with established basic lifting technique and qualified supervision. Reviewed Class 4, saved workload/progression, drill use and available feedback before this prescription. No athlete completion, symptoms, load tolerance or improvement has been reported. This is a conditional planned class, not the next calendar day. New tasks require demonstrated control in the first prescribed attempts; no separate readiness test is added. Daily stimulus brief: E1 practices one receive-to-return action at a time. Other jobs connect leg preload to a guided arm press, arm draw to unilateral projection, loaded reach to pulling, one brief hand-contact reversal, and a higher forward release path. These are conditional skill exposures; first-attempt control decides the suitable version.

E: Light resistance, rapid purposeful effort and controlled resets. Use the least assistance/load needed to preserve speed and position; no generic age-based weight. No failure sets or conditioning circuit.

Recovery and quality: Rest 90 seconds between exercises, including after E6 before Section 3; extend to 2–3 minutes if control, attention or speed has not returned. Returns are controlled, not explosive, unless the row explicitly describes a linked action. Stop the set for pain, jerking, unwanted rotation, hard/asymmetric hand reception or clear loss of speed; reduce load/complexity for remaining work only if control returns. Otherwise stop and record the shortfall. Do not make up missed reps or count a non-flight press as a hand landing.

Delivery: Use a coach-controlled feed lane with no parallel throwing. Overhead release requires its own confirmed clearance; a 10 m lane does not prove containment. The band/bar bay and hand-flight support must sit outside all ball paths. No assumed partner skill, ball specification or staff count. Pair-contact push-ups require an immovable support and visibly controlled reception. Ball releases require an inspected throw-rated wall with a protected rebound area, or a clear open corridor containing flight, bounce and roll. No rebound catches unless explicitly prescribed in a row. Retrieve stopped balls on the coach's signal; nobody waits downrange. Three separate 10 m lanes do not confirm throwing containment or extra run-off. Equipment quantities, ball mass/size, anchor ratings, bar minimum load and support dimensions remain unconfirmed. Every replacement occupies its original slot only; a resisted press replacing a throw removes that release exposure and cannot supply the same assessment.
S: Light, controlled strengthening; keep at least 5 technically sound repetitions in reserve. These sets should not tire the athlete before primary lifting.

Rest 45 seconds between exercises and 60 seconds after S2 before strength preparation. Use lighter resistance or shorter comfortable range if control fades. Stop for symptoms rather than completing a nominal count.
P: These are working sets, each finishing with approximately 2–3 technically sound repetitions in reserve. Select challenging loads/assistance individually; a small set count does not mean a light effort. No forced reps, maximum testing, unstable supports or timed rotation. Work in order.

upper-body-force.quality: Quality marker, within E1: In E1 record successful receive-set-single-arm releases out of three attempts per arm. Ball remains controlled, the assisting hand clears before release and shoulders stay forward. Record arm, ball and replacement. Do not infer a weak side without actual observations. Record valid attempts and actual work, including misses; an invalid attempt consumes a rep. No bonus test attempts. Do not compare measurements from different drills as the same test.
upper-body-force.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1, supplied separately. Do not create or modify it. Its duration and workload are unknown; check its actual upper-body demand before proceeding.
upper-body-force.explosiveNotes: Baseline and current evidence: Ages 12–14 with established basic lifting technique and qualified supervision. Reviewed Class 6, saved workload/progression, drill use and available feedback before this prescription. No athlete completion, symptoms, load tolerance or improvement has been reported. This is a conditional planned class, not the next calendar day. New tasks require demonstrated control in the first prescribed attempts; no separate readiness test is added. Daily stimulus brief: The main projection task changes from two-hand receiving to one-arm release. Supported unilateral speed row and floor press isolate the arm's contribution; a modest vertical pull and dip-assisted landmine drive cover complementary pull/press demands. Two bilateral releases integrate the sides without a separate test block.

E: Light resistance, rapid purposeful effort and controlled resets. Use the least assistance/load needed to preserve speed and position; no generic age-based weight. No failure sets or conditioning circuit.

Recovery and quality: Rest 90 seconds between exercises, including after E6 before Section 3; extend to 2–3 minutes if control, attention or speed has not returned. Returns are controlled, not explosive, unless the row explicitly describes a linked action. Stop the set for pain, jerking, unwanted rotation, hard/asymmetric hand reception or clear loss of speed; reduce load/complexity for remaining work only if control returns. Otherwise stop and record the shortfall. Do not make up missed reps or count a non-flight press as a hand landing.

Delivery: Coach controls every feed in a protected lane; only a ball manageable by one arm is permitted. Use the same inspection/clearance rules for the bilateral release. Keep the supported-row and floor-press stations outside ball paths; inspect minimum landmine load and the overhead band attachment. No one-arm hanging or unsupported ballistic dumbbell catch is required. Ball releases require an inspected throw-rated wall with a protected rebound area, or a clear open corridor containing flight, bounce and roll. No rebound catches unless explicitly prescribed in a row. Retrieve stopped balls on the coach's signal; nobody waits downrange. Three separate 10 m lanes do not confirm throwing containment or extra run-off. Equipment quantities, ball mass/size, anchor ratings, bar minimum load and support dimensions remain unconfirmed. Every replacement occupies its original slot only; a resisted press replacing a throw removes that release exposure and cannot supply the same assessment.
S: Light, controlled strengthening; keep at least 5 technically sound repetitions in reserve. These sets should not tire the athlete before primary lifting.

Rest 45 seconds between exercises and 60 seconds after S2 before strength preparation. Use lighter resistance or shorter comfortable range if control fades. Stop for symptoms rather than completing a nominal count.
P: These are working sets, each finishing with approximately 2–3 technically sound repetitions in reserve. Select challenging loads/assistance individually; a small set count does not mean a light effort. No forced reps, maximum testing, unstable supports or timed rotation. Work in order.

Load-preparation sets of these same listed lifts: P1: 1 × 5 then 1 × 3 per arm; P2: 1 × 5 per arm; P3: 1 × 5 per arm; P4: 1 × 5; P5: 1 × 5; P6: 1 × 5. Use very light resistance; where two preparation sets are listed, the second is intermediate. Keep at least 5 technical reps in reserve. Rest 60 seconds between preparation rounds, 30 seconds between arms within a preparation round, then 90 seconds before P1/P2 working sets or 60 seconds before P3–P6 work. Preparation totals 51 repetitions, 7 rounds / 11 bouts. Extra load-finding reps add actual workload and time; never add an exercise.

Strength transitions: Rest 2 minutes after P1, P2 and P3, and 90 seconds after P4 and P5, before preparing the next lift. Increase load only when an available prescribed set can remain at the stated range, tempo and reserve; if the next increment is too large, hold the load. All symptom, speed and technique stops take precedence over the planned count.
