upper-body-force.progression: Progression note: Class 6 used one set of six for each primary lift. Here the main press changes to single-arm Floor Press 2 × 5 per arm, with one set of each supporting lift, including Row 1 × 6 per arm and strict Landmine Press 1 × 6 per arm. Seven rounds expand to eleven actual bouts because three lifts are unilateral; 64 task reps must not be mistaken for 64 bilateral cycles. No automatic load escalation: choose loads afresh for unilateral control, and retain a one-set version if readiness does not support the second press set. Before future advancement require both sides to demonstrate the stated control/reserve and reported recovery.

upper-body-force.title: Class 8
upper-body-force.effort: Transfer force into a strong backward draw while maintaining grip and shoulder control.
upper-body-force.delivery: Workload and timing: 13 rapid pull bilateral; 8 alternating arm pull; 4 throw unilateral; 3 throw bilateral. Primary work totals 66 task repetitions in 8 rounds / 10 bouts; resilience totals 20 task repetitions. Bilateral cycles count once; unilateral doses count both arms. These exposure types are not equivalent stress units. No lower-body jumping, sprinting or rotational throw work is added. Estimate 59–68 minutes after Access & Prepare 1, including listed work, resets, recovery, preparation and instruction; additional group queues or extra coaching add time. Complete session length is unresolved. Match the actual booking rather than compressing recovery. Scheduling: Review recent/upcoming throwing, contact sport, lifting and hand-supported tumbling. Plan the next demanding upper-body exposure on a nonconsecutive occasion, commonly 48–72 hours later initially, then adjust to actual recovery and schedule. Elapsed time is not proof of readiness. Body control remains separate.

upper-body-force.quality: Quality marker, within E1: In E1 record valid connected pulls out of 6: hips and elbows contribute smoothly, the bar remains controlled, shoulders do not shrug and there is no twisting or separate deadlift-then-row sequence. If using strict rows instead, record a different task; do not compare bar speed without a verified measurement method. Record valid attempts and actual work, including misses; an invalid attempt consumes a rep. No bonus test attempts. Do not compare measurements from different drills as the same test.
upper-body-force.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1, supplied separately. Do not create or modify it. Its duration and workload are unknown; check its actual upper-body demand before proceeding.
upper-body-force.explosiveNotes: Baseline and current evidence: Ages 12–14 with established basic lifting technique and qualified supervision. Reviewed Class 7, saved workload/progression, drill use and available feedback before this prescription. No athlete completion, symptoms, load tolerance or improvement has been reported. This is a conditional planned class, not the next calendar day. New tasks require demonstrated control in the first prescribed attempts; no separate readiness test is added. Daily stimulus brief: The main continuous power row connects a small hip impulse to arm force without a separate lower-body exercise. Alternating draws, elbow reversal and unilateral downward release provide differentiated pulling jobs. A small kneeling forward pass and shoulder-only pull preserve complementary force directions without new high-volume work.

E: Light resistance, rapid purposeful effort and controlled resets. Use the least assistance/load needed to preserve speed and position; no generic age-based weight. No failure sets or conditioning circuit.

Recovery and quality: Rest 90 seconds between exercises, including after E6 before Section 3; extend to 2–3 minutes if control, attention or speed has not returned. Returns are controlled, not explosive, unless the row explicitly describes a linked action. Stop the set for pain, jerking, unwanted rotation, hard/asymmetric hand reception or clear loss of speed; reduce load/complexity for remaining work only if control returns. Otherwise stop and record the shortfall. Do not make up missed reps or count a non-flight press as a hand landing.

Delivery: Inspect landmine arc, grip and plate clearance; nobody stands in its sweep. Use separate contained slam and forward-pass zones sequentially. Overhead and face-height band attachment points must be rated and permitted; they are not confirmed by band ownership. All ball and band replacements are slot-specific and change actual exposure counts. Ball releases require an inspected throw-rated wall with a protected rebound area, or a clear open corridor containing flight, bounce and roll. No rebound catches unless explicitly prescribed in a row. Retrieve stopped balls on the coach's signal; nobody waits downrange. Three separate 10 m lanes do not confirm throwing containment or extra run-off. Equipment quantities, ball mass/size, anchor ratings, bar minimum load and support dimensions remain unconfirmed. Every replacement occupies its original slot only; a resisted press replacing a throw removes that release exposure and cannot supply the same assessment.
S: Light, controlled strengthening; keep at least 5 technically sound repetitions in reserve. These sets should not tire the athlete before primary lifting.

Rest 45 seconds between exercises and 60 seconds after S2 before strength preparation. Use lighter resistance or shorter comfortable range if control fades. Stop for symptoms rather than completing a nominal count.
P: These are working sets, each finishing with approximately 2–3 technically sound repetitions in reserve. Select challenging loads/assistance individually; a small set count does not mean a light effort. No forced reps, maximum testing, unstable supports or timed rotation. Work in order.

Load-preparation sets of these same listed lifts: P1: 1 × 5 per arm; P2: 1 × 5; P3: 1 × 5; P4: 1 × 5; P5: 1 × 5; P6: 1 × 5. Use very light resistance; where two preparation sets are listed, the second is intermediate. Keep at least 5 technical reps in reserve. Rest 60 seconds between preparation rounds, 30 seconds between arms within a preparation round, then 90 seconds before P1/P2 working sets or 60 seconds before P3–P6 work. Preparation totals 35 repetitions, 6 rounds / 7 bouts. Extra load-finding reps add actual workload and time; never add an exercise.

Strength transitions: Rest 2 minutes after P1, P2 and P3, and 90 seconds after P4 and P5, before preparing the next lift. Increase load only when an available prescribed set can remain at the stated range, tempo and reserve; if the next increment is too large, hold the load. All symptom, speed and technique stops take precedence over the planned count.

upper-body-force.progression: Progression note: Class 7 prescribed 64 task reps across eleven unilateral-heavy primary bouts. This class returns to the already written Class 3 pulling allocation: One-Arm Row 2 × 6 per arm, Lat Pulldown 2 × 6, and one set each of rear-delt row, curl, Floor Press and elbow extension. That is eight rounds, ten bouts and 66 task reps. This returns to a known prescription, not an observed successful dose. The body-assisted speed row uses a light load independent of primary-row loading. Hold or regress if first-set mechanics or actual recovery does not support it; later progression requires reported control, reserve and recovery.

upper-body-force.title: Class 9
upper-body-force.effort: Time a controlled plant with forceful upper-body projection and pulling.
upper-body-force.delivery: Workload and timing: 6 throw bilateral; 4 throw unilateral; 4 alternating rope pull; 4 rapid pull unilateral; 6 rapid press bilateral. Primary work totals 68 task repetitions in 8 rounds / 10 bouts; resilience totals 18 task repetitions. Bilateral cycles count once; unilateral doses count both arms. These exposure types are not equivalent stress units. No lower-body jumping, sprinting or rotational throw work is added. Estimate 62–71 minutes after Access & Prepare 1, including listed work, resets, recovery, preparation and instruction; additional group queues or extra coaching add time. Complete session length is unresolved. Match the actual booking rather than compressing recovery. Scheduling: Review recent/upcoming throwing, contact sport, lifting and hand-supported tumbling. Plan the next demanding upper-body exposure on a nonconsecutive occasion, commonly 48–72 hours later initially, then adjust to actual recovery and schedule. Elapsed time is not proof of readiness. Body control remains separate.

upper-body-force.quality: Quality marker, within E1: In E1 record valid attempts out of three per lead foot: one controlled step, release timed to the plant, rear foot grounded, no trunk twist and a balanced finish inside the marked movement area. This moving release is not directly comparable with stationary pass distance. Record valid attempts and actual work, including misses; an invalid attempt consumes a rep. No bonus test attempts. Do not compare measurements from different drills as the same test.
upper-body-force.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1, supplied separately. Do not create or modify it. Its duration and workload are unknown; check its actual upper-body demand before proceeding.
upper-body-force.explosiveNotes: Baseline and current evidence: Ages 12–14 with established basic lifting technique and qualified supervision. Reviewed Class 8, saved workload/progression, drill use and available feedback before this prescription. No athlete completion, symptoms, load tolerance or improvement has been reported. This is a conditional planned class, not the next calendar day. New tasks require demonstrated control in the first prescribed attempts; no separate readiness test is added. Daily stimulus brief: The main task is one-step two-arm projection. A contralateral step-to-one-arm release and backward traction step extend the force-transfer problem in clearly different ways. Familiar short pulls and guided pressing limit extra learning demand; a modest wall push-off gives fixed-contact force expression without another ball release.

E: Light resistance, rapid purposeful effort and controlled resets. Use the least assistance/load needed to preserve speed and position; no generic age-based weight. No failure sets or conditioning circuit.

Recovery and quality: Rest 90 seconds between exercises, including after E6 before Section 3; extend to 2–3 minutes if control, attention or speed has not returned. Returns are controlled, not explosive, unless the row explicitly describes a linked action. Stop the set for pain, jerking, unwanted rotation, hard/asymmetric hand reception or clear loss of speed; reduce load/complexity for remaining work only if control returns. Otherwise stop and record the shortfall. Do not make up missed reps or count a non-flight press as a hand landing.

Delivery: Allocate and inspect a movement zone of up to 2 m within one 10 m lane for the start, single step and balanced stop; this is a programming requirement, not confirmed free space. Ball flight/bounce/roll needs additional contained clearance within the actual site. If both cannot fit, use stationary replacements. Keep backward rope stepping away from ball paths. The wall push-off needs a structural wall; no wall is inferred merely from medicine-ball ownership. Ball releases require an inspected throw-rated wall with a protected rebound area, or a clear open corridor containing flight, bounce and roll. No rebound catches unless explicitly prescribed in a row. Retrieve stopped balls on the coach's signal; nobody waits downrange. Three separate 10 m lanes do not confirm throwing containment or extra run-off. Equipment quantities, ball mass/size, anchor ratings, bar minimum load and support dimensions remain unconfirmed. Every replacement occupies its original slot only; a resisted press replacing a throw removes that release exposure and cannot supply the same assessment.
S: Light, controlled strengthening; keep at least 5 technically sound repetitions in reserve. These sets should not tire the athlete before primary lifting.

Rest 45 seconds between exercises and 60 seconds after S2 before strength preparation. Use lighter resistance or shorter comfortable range if control fades. Stop for symptoms rather than completing a nominal count.
P: These are working sets, each finishing with approximately 2–3 technically sound repetitions in reserve. Select challenging loads/assistance individually; a small set count does not mean a light effort. No forced reps, maximum testing, unstable supports or timed rotation. Work in order.

Load-preparation sets of these same listed lifts: P1: 1 × 6 then 1 × 3; P2: 1 × 5 per arm; P3: 1 × 3; P4: 1 × 5; P5: 1 × 5; P6: 1 × 5. Use very light resistance; where two preparation sets are listed, the second is intermediate. Keep at least 5 technical reps in reserve. Rest 60 seconds between preparation rounds, 30 seconds between arms within a preparation round, then 90 seconds before P1/P2 working sets or 60 seconds before P3–P6 work. Preparation totals 37 repetitions, 7 rounds / 8 bouts. Extra load-finding reps add actual workload and time; never add an exercise.

Strength transitions: Rest 2 minutes after P1, P2 and P3, and 90 seconds after P4 and P5, before preparing the next lift. Increase load only when an available prescribed set can remain at the stated range, tempo and reserve; if the next increment is too large, hold the load. All symptom, speed and technique stops take precedence over the planned count.

upper-body-force.progression: Progression note: Class 8 used the pulling-emphasis strength allocation. This class returns to the Class 1/2 balanced eight-round strength prescription, 68 task reps, at familiar demonstrated effort rather than higher weights. The new variable is plant-to-arm coordination; no sprint or jump is added. There are 14 prescribed movement steps: six bilateral-pass steps, four single-arm-throw steps and four rope-draw steps. They are not sprint metres or jump contacts. Without demonstrated plant control, stationary same-slot versions are the default. Future progression needs actual balanced finishes, controlled release line, technical strength reserve and recovery.

upper-body-force.title: Class 10
upper-body-force.effort: Finish forceful presses and pulls in controlled positions while preserving quality for primary strength.
upper-body-force.delivery: Workload and timing: 9 rapid press bilateral; 7 rapid pull bilateral; 4 rapid shoulder pull bilateral; 3 throw bilateral. Primary work totals 68 task repetitions in 8 rounds / 10 bouts; resilience totals 18 task repetitions. Bilateral cycles count once; unilateral doses count both arms. These exposure types are not equivalent stress units. No lower-body jumping, sprinting or rotational throw work is added. Estimate 60–69 minutes after Access & Prepare 1, including listed work, resets, recovery, preparation and instruction; additional group queues or extra coaching add time. Complete session length is unresolved. Match the actual booking rather than compressing recovery. Scheduling: Review recent/upcoming throwing, contact sport, lifting and hand-supported tumbling. Plan the next demanding upper-body exposure on a nonconsecutive occasion, commonly 48–72 hours later initially, then adjust to actual recovery and schedule. Elapsed time is not proof of readiness. Body control remains separate.

upper-body-force.quality: Quality marker, within E1: In E1 record clean finishes out of six attempts: held start stays still, wrists stay aligned, both arms complete rapidly and the ribs do not flare. Record band setup and range. This partial-range task is not comparable with full-range pressing speed or chest-pass distance. Record valid attempts and actual work, including misses; an invalid attempt consumes a rep. No bonus test attempts. Do not compare measurements from different drills as the same test.

upper-body-force.explosiveNotes: Baseline and current evidence: Ages 12–14 with established basic lifting technique and qualified supervision. Reviewed Class 9, saved workload/progression, drill use and available feedback before this prescription. No athlete completion, symptoms, load tolerance or improvement has been reported. This is a conditional planned class, not the next calendar day. New tasks require demonstrated control in the first prescribed attempts; no separate readiness test is added. Daily stimulus brief: Short mid-range press and row efforts address force completion; a nearly straight-elbow backward task separates shoulder contribution. Three familiar low-dose tasks preserve fixed-contact pushing, forward release and elbow-flexion speed without increasing coordination demands before strength.

E: Light resistance, rapid purposeful effort and controlled resets. Use the least assistance/load needed to preserve speed and position; no generic age-based weight. No failure sets or conditioning circuit.

Recovery and quality: Rest 90 seconds between exercises, including after E6 before Section 3; extend to 2–3 minutes if control, attention or speed has not returned. Returns are controlled, not explosive, unless the row explicitly describes a linked action. Stop the set for pain, jerking, unwanted rotation, hard/asymmetric hand reception or clear loss of speed; reduce load/complexity for remaining work only if control returns. Otherwise stop and record the shortfall. Do not make up missed reps or count a non-flight press as a hand landing.

Delivery: This class needs a permitted self-anchored band setup, dumbbells/floor support, an inspected structural wall for push-off and a contained coach-fed pass area. No overhead band attachment is required by the base prescription. Keep the quick reverse fly low-load and in a clear arm-sweep area; do not place it near passing athletes. Ball releases require an inspected throw-rated wall with a protected rebound area, or a clear open corridor containing flight, bounce and roll. No rebound catches unless explicitly prescribed in a row. Retrieve stopped balls on the coach's signal; nobody waits downrange. Three separate 10 m lanes do not confirm throwing containment or extra run-off. Equipment quantities, ball mass/size, anchor ratings, bar minimum load and support dimensions remain unconfirmed. Every replacement occupies its original slot only; a resisted press replacing a throw removes that release exposure and cannot supply the same assessment.
S: Light, controlled strengthening; keep at least 5 technically sound repetitions in reserve. These sets should not tire the athlete before primary lifting.

Rest 45 seconds between exercises and 60 seconds after S2 before strength preparation. Use lighter resistance or shorter comfortable range if control fades. Stop for symptoms rather than completing a nominal count.
P: These are working sets, each finishing with approximately 2–3 technically sound repetitions in reserve. Select challenging loads/assistance individually; a small set count does not mean a light effort. No forced reps, maximum testing, unstable supports or timed rotation. Work in order.

Load-preparation sets of these same listed lifts: P1: 1 × 6 then 1 × 3; P2: 1 × 5 per arm; P3: 1 × 3; P4: 1 × 5; P5: 1 × 5; P6: 1 × 5. Use very light resistance; where two preparation sets are listed, the second is intermediate. Keep at least 5 technical reps in reserve. Rest 60 seconds between preparation rounds, 30 seconds between arms within a preparation round, then 90 seconds before P1/P2 working sets or 60 seconds before P3–P6 work. Preparation totals 37 repetitions, 7 rounds / 8 bouts. Extra load-finding reps add actual workload and time; never add an exercise.

Strength transitions: Rest 2 minutes after P1, P2 and P3, and 90 seconds after P4 and P5, before preparing the next lift. Increase load only when an available prescribed set can remain at the stated range, tempo and reserve; if the next increment is too large, hold the load. All symptom, speed and technique stops take precedence over the planned count.

upper-body-force.progression: Progression note: Class 9 balanced strength doses are retained exactly: Floor Press 2 × 6, Row 2 × 6 per arm, and one set of eight for each remaining lift, totaling eight rounds and 68 task reps. The new drill emphasis is force completion, not an automatic strength-load increase. If actual prior full-range sets were controlled at the stated reserve with good recovery, consider the smallest practical increment on only one priority lift; otherwise hold or reduce. Do not shorten range to claim a heavier successful strength set. No class has established that an increment was earned.

upper-body-force.title: Class 11
upper-body-force.effort: Integrate receiving, a controlled plant and organized arm-force onset without inventing an athlete-specific weakness.
upper-body-force.delivery: Workload and timing: 7 throw bilateral; 4 rapid press unilateral; 6 rapid pull bilateral; 3 hand landing bilateral. Primary work totals 64 task repetitions in 8 rounds / 10 bouts; resilience totals 20 task repetitions. Bilateral cycles count once; unilateral doses count both arms. These exposure types are not equivalent stress units. No lower-body jumping, sprinting or rotational throw work is added. Estimate 61–70 minutes after Access & Prepare 1, including listed work, resets, recovery, preparation and instruction; additional group queues or extra coaching add time. Complete session length is unresolved. Match the actual booking rather than compressing recovery. Scheduling: Review recent/upcoming throwing, contact sport, lifting and hand-supported tumbling. Plan the next demanding upper-body exposure on a nonconsecutive occasion, commonly 48–72 hours later initially, then adjust to actual recovery and schedule. Elapsed time is not proof of readiness. Body control remains separate.

upper-body-force.quality: Quality marker, within E1: In E1 record valid cycles out of two per lead foot: clean receipt, exactly one controlled step, forward release on plant and a balanced stop. Record any simplified version and actual catches/steps. Do not label one lead foot weak without observations. Record valid attempts and actual work, including misses; an invalid attempt consumes a rep. No bonus test attempts. Do not compare measurements from different drills as the same test.

upper-body-force.explosiveNotes: Baseline and current evidence: Ages 12–14 with established basic lifting technique and qualified supervision. Reviewed Class 10, saved workload/progression, drill use and available feedback before this prescription. No athlete completion, symptoms, load tolerance or improvement has been reported. This is a conditional planned class, not the next calendar day. New tasks require demonstrated control in the first prescribed attempts; no separate readiness test is added. Daily stimulus brief: No deficit has been reported, so the chosen emphasis is integration. E1 links a gentle received load to one plant and forward release. Cued one-arm pressing and bilateral pulling emphasize readiness-to-force onset; three familiar short tasks preserve body-assisted pulling, higher forward projection and hand-contact force expression.

E: Light resistance, rapid purposeful effort and controlled resets. Use the least assistance/load needed to preserve speed and position; no generic age-based weight. No failure sets or conditioning circuit.

Recovery and quality: Rest 90 seconds between exercises, including after E6 before Section 3; extend to 2–3 minutes if control, attention or speed has not returned. Returns are controlled, not explosive, unless the row explicitly describes a linked action. Stop the set for pain, jerking, unwanted rotation, hard/asymmetric hand reception or clear loss of speed; reduce load/complexity for remaining work only if control returns. Otherwise stop and record the shortfall. Do not make up missed reps or count a non-flight press as a hand landing.

Delivery: Coach supervises the entire receive-step cycle in one protected lane. An inspected movement zone up to 2 m plus contained ball flight/bounce must fit; use stationary replacements otherwise. Keep the overhead throw and hand-flight support separate from that lane. Cue drills use voice only and require no timing device or added reaction station. Ball releases require an inspected throw-rated wall with a protected rebound area, or a clear open corridor containing flight, bounce and roll. No rebound catches unless explicitly prescribed in a row. Retrieve stopped balls on the coach's signal; nobody waits downrange. Three separate 10 m lanes do not confirm throwing containment or extra run-off. Equipment quantities, ball mass/size, anchor ratings, bar minimum load and support dimensions remain unconfirmed. Every replacement occupies its original slot only; a resisted press replacing a throw removes that release exposure and cannot supply the same assessment.
S: Light, controlled strengthening; keep at least 5 technically sound repetitions in reserve. These sets should not tire the athlete before primary lifting.

Rest 45 seconds between exercises and 60 seconds after S2 before strength preparation. Use lighter resistance or shorter comfortable range if control fades. Stop for symptoms rather than completing a nominal count.
P: These are working sets, each finishing with approximately 2–3 technically sound repetitions in reserve. Select challenging loads/assistance individually; a small set count does not mean a light effort. No forced reps, maximum testing, unstable supports or timed rotation. Work in order.

Load-preparation sets of these same listed lifts: P1: 1 × 6 then 1 × 3; P2: 1 × 5 per arm; P3: 1 × 3; P4: 1 × 5; P5: 1 × 5; P6: 1 × 5. Use very light resistance; where two preparation sets are listed, the second is intermediate. Keep at least 5 technical reps in reserve. Rest 60 seconds between preparation rounds, 30 seconds between arms within a preparation round, then 90 seconds before P1/P2 working sets or 60 seconds before P3–P6 work. Preparation totals 37 repetitions, 7 rounds / 8 bouts. Extra load-finding reps add actual workload and time; never add an exercise.

Strength transitions: Rest 2 minutes after P1, P2 and P3, and 90 seconds after P4 and P5, before preparing the next lift. Increase load only when an available prescribed set can remain at the stated range, tempo and reserve; if the next increment is too large, hold the load. All symptom, speed and technique stops take precedence over the planned count.

upper-body-force.title: Class 12
upper-body-force.effort: Review clean straight-line projection and purposeful push/pull force under controlled, documented conditions.
upper-body-force.delivery: Workload and timing: 9 throw bilateral; 4 rapid press unilateral; 4 rapid pull unilateral; 4 alternating arm press; 3 rapid shoulder pull bilateral; 4 throw unilateral. Primary work totals 68 task repetitions in 8 rounds / 10 bouts; resilience totals 14 task repetitions. Bilateral cycles count once; unilateral doses count both arms. These exposure types are not equivalent stress units. No lower-body jumping, sprinting or rotational throw work is added. Estimate 65–74 minutes after Access & Prepare 1, including listed work, resets, recovery, preparation and instruction; additional group queues or extra coaching add time. Complete session length is unresolved. Match the actual booking rather than compressing recovery. Scheduling: Review recent/upcoming throwing, contact sport, lifting and hand-supported tumbling. Plan the next demanding upper-body exposure on a nonconsecutive occasion, commonly 48–72 hours later initially, then adjust to actual recovery and schedule. Elapsed time is not proof of readiness. Body control remains separate.

upper-body-force.explosiveNotes: Baseline and current evidence: Ages 12–14 with established basic lifting technique and qualified supervision. Reviewed Class 11, saved workload/progression, drill use and available feedback before this prescription. No athlete completion, symptoms, load tolerance or improvement has been reported. This is a conditional planned class, not the next calendar day. New tasks require demonstrated control in the first prescribed attempts; no separate readiness test is added. Daily stimulus brief: E1 occupies a normal explosive slot as the justified reference task. Short unilateral force-onset, finish-range pulling and alternating loaded pressing review complementary arm-control jobs. A shoulder-only pull and fixed-base unilateral release complete the six slots without catches, travel or hand impacts. The original six strength lifts retain a comparable prescription, not a maximum test.

E: Light resistance, rapid purposeful effort and controlled resets. Use the least assistance/load needed to preserve speed and position; no generic age-based weight. No failure sets or conditioning circuit.

Recovery and quality: Rest 90 seconds between exercises, including after E6 before Section 3; extend to 2–3 minutes if control, attention or speed has not returned. Returns are controlled, not explosive, unless the row explicitly describes a linked action. Stop the set for pain, jerking, unwanted rotation, hard/asymmetric hand reception or clear loss of speed; reduce load/complexity for remaining work only if control returns. Otherwise stop and record the shortfall. Do not make up missed reps or count a non-flight press as a hand landing.

Delivery: Use a protected forward-release bay, inspected self-anchored band setup, stable floor/row supports and light dumbbells. No overhead attachment, moving release or coach feed is required. If the ball or site differs from actual baseline, record it and withhold a direct comparison. Keep the alternating floor press controlled; never toss or hand off weights between arms. Ball releases require an inspected throw-rated wall with a protected rebound area, or a clear open corridor containing flight, bounce and roll. No rebound catches unless explicitly prescribed in a row. Retrieve stopped balls on the coach's signal; nobody waits downrange. Three separate 10 m lanes do not confirm throwing containment or extra run-off. Equipment quantities, ball mass/size, anchor ratings, bar minimum load and support dimensions remain unconfirmed. Every replacement occupies its original slot only; a resisted press replacing a throw removes that release exposure and cannot supply the same assessment.
S: Light, controlled strengthening; keep at least 5 technically sound repetitions in reserve. These sets should not tire the athlete before primary lifting.

Rest 45 seconds between exercises and 60 seconds after S2 before strength preparation. Use lighter resistance or shorter comfortable range if control fades. Stop for symptoms rather than completing a nominal count.
P: These are working sets, each finishing with approximately 2–3 technically sound repetitions in reserve. Select challenging loads/assistance individually; a small set count does not mean a light effort. No forced reps, maximum testing, unstable supports or timed rotation. Work in order.

Load-preparation sets of these same listed lifts: P1: 1 × 6 then 1 × 3; P2: 1 × 5 per arm; P3: 1 × 3; P4: 1 × 5; P5: 1 × 5; P6: 1 × 5. Use very light resistance; where two preparation sets are listed, the second is intermediate. Keep at least 5 technical reps in reserve. Rest 60 seconds between preparation rounds, 30 seconds between arms within a preparation round, then 90 seconds before P1/P2 working sets or 60 seconds before P3–P6 work. Preparation totals 37 repetitions, 7 rounds / 8 bouts. Extra load-finding reps add actual workload and time; never add an exercise.

Strength transitions: Rest 2 minutes after P1, P2 and P3, and 90 seconds after P4 and P5, before preparing the next lift. Increase load only when an available prescribed set can remain at the stated range, tempo and reserve; if the next increment is too large, hold the load. All symptom, speed and technique stops take precedence over the planned count.

upper-body-force.progression: Progression note: Class 11 reduced two pressing supports to six reps. Here the original Class 1 strength prescription is restored: Floor Press 2 × 6, Row 2 × 6 per arm and one set of eight for each other lift, eight rounds and 68 task reps. Use current technically suitable loads at 2–3 RIR; repeat a prior load only if it remains appropriate. Compare actual load/quality records descriptively because preceding explosive exposure and readiness may differ. The exact E1 drill/dose is repeated for a possible matched reference; no athlete completion or improvement has been supplied. The next cycle should target a limitation shown by actual response, not an invented successful outcome.

lower-body-force.title: Week 1 — Settled force initiation
lower-body-force.effort: Produce a decisive knee, hip and ankle push from organized positions; express it upward and forward.
lower-body-force.delivery: Estimate 59–66 minutes after Access & Prepare 1 for an athlete with equipment access. Includes work, resets, listed recovery, preparation, transitions and 10–16 minutes of extra instruction/setup; additional queues, rest or load-finding add time. Existing preparation duration and total booking fit remain unresolved. Never compress needed recovery to fit a clock. One coached focus class per week for twelve weeks. Review actual sport, leg lifting, running, jumping and tumbling before delivery. Initially allow roughly 48–72 hours before another demanding leg exposure when the full schedule permits, adjusting to actual recovery; a week elapsed is not proof of readiness. Resume missed classes without doubling up. No additional full workouts or body-control blocks are prescribed.

lower-body-force.explosiveNotes: The still-start squat jump is the main task. Separate hip-driven implement motion, grounded ankle finish, forward projection, one-lead-leg rise and a small leg-driven release. Six direct strength jobs supply knee/hip extension, lead-leg contribution, knee-flexor leverage and both knee-angle plantar-flexion demands.

E: Use light resistance or bodyweight that permits visibly rapid force with control. Begin with E1 while fresh. Each row has a distinct job; supporting work stays small. Rest may be extended to 2–3 minutes when speed, control or attention has not returned. Stop for pain, loss of alignment, stiff/asymmetric landing or clear slowing; rest and regress remaining work only if control returns, otherwise record stopped work. Never make up failed attempts. No drop landings or rotational throws are prescribed.
S: Light controlled strengthening, at least 5 technical reps in reserve. Do not chase burn, shaking or pre-fatigue. Reduce load/range when control fades; stop for symptoms.
P: Working sets are challenging at about 2–3 technical reps/cycles in reserve. Select load/lever from demonstrated ability, not age or calendar week. Keep the stated controlled lowering and complete range; no forced repetitions, maximum testing or conditioning circuit. Check late-set and late-session quality; record reductions instead of forcing nominal completion.

lower-body-force.setup: Use one inspected takeoff lane, one low step and stable hand support; no jumping down. Kettlebell and throw tasks require separate clearance and coach attention. If the minimum bell or ball cannot move quickly with control, use the listed same-slot version. Inspect stable supports, minimum loads, surface grip and all active/waiting/return paths. Keep one athlete active per lane under suitable supervision; no group size or station count is assumed. Three separate 10 m lanes are not a 30 m runway. Ball releases need separately verified flight/bounce/roll containment. Replacements occupy the original slot; missing readiness or equipment can change the practice exposure and actual totals. Before applying multiple replacements, check the other rows: a replacement must not duplicate an exercise already delivered in another slot. Do not add duplicate work just to fill the count. If the supplied replacements cannot preserve distinct jobs, stop the affected slot and record a modified/incomplete session for revision; do not claim the planned six distinct explosive tasks were completed. Changed reset time, takeoff/landing type, sides and reps belong in the actual record.
lower-body-force.progression: No earlier prescription exists in this course. Establish Goblet Squat 2 × 6, RDL 2 × 6, Split Squat 1 × 5 per leg, both calf variants 1 × 8 and three complete walkout cycles. Loads follow current demonstrated control at 2–3 technical RIR. This is a baseline prescription, not evidence of beginner status or successful completion. Next week may shift investment toward hip force without automatically increasing load or total work.

lower-body-force.delivery: Estimate 54–61 minutes after Access & Prepare 1 for an athlete with equipment access. Includes work, resets, listed recovery, preparation, transitions and 10–16 minutes of extra instruction/setup; additional queues, rest or load-finding add time. Existing preparation duration and total booking fit remain unresolved. Never compress needed recovery to fit a clock. One coached focus class per week for twelve weeks. Review actual sport, leg lifting, running, jumping and tumbling before delivery. Initially allow roughly 48–72 hours before another demanding leg exposure when the full schedule permits, adjusting to actual recovery; a week elapsed is not proof of readiness. Resume missed classes without doubling up. No additional full workouts or body-control blocks are prescribed.

lower-body-force.setup: Keep swing, seated-jump and ball-release areas separate. Seat fit must permit feet planted and a clear floor landing in front; no rebound catches or jumping down from a box. Introduce the continuous swing only when the first prescribed repetitions stay hip-driven. Inspect stable supports, minimum loads, surface grip and all active/waiting/return paths. Keep one athlete active per lane under suitable supervision; no group size or station count is assumed. Three separate 10 m lanes are not a 30 m runway. Ball releases need separately verified flight/bounce/roll containment. Replacements occupy the original slot; missing readiness or equipment can change the practice exposure and actual totals. Before applying multiple replacements, check the other rows: a replacement must not duplicate an exercise already delivered in another slot. Do not add duplicate work just to fill the count. If the supplied replacements cannot preserve distinct jobs, stop the affected slot and record a modified/incomplete session for revision; do not claim the planned six distinct explosive tasks were completed. Changed reset time, takeoff/landing type, sides and reps belong in the actual record.
lower-body-force.progression: Week 1 prescribed eight primary rounds and nine bouts. Week 2 keeps RDL 2 × 6, reduces Goblet Squat to 1 × 6 and replaces Split Squat 1 × 5 per leg with floor bridge 1 × 6, giving seven rounds/seven bouts. Calf and walkout doses stay unchanged. This redirects effort to the hip while reducing overall strength work; it does not assert tolerance of new swing/rebound demands. Hold load until actual controlled completion and recovery support one relevant change.

lower-body-force.delivery: Estimate 64–71 minutes after Access & Prepare 1 for an athlete with equipment access. Includes work, resets, listed recovery, preparation, transitions and 10–16 minutes of extra instruction/setup; additional queues, rest or load-finding add time. Existing preparation duration and total booking fit remain unresolved. Never compress needed recovery to fit a clock. One coached focus class per week for twelve weeks. Review actual sport, leg lifting, running, jumping and tumbling before delivery. Initially allow roughly 48–72 hours before another demanding leg exposure when the full schedule permits, adjusting to actual recovery; a week elapsed is not proof of readiness. Resume missed classes without doubling up. No additional full workouts or body-control blocks are prescribed.

lower-body-force.quality: Within E1 record controlled split-start projections separately for each lead leg: front foot loaded, no twist, feet parallel at reception and a quiet 2 s hold. Record all four attempts per lead; no weak side is inferred before actual data exists. Use the listed attempts only; a miss or invalid attempt consumes the dose. Record actual attempts, setup and any substitutions; no bonus tests or comparison across unlike tasks.
lower-body-force.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1, supplied separately and unchanged. Do not create or infer its exercises, duration or workload. Check its actual lower-body demand before proceeding.
lower-body-force.explosiveNotes: The split-start broad jump keeps two-foot takeoff/reception but biases initiation toward one lead leg. Single-leg hip and ankle tasks isolate contributors; grounded step-up coordination and a small scoop connect them. Two short starts provide limited acceleration practice, not maximum-speed development.

E: Use light resistance or bodyweight that permits visibly rapid force with control. Begin with E1 while fresh. Each row has a distinct job; supporting work stays small. Rest may be extended to 2–3 minutes when speed, control or attention has not returned. Stop for pain, loss of alignment, stiff/asymmetric landing or clear slowing; rest and regress remaining work only if control returns, otherwise record stopped work. Never make up failed attempts. No drop landings or rotational throws are prescribed.
S: Light controlled strengthening, at least 5 technical reps in reserve. Do not chase burn, shaking or pre-fatigue. Reduce load/range when control fades; stop for symptoms.
P: Working sets are challenging at about 2–3 technical reps/cycles in reserve. Select load/lever from demonstrated ability, not age or calendar week. lower-body-force.setup: Inspect the split takeoff and receiving corridor. The two 2 m starts reserve the first 1 m for the starting stance, accelerate from 1 m to 3 m and need the final 7 m clear for deceleration; if the actual athlete cannot stop within it, use the listed grounded replacement. Running foot strikes are not counted as jump landings; record actual running contacts only if measured. Inspect stable supports, minimum loads, surface grip and all active/waiting/return paths. Keep one athlete active per lane under suitable supervision; no group size or station count is assumed. Three separate 10 m lanes are not a 30 m runway. Ball releases need separately verified flight/bounce/roll containment. Replacements occupy the original slot; missing readiness or equipment can change the practice exposure and actual totals. Braking travel, ordinary running foot strikes and walking returns are not jump contacts or the recorded accelerating metres; actual distances/steps remain unknown and must be logged if measured. Mark the entire start/drive/stop envelope inside the lane: front starting foot at 1 m, trailing foot inside the first metre, drive to 3 m and stop by 10 m. Shorten effort or use the grounded replacement if the stance or stopping margin does not fit. Before applying multiple replacements, check the other rows: a replacement must not duplicate an exercise already delivered in another slot. Do not add duplicate work just to fill the count. If the supplied replacements cannot preserve distinct jobs, stop the affected slot and record a modified/incomplete session for revision; do not claim the planned six distinct explosive tasks were completed. Changed reset time, takeoff/landing type, sides and reps belong in the actual record.

Seven rounds now require nine bouts, so this is not an equal-time dose merely because the round count matches. Choose loads for current split-stance control; no increase is earned. lower-body-force.quality: Use E1’s three attempts to record settled-start control and a quiet held reception, under the same setup as Week 1 if comparison is intended. Three attempts are a reduced sample, not a matched six-attempt performance test. Use the listed attempts only; a miss or invalid attempt consumes the dose. Record actual attempts, setup and any substitutions; no bonus tests or comparison across unlike tasks.
lower-body-force.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1, supplied separately and unchanged. Do not create or infer its exercises, duration or workload. Check its actual lower-body demand before proceeding.
lower-body-force.explosiveNotes: A short familiar still-start jump leads. Retained grounded hip, ankle and step-up tasks plus two isolated countermovement jumps maintain six separate jobs with fewer repetitions. All drills deliberately repeat for consolidation; no new test or skill is introduced.

E: Use light resistance or bodyweight that permits visibly rapid force with control. Begin with E1 while fresh. Each row has a distinct job; supporting work stays small. Rest may be extended to 2–3 minutes when speed, control or attention has not returned. Stop for pain, loss of alignment, stiff/asymmetric landing or clear slowing; rest and regress remaining work only if control returns, otherwise record stopped work. Never make up failed attempts. No drop landings or rotational throws are prescribed.
S: Light controlled strengthening, at least 5 technical reps in reserve. Do not chase burn, shaking or pre-fatigue. Reduce load/range when control fades; stop for symptoms.
P: Working sets are challenging at about 2–3 technical reps/cycles in reserve. Select load/lever from demonstrated ability, not age or calendar week. Keep the stated controlled lowering and complete range; no forced repetitions, maximum testing or conditioning circuit. Check late-set and late-session quality; record reductions instead of forcing nominal completion.

lower-body-force.setup: Use the same low step, stable supports and grounded equipment arrangements already specified. No throwing station, linked landing, running lane start or new apparatus is needed. Keep individual load preparation despite the smaller working dose. Inspect stable supports, minimum loads, surface grip and all active/waiting/return paths. Keep one athlete active per lane under suitable supervision; no group size or station count is assumed. Three separate 10 m lanes are not a 30 m runway. Ball releases need separately verified flight/bounce/roll containment. Replacements occupy the original slot; missing readiness or equipment can change the practice exposure and actual totals. Before applying multiple replacements, check the other rows: a replacement must not duplicate an exercise already delivered in another slot. Do not add duplicate work just to fill the count. If the supplied replacements cannot preserve distinct jobs, stop the affected slot and record a modified/incomplete session for revision; do not claim the planned six distinct explosive tasks were completed. Changed reset time, takeoff/landing type, sides and reps belong in the actual record.
lower-body-force.progression: Compared with Week 5, linked contacts and throws are removed, primary bouts fall seven to six, conventional working reps fall 32 to 22, and walkouts remain two cycles. Split Squat gives way to familiar bilateral floor bridge to reduce side-specific work. All six primary entries stay challenging at 2–3 technical RIR using currently appropriate load/lever; reduce load as needed rather than preserving fatigue. Preparation is one light three-rep set per conventional lift and one walkout cycle. Week 7 demand is conditional on actual recovery, never on this written lighter week.

lower-body-force.title: Week 7 — Independent stance-leg force
lower-body-force.effort: Produce upward and short forward force from each stance leg while controlling the pelvis and receiving on two feet.
lower-body-force.delivery: Estimate 58–65 minutes after Access & Prepare 1 for an athlete with equipment access. Includes work, resets, listed recovery, preparation, transitions and 10–16 minutes of extra instruction/setup; additional queues, rest or load-finding add time. Existing preparation duration and total booking fit remain unresolved. Never compress needed recovery to fit a clock. One coached focus class per week for twelve weeks. Review actual sport, leg lifting, running, jumping and tumbling before delivery. Initially allow roughly 48–72 hours before another demanding leg exposure when the full schedule permits, adjusting to actual recovery; a week elapsed is not proof of readiness. Resume missed classes without doubling up. No additional full workouts or body-control blocks are prescribed.

lower-body-force.quality: In E1 record each takeoff leg, actual hand/arm strategy and whether the two-foot reception is quiet and held for 2 s. An uncontrolled first attempt triggers the grounded replacement for remaining attempts; no extra prerequisite test or symmetry claim is added. Use the listed attempts only; a miss or invalid attempt consumes the dose. Record actual attempts, setup and any substitutions; no bonus tests or comparison across unlike tasks.
lower-body-force.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1, supplied separately and unchanged. Do not create or infer its exercises, duration or workload. Check its actual lower-body demand before proceeding.
lower-body-force.explosiveNotes: Six low, isolated one-leg vertical takeoffs anchor the session. Grounded lead-biased hip initiation, supported one-leg knee force, ankle force and hip finish support them; two short forward takeoffs provide a small vector transfer. No same-leg landing series is prescribed.

E: Use light resistance or bodyweight that permits visibly rapid force with control. Begin with E1 while fresh. Each row has a distinct job; supporting work stays small. Rest may be extended to 2–3 minutes when speed, control or attention has not returned. Stop for pain, loss of alignment, stiff/asymmetric landing or clear slowing; rest and regress remaining work only if control returns, otherwise record stopped work. Never make up failed attempts. No drop landings or rotational throws are prescribed.
S: Light controlled strengthening, at least 5 technical reps in reserve. Do not chase burn, shaking or pre-fatigue. Reduce load/range when control fades; stop for symptoms.
P: Working sets are challenging at about 2–3 technical reps/cycles in reserve. Select load/lever from demonstrated ability, not age or calendar week. Keep the stated controlled lowering and complete range; no forced repetitions, maximum testing or conditioning circuit. Check late-set and late-session quality; record reductions instead of forcing nominal completion.

lower-body-force.setup: Keep both receiving tasks in the marked short-takeoff area, leaving the rest of the lane clear. No box reception or running approach is required. Stable hand supports must be independently inspected. The single-leg calf preparation and work are separately dosed per leg. Inspect stable supports, minimum loads, surface grip and all active/waiting/return paths. Keep one athlete active per lane under suitable supervision; no group size or station count is assumed. Three separate 10 m lanes are not a 30 m runway. Ball releases need separately verified flight/bounce/roll containment. Replacements occupy the original slot; missing readiness or equipment can change the practice exposure and actual totals. Before applying multiple replacements, check the other rows: a replacement must not duplicate an exercise already delivered in another slot. Do not add duplicate work just to fill the count. If the supplied replacements cannot preserve distinct jobs, stop the affected slot and record a modified/incomplete session for revision; do not claim the planned six distinct explosive tasks were completed. Changed reset time, takeoff/landing type, sides and reps belong in the actual record.
lower-body-force.progression: Week 6 deliberately reduced work. This conditional week restores eight landing events with eight single-leg takeoffs, six primary rounds/eight bouts and 34 conventional reps plus two walkout cycles. Split Squat returns at 1 × 4 per leg; RDL/bridge become 1 × 5; supported Single-Leg Calf Raise 1 × 5 per leg replaces bilateral straight-knee calf loading. Goblet Squat is omitted because lead-leg knee force is the priority. Do not restore this demand merely because the midpoint week was authored: hold Week 6 or use the listed lower-complexity replacements if actual readiness is unconfirmed at delivery.

lower-body-force.title: Week 8 — Hip-to-ankle sequencing
lower-body-force.effort: Connect rapid hip extension through the ankle without compensatory trunk or arm motion.
lower-body-force.delivery: Estimate 52–58 minutes after Access & Prepare 1 for an athlete with equipment access. Includes work, resets, listed recovery, preparation, transitions and 10–16 minutes of extra instruction/setup; additional queues, rest or load-finding add time. Existing preparation duration and total booking fit remain unresolved. Never compress needed recovery to fit a clock. One coached focus class per week for twelve weeks. Review actual sport, leg lifting, running, jumping and tumbling before delivery. Initially allow roughly 48–72 hours before another demanding leg exposure when the full schedule permits, adjusting to actual recovery; a week elapsed is not proof of readiness. Resume missed classes without doubling up. No additional full workouts or body-control blocks are prescribed.

lower-body-force.quality: In E1 record whether the six listed releases show hip drive preceding a smooth forefoot finish, with no second dip or arm curl. Keep ball, start position and trajectory noted; do not compare distance with the earlier different scoop executions. Use the listed attempts only; a miss or invalid attempt consumes the dose. Record actual attempts, setup and any substitutions; no bonus tests or comparison across unlike tasks.
lower-body-force.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1, supplied separately and unchanged. Do not create or infer its exercises, duration or workload. Check its actual lower-body demand before proceeding.
lower-body-force.explosiveNotes: The held-hinge leg-driven release leads, with small forward ankle impulses, familiar hip reversals, a stance-leg finish, flexed-knee ankle output and a seated knee/hip start supporting distinct parts of the chain. Landing exposure falls and primary work returns to bilateral bases.

E: Use light resistance or bodyweight that permits visibly rapid force with control. Begin with E1 while fresh. Each row has a distinct job; supporting work stays small. Rest may be extended to 2–3 minutes when speed, control or attention has not returned. Stop for pain, loss of alignment, stiff/asymmetric landing or clear slowing; rest and regress remaining work only if control returns, otherwise record stopped work. Never make up failed attempts. No drop landings or rotational throws are prescribed.
S: Light controlled strengthening, at least 5 technical reps in reserve. Do not chase burn, shaking or pre-fatigue. Reduce load/range when control fades; stop for symptoms.
P: Working sets are challenging at about 2–3 technical reps/cycles in reserve. Select load/lever from demonstrated ability, not age or calendar week. Keep the stated controlled lowering and complete range; no forced repetitions, maximum testing or conditioning circuit. Check late-set and late-session quality; record reductions instead of forcing nominal completion.

lower-body-force.setup: Verify ball flight, ceiling, bounce and roll containment before using the main release. Keep the short pogo series well inside the first 3 m with remaining space clear. Bench height must fit the athlete for both sit-to-stand and seated calf work; no adjustable bench is presumed. Inspect stable supports, minimum loads, surface grip and all active/waiting/return paths. Keep one athlete active per lane under suitable supervision; no group size or station count is assumed. Three separate 10 m lanes are not a 30 m runway. Ball releases need separately verified flight/bounce/roll containment. Replacements occupy the original slot; missing readiness or equipment can change the practice exposure and actual totals. Before applying multiple replacements, check the other rows: a replacement must not duplicate an exercise already delivered in another slot. Do not add duplicate work just to fill the count. If the supplied replacements cannot preserve distinct jobs, stop the affected slot and record a modified/incomplete session for revision; do not claim the planned six distinct explosive tasks were completed. Changed reset time, takeoff/landing type, sides and reps belong in the actual record.
lower-body-force.progression: Week 7 prescribed eight unilateral takeoffs and eight bilateral landings. Here only three small bilateral pogo landings remain, alongside six separate throws. RDL returns to two rounds at 2 × 5 rather than the older 2 × 6; Goblet Squat 1 × 5 replaces Split Squat, and bilateral straight-knee calf 1 × 6 replaces the single-leg calf. Seven primary rounds/seven bouts contain 32 conventional reps plus two cycles. The second RDL round is a conditional restoration of hinge practice, not permission for heavier loads; hold one round if actual readiness does not support it and log the modification.

lower-body-force.title: Week 9 — Controlled entry into force
lower-body-force.effort: Turn a quiet, short entry into a purposeful upward or forward leg push.
lower-body-force.delivery: Estimate 53–60 minutes after Access & Prepare 1 for an athlete with equipment access. Includes work, resets, listed recovery, preparation, transitions and 10–16 minutes of extra instruction/setup; additional queues, rest or load-finding add time. Existing preparation duration and total booking fit remain unresolved. Never compress needed recovery to fit a clock. One coached focus class per week for twelve weeks. Review actual sport, leg lifting, running, jumping and tumbling before delivery. Initially allow roughly 48–72 hours before another demanding leg exposure when the full schedule permits, adjusting to actual recovery; a week elapsed is not proof of readiness. Resume missed classes without doubling up. No additional full workouts or body-control blocks are prescribed.

lower-body-force.quality: In E1 record whether the two walking foot placements lead to a stable two-foot plant, clear upward push and a 2 s held reception. A rushed plant, extra hop or unstable reception consumes the attempt and triggers a simpler remaining prescription. Use the listed attempts only; a miss or invalid attempt consumes the dose. Record actual attempts, setup and any substitutions; no bonus tests or comparison across unlike tasks.
lower-body-force.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1, supplied separately and unchanged. Do not create or infer its exercises, duration or workload. Check its actual lower-body demand before proceeding.
lower-body-force.explosiveNotes: Four walk-in vertical takeoffs anchor the day; two short forward takeoffs change output direction. Grounded lunge return, a stepped leg-driven release, a small step reversal and hip-finish reversal train controlled entry without adding hard approaches. Strength work is reduced while entry constraints change.

E: Use light resistance or bodyweight that permits visibly rapid force with control. Begin with E1 while fresh. Each row has a distinct job; supporting work stays small. Rest may be extended to 2–3 minutes when speed, control or attention has not returned. Stop for pain, loss of alignment, stiff/asymmetric landing or clear slowing; rest and regress remaining work only if control returns, otherwise record stopped work. Never make up failed attempts. No drop landings or rotational throws are prescribed.
S: Light controlled strengthening, at least 5 technical reps in reserve. Do not chase burn, shaking or pre-fatigue. Reduce load/range when control fades; stop for symptoms.
P: Working sets are challenging at about 2–3 technical reps/cycles in reserve. Select load/lever from demonstrated ability, not age or calendar week. Keep the stated controlled lowering and complete range; no forced repetitions, maximum testing or conditioning circuit. Check late-set and late-session quality; record reductions instead of forcing nominal completion.

lower-body-force.setup: Mark the whole walking entry and takeoff/receiving corridor within the first 3 m, leaving 7 m clear; shorten steps and projection or use stationary replacements if the actual athlete cannot fit. E1/E2 contain 12 total walking entry foot placements and E4 adds two, for 14 prescribed approach steps. Ordinary reset walks and grounded lunge/step movements are separate unmeasured travel, not sprint metres or jump contacts. No start is outside the lane. Inspect stable supports, minimum loads, surface grip and all active/waiting/return paths. Keep one athlete active per lane under suitable supervision; no group size or station count is assumed. Three separate 10 m lanes are not a 30 m runway. Ball releases need separately verified flight/bounce/roll containment. Replacements occupy the original slot; missing readiness or equipment can change the practice exposure and actual totals. Before applying multiple replacements, check the other rows: a replacement must not duplicate an exercise already delivered in another slot. Do not add duplicate work just to fill the count. If the supplied replacements cannot preserve distinct jobs, stop the affected slot and record a modified/incomplete session for revision; do not claim the planned six distinct explosive tasks were completed. Changed reset time, takeoff/landing type, sides and reps belong in the actual record.
lower-body-force.progression: Week 8 had seven primary rounds/seven bilateral bouts. Here Reverse Lunge returns at 1 × 4 per leg, RDL falls 2 × 5 to 1 × 5 and Goblet Squat stays 1 × 5; bridge gives way to the lead-leg job. Six rounds/seven bouts contain 30 conventional reps plus two cycles. Keep all approach entries walking-speed, and hold load while actual entry control is assessed; no faster entry or heavier load follows automatically.

lower-body-force.title: Week 10 — Force through the finish
lower-body-force.effort: Complete knee, hip and ankle extension without losing the force-producing base or compensating through the trunk.
lower-body-force.delivery: Estimate 54–61 minutes after Access & Prepare 1 for an athlete with equipment access. Includes work, resets, listed recovery, preparation, transitions and 10–16 minutes of extra instruction/setup; additional queues, rest or load-finding add time. Existing preparation duration and total booking fit remain unresolved. Never compress needed recovery to fit a clock. One coached focus class per week for twelve weeks. Review actual sport, leg lifting, running, jumping and tumbling before delivery. Initially allow roughly 48–72 hours before another demanding leg exposure when the full schedule permits, adjusting to actual recovery; a week elapsed is not proof of readiness. Resume missed classes without doubling up. No additional full workouts or body-control blocks are prescribed.

lower-body-force.quality: Record E1’s six attempts under the Week 4 setup when possible: one controlled dip, clear extension and a held quiet reception. Do not chase a locked knee, exaggerated toe point or arched finish; changed setup makes output comparisons descriptive only. Use the listed attempts only; a miss or invalid attempt consumes the dose. lower-body-force.explosiveNotes: The familiar countermovement jump provides the main upward-force reference. Grounded lead-leg extension, a bench-supported hip finish, rear-ankle output, four fixed-split receptions and a familiar hip reversal give distinct supporting jobs. Walking entries are removed and primary work uses bilateral bases.

E: Use light resistance or bodyweight that permits visibly rapid force with control. Begin with E1 while fresh. Each row has a distinct job; supporting work stays small. Rest may be extended to 2–3 minutes when speed, control or attention has not returned. Stop for pain, loss of alignment, stiff/asymmetric landing or clear slowing; rest and regress remaining work only if control returns, otherwise record stopped work. Never make up failed attempts. No drop landings or rotational throws are prescribed.
S: Light controlled strengthening, at least 5 technical reps in reserve. Do not chase burn, shaking or pre-fatigue. Reduce load/range when control fades; stop for symptoms.
P: Working sets are challenging at about 2–3 technical reps/cycles in reserve. Select load/lever from demonstrated ability, not age or calendar week. Keep the stated controlled lowering and complete range; no forced repetitions, maximum testing or conditioning circuit. Check late-set and late-session quality; record reductions instead of forcing nominal completion.

lower-body-force.setup: The new rapid hip thrust requires a bench that fits the athlete and cannot slide; the floor-bridge replacement is already fully dosed. Keep split-stance takeoff/receiving inside a marked short area. Rear-heel work stays grounded and outside active lanes. No running entry or object release is needed. Inspect stable supports, minimum loads, surface grip and all active/waiting/return paths. Keep one athlete active per lane under suitable supervision; no group size or station count is assumed. Three separate 10 m lanes are not a 30 m runway. Ball releases need separately verified flight/bounce/roll containment. Replacements occupy the original slot; missing readiness or equipment can change the practice exposure and actual totals. Before applying multiple replacements, check the other rows: a replacement must not duplicate an exercise already delivered in another slot. Do not add duplicate work just to fill the count. If the supplied replacements cannot preserve distinct jobs, stop the affected slot and record a modified/incomplete session for revision; do not claim the planned six distinct explosive tasks were completed. Changed reset time, takeoff/landing type, sides and reps belong in the actual record.
lower-body-force.progression: Week 9 prescribed six primary rounds/seven bouts. Here Goblet Squat returns to two rounds at 2 × 5, RDL remains 1 × 5 and floor bridge 1 × 5 replaces Reverse Lunge. Seven rounds/seven bilateral bouts contain 32 conventional reps plus two walkout cycles. Landings rise six to ten but walking entries and throws are removed; the different event types are not treated as equivalent stress. Use modest split-jump height and hold load; reduce the remaining jump effort or strength round if actual quality warrants it.

lower-body-force.title: Week 11 — Connect and control
lower-body-force.effort: Connect a small receiving or lowering action to purposeful leg force, while retaining the ability to stop and reset.
lower-body-force.delivery: Estimate 50–57 minutes after Access & Prepare 1 for an athlete with equipment access. Includes work, resets, listed recovery, preparation, transitions and 10–16 minutes of extra instruction/setup; additional queues, rest or load-finding add time. Existing preparation duration and total booking fit remain unresolved. Never compress needed recovery to fit a clock. One coached focus class per week for twelve weeks. Review actual sport, leg lifting, running, jumping and tumbling before delivery. Initially allow roughly 48–72 hours before another demanding leg exposure when the full schedule permits, adjusting to actual recovery; a week elapsed is not proof of readiness. Resume missed classes without doubling up. No additional full workouts or body-control blocks are prescribed.

lower-body-force.quality: In E1 record whether each first reception permits the second controlled upward push and whether the final landing is held. Four attempts are the entire dose; an invalid first landing stops that pair. Do not compare paired-jump output directly with isolated references. Use the listed attempts only; a miss or invalid attempt consumes the dose. Record actual attempts, setup and any substitutions; no bonus tests or comparison across unlike tasks.
lower-body-force.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1, supplied separately and unchanged. Do not create or infer its exercises, duration or workload. Check its actual lower-body demand before proceeding.
lower-body-force.explosiveNotes: Two controlled vertical-jump pairs lead. Grounded split-stance release, a small step reversal, rapid floor-to-stand loading, interrupted ankle pairs and a familiar hip finish cover the other force jobs. This is a small integration exposure, not a workload peak or fatigue challenge.

E: Use light resistance or bodyweight that permits visibly rapid force with control. Begin with E1 while fresh. Each row has a distinct job; supporting work stays small. Rest may be extended to 2–3 minutes when speed, control or attention has not returned. Stop for pain, loss of alignment, stiff/asymmetric landing or clear slowing; rest and regress remaining work only if control returns, otherwise record stopped work. Never make up failed attempts. No drop landings or rotational throws are prescribed.
S: Light controlled strengthening, at least 5 technical reps in reserve. Do not chase burn, shaking or pre-fatigue. Reduce load/range when control fades; stop for symptoms.
P: Working sets are challenging at about 2–3 technical reps/cycles in reserve. Select load/lever from demonstrated ability, not age or calendar week. Keep the stated controlled lowering and complete range; no forced repetitions, maximum testing or conditioning circuit. Check late-set and late-session quality; record reductions instead of forcing nominal completion.

lower-body-force.setup: No walking approach is prescribed. Keep linked jumps and ankle pairs in place within the marked receiving area; separate their reset periods. Four pogo repetitions are explicitly two pairs, with between-rep gaps 0 / 15 / 0 s. Verify bell handle height and minimum load, stable low step and ball containment before delivery. Inspect stable supports, minimum loads, surface grip and all active/waiting/return paths. Keep one athlete active per lane under suitable supervision; no group size or station count is assumed. Three separate 10 m lanes are not a 30 m runway. Ball releases need separately verified flight/bounce/roll containment. Replacements occupy the original slot; missing readiness or equipment can change the practice exposure and actual totals. Before applying multiple replacements, check the other rows: a replacement must not duplicate an exercise already delivered in another slot. Do not add duplicate work just to fill the count. If the supplied replacements cannot preserve distinct jobs, stop the affected slot and record a modified/incomplete session for revision; do not claim the planned six distinct explosive tasks were completed. Changed reset time, takeoff/landing type, sides and reps belong in the actual record.
lower-body-force.progression: Week 10 had seven primary rounds/seven bouts and 32 conventional reps. This week uses six rounds/seven bouts and 30 reps plus two cycles: Goblet Squat falls 2 × 5 to 1 × 5, RDL stays 1 × 5 and Split Squat 1 × 4 per leg replaces floor bridge. Landing events fall ten to eight, with four of the eight low-amplitude ankle contacts; two grounded throws return. These mixed events are not equivalent stress units. Keep modest jump height and current technical reserve; linking is conditional on demonstrated first-reception control.

lower-body-force.title: Week 12 — Review and next-cycle decision
lower-body-force.effort: Review still-start leg-force quality under matched conditions, then retain a small dose of direct knee, hip and ankle support.
lower-body-force.delivery: Estimate 51–58 minutes after Access & Prepare 1 for an athlete with equipment access. Includes work, resets, listed recovery, preparation, transitions and 10–16 minutes of extra instruction/setup; additional queues, rest or load-finding add time. Existing preparation duration and total booking fit remain unresolved. Never compress needed recovery to fit a clock. One coached focus class per week for twelve weeks. Review actual sport, leg lifting, running, jumping and tumbling before delivery. Initially allow roughly 48–72 hours before another demanding leg exposure when the full schedule permits, adjusting to actual recovery; a week elapsed is not proof of readiness. Resume missed classes without doubling up. No additional full workouts or body-control blocks are prescribed.

lower-body-force.quality: For E1 match Week 1 surface, footwear, hands at hips, actual quarter-squat depth, 2 s stationary start, absence of a second dip, bilateral 2 s reception, six attempts and 90 s set recovery. Compare a measured output only if the same verified device/method and conditions were actually recorded at both exposures. Otherwise report current execution only; missing baseline is not zero. Use the listed attempts only; a miss or invalid attempt consumes the dose. Record actual attempts, setup and any substitutions; no bonus tests or comparison across unlike tasks.
lower-body-force.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1, supplied separately and unchanged. Do not create or infer its exercises, duration or workload. Check its actual lower-body demand before proceeding.
lower-body-force.explosiveNotes: The original six-attempt settled squat jump is the only matched performance reference. Five familiar reduced-dose supports keep hip initiation, ankle finish, lead-leg drive, leg-led forward release and independent knee force represented. Strength holds the prior working dose; no final-week peak or new skill is imposed.

E: Use light resistance or bodyweight that permits visibly rapid force with control. Begin with E1 while fresh. Each row has a distinct job; supporting work stays small. Rest may be extended to 2–3 minutes when speed, control or attention has not returned. Stop for pain, loss of alignment, stiff/asymmetric landing or clear slowing; rest and regress remaining work only if control returns, otherwise record stopped work. Never make up failed attempts. No drop landings or rotational throws are prescribed.
S: Light controlled strengthening, at least 5 technical reps in reserve. Do not chase burn, shaking or pre-fatigue. Reduce load/range when control fades; stop for symptoms.
P: Working sets are challenging at about 2–3 technical reps/cycles in reserve. Select load/lever from demonstrated ability, not age or calendar week. Keep the stated controlled lowering and complete range; no forced repetitions, maximum testing or conditioning circuit. Check late-set and late-session quality; record reductions instead of forcing nominal completion.

lower-body-force.setup: Reuse the actual Week 1 setup for E1 if it is known and suitable. A changed surface, arm strategy, dip, measurement method or recovery is recorded as an unmatched comparison. Other supporting tasks are deliberately lower-dose and not pre/post tests. No extra trials, force-plate protocol or timing-gate capability is invented. Inspect stable supports, minimum loads, surface grip and all active/waiting/return paths. Keep one athlete active per lane under suitable supervision; no group size or station count is assumed. Three separate 10 m lanes are not a 30 m runway. Ball releases need separately verified flight/bounce/roll containment. Replacements occupy the original slot; missing readiness or equipment can change the practice exposure and actual totals. Before applying multiple replacements, check the other rows: a replacement must not duplicate an exercise already delivered in another slot. Do not add duplicate work just to fill the count. If the supplied replacements cannot preserve distinct jobs, stop the affected slot and record a modified/incomplete session for revision; do not claim the planned six distinct explosive tasks were completed. Changed reset time, takeoff/landing type, sides and reps belong in the actual record.
lower-body-force.progression: Week 11 linked jumps and pogos are removed. Week 12 uses six isolated bilateral landings, two throws and ten grounded rapid reps; primary strength holds exactly six rounds/seven bouts, 30 conventional reps and two walkout cycles. Strength loads are held only if current technique/reserve support them; heavier loads are never inferred from reaching Week 12. Compare recurring lift technique, actual load, range, reserve and recovery only where compatible records exist. The next cycle should retain, reduce or advance one relevant variable based on actual observations.

Start in a modest staggered stance, sleeve near the rear shoulder; pivot the rear foot and turn into a controlled forward/up press. No dip-drive, jump or release. Return in 3 seconds; keep the shoulder away from the ear. Rest 90 seconds between sides; 2 minutes between rounds. Reduce load if the elbow/wrist collapses or the lower back supplies the finish.

exercises.dose: 1 × 8 per arm; 16 reps

Band anchored in front at lower-chest height, opposite foot forward; reach without rounding, then turn feet/hips/trunk modestly as the elbow draws toward the same-side lower ribs. Return in 3 seconds under band tension. This is a single rotational row, not a row-plus-twist combination. Rest 90 seconds between sides. Reduce tension if the shoulder hikes or the athlete yanks from the low back.

rotation-upper.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1, unchanged. Content, duration and overlapping loading are unavailable; do not recreate it or assign it a time. Review its actual demands before delivery.
rotation-upper.explosiveNotes: Exactly six exercises. Movement is deliberately small, with total travel no more than 1 m. The upper-body rotational impulse is the task; this is not a sprint or agility conditioning session. Use light implements and fast coordinated intent; a retained-load drill ends under control rather than being released. Both sides receive the written dose.

exercises.description: Maintain turning strength without substituting side bending. Use both hands and softly bent elbows. Turn feet/hips with a modest side-to-side arc; keep ribs over pelvis. One one-way traverse is one rep and the reverse is the next rep; six alternating traverses contain three per direction. Take about 2 seconds per traverse and settle briefly at the endpoint. Reduce arc/load if the knee twists, trunk leans or endpoint runs away.

Turn feet/hips/trunk modestly while drawing the elbow toward the same-side lower ribs; return in 3 seconds. Keep the shoulder down and trunk long. Reduce band tension/turn range if the shoulder hikes or the athlete yanks from the low back.

Use less load for rib flare or elbow/wrist collapse; if minimum bar load is unsuitable, use a rotational band press instead at this dose.
