rotation-upper.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1, unchanged. Content, duration and overlapping loading are unavailable; do not recreate it or assign it a time. Review its actual demands before delivery.
rotation-upper.explosiveNotes: Exactly six exercises. E1 exactly repeats Class 1’s 2 × 3 per side, including 90-second between-side/set recovery. E2 is only 1 × 2 per side; the other reference/support doses are modest. No extra test attempts, catch circuits or maximum-load tests. Use light implements and fast coordinated intent; a retained-load drill ends under control rather than being released. Both sides receive the written dose.

rotation-lower.title: Class 1
rotation-lower.effort: Produce a quick support-foot pivot and pelvic turn into a low roundhouse kick, then recover the leg and stance under control. Framework: Rotational explosiveness > Lower-body emphasis (rotational kicks).
rotation-lower.delivery: Allow approximately 83–90 minutes for this prescribed work, including the modeled rests, stated load-preparation sets, demonstrations, equipment adjustment and recording, with prompt equipment access. Access & Prepare 1, extra ramps, longer recovery and group queues are additional. The full session duration is unresolved. A 60-minute total booking cannot fit this version; a 90-minute total booking is not established as feasible. Use a confirmed cleared section within a 10 m lane, with separate waiting space outside the sweep/landing area. Lane widths, bench fit, band loops, class size and staffing must be checked; one lane being long enough does not establish group capacity. See the delivery audit.

exercises.name: Split-stance explosive hip pivot — grounded, proposed exercise
exercises.sourceName: Split-stance explosive hip pivot — grounded, proposed exercise
exercises.dose: 1 × 2 per direction = 4 attempts. Start in a short split stance; rapidly shift toward the lead leg and turn feet and pelvis together through a comfortable approximately 45° arc. Heels may release; both forefeet remain grounded. No kick or jump. Finish still for 2 s. Rest 20 s between attempts, then 60 s before E2.
exercises.description: Isolate the support-foot release and hip-turn initiation before adding a swinging leg. Mirror the stance for the opposite direction. Keep knees soft and following toes; reduce turn size if a foot sticks, knee twists or trunk leads the turn. Stop if the surface will not permit controlled pivoting.

From the same short fighting stance with the kicking leg initially at the rear, turn the support foot with the pelvis, lift and sweep the bent thigh, then extend only through a controllable low arc, recoil and return to the starting stance; hold 2 s. Foot stays below hip height. Rest 20 s between the two reps, 60 s between legs, 90 s between rounds, and 90 s after the final round.

No target, impact, partner contact, head-height kick, jump or spinning kick. Use a shorter arc and less terminal extension instead if recoil or balance is lost. Never snap an unsupported knee into lockout.

rotation-lower.title: Class 4
rotation-lower.effort: Sweep the free leg quickly through a low rotational kick and arrest it in a controlled re-chamber before putting it down. Exact framework: Rotational explosiveness > Lower-body emphasis (rotational kicks).
rotation-lower.delivery: Approximately 75–82 minutes outside Access & Prepare 1, with prompt equipment access. The audit models actual prescribed resets, rests, both sides, preparation sets and 13 minutes for instruction/setup/recording. Group queues, extra coaching, ramps and longer recovery are additional. Full session duration is unresolved; do not assume a 60- or 90-minute total booking fits. Keep vertical jumps in a cleared footprint, hops within 0.5 m and kick sweeps below hip height with clear space all around; retain at least 2 m recovery clearance in the 10 m lane. Confirm lane width, swept-leg clearance, waiting/return areas, bench fit, secure band loops and staffing. Run each athlete's four sections in order; equipment rotation is not permission to do strength before explosiveness. No throwing wall, pad, cable machine, external band anchor, rack or device capability is presumed.

rotation-lower.title: Class 9
rotation-lower.effort: Create a small amount of separation, produce a low rotational counter-kick and recover without uncontrolled spin or drift. Exact framework: Rotational explosiveness > Lower-body emphasis (rotational kicks).
rotation-lower.delivery: Approximately 75–82 minutes outside Access & Prepare 1, with prompt equipment access. The audit models actual prescribed resets, rests, both sides, preparation sets and 13 minutes for instruction/setup/recording. Group queues, extra coaching, ramps and longer recovery are additional. Full session duration is unresolved; do not assume a 60- or 90-minute total booking fits. Retreat/drop-step sequences fit within 2 m plus 2 m recovery clearance in a 10 m lane; backward flight is at most 0.5 m. Confirm width for the lateral returns and keep all queues away from behind the athlete. Confirm lane width, swept-leg clearance, waiting/return areas, bench fit, secure band loops and staffing. Run each athlete's four sections in order; equipment rotation is not permission to do strength before explosiveness. No throwing wall, pad, cable machine, external band anchor, rack or device capability is presumed.

rotation-lower.delivery: Approximately 85–92 minutes outside Access & Prepare 1, with prompt equipment access. The audit models actual prescribed resets, rests, both sides, preparation sets and 13 minutes for instruction/setup/recording. Group queues, extra coaching, ramps and longer recovery are additional. Full session duration is unresolved; do not assume a 60- or 90-minute total booking fits. Cones are visual identifiers outside the landing/sweep area, not obstacles. Entries/bounds stay within 1–2 m plus 2 m clear recovery inside a 10 m lane. One active cued athlete at a time unless staffing and separation are actually verified. Confirm lane width, swept-leg clearance, waiting/return areas, bench fit, secure band loops and staffing. Run each athlete's four sections in order; equipment rotation is not permission to do strength before explosiveness. No throwing wall, pad, cable machine, external band anchor, rack or device capability is presumed.

rotation-lower.title: Class 12
rotation-lower.effort: Reproduce the original stationary rotational-kick conditions, then sample short entry and recovery applications without maximal testing. Exact framework: Rotational explosiveness > Lower-body emphasis (rotational kicks).
rotation-lower.delivery: Approximately 75–82 minutes outside Access & Prepare 1, with prompt equipment access. The audit models actual prescribed resets, rests, both sides, preparation sets and 13 minutes for instruction/setup/recording. Group queues, extra coaching, ramps and longer recovery are additional. Full session duration is unresolved; do not assume a 60- or 90-minute total booking fits. The first three drills use their original cleared setup where available. Application entries stay within 2 m plus 2 m clear recovery in a 10 m lane, with the original visual kick line unobstructed and all cones outside the sweep. Confirm lane width, swept-leg clearance, waiting/return areas, bench fit, secure band loops and staffing. Run each athlete's four sections in order; equipment rotation is not permission to do strength before explosiveness. No throwing wall, pad, cable machine, external band anchor, rack or device capability is presumed.

A loop around the lower shins resists the working foot moving outward, lightly clear of the floor, while that knee stays in place; the other foot is firmly planted. 2 s outward rotation, 2 s controlled return. Rest 60 s between sides, then 60 s.
exercises.description: Retain the direct hip-torque strength anchor at its established technical range. Use modest rotation, enough resistance for 2–3 clean RIR, and a quiet knee/pelvis. If a secure loop cannot be fitted, use instead self-resisted seated hip internal rotation: opposite hand resisting the outside of the lower shin, same reps/tempo. Log manual resistance as less reproducible.

exercises.dose: 1 × 3 jumps. Controlled submaximal height; 20 s between jumps; 60 s before E2.
exercises.description: Establish the terminal braking pattern before asking for rebounds. Use a smooth dip and arm swing, jump vertically, then let ankles, knees and hips yield together and hold 2 s. Keep pressure centered over both feet. Reduce height if the landing needs a step or the trunk folds; stop if control is not restored.

Allow necessary joint flexion; do not lock the knees or force pogo mechanics onto a larger jump. Lower amplitude if a second dip, collapse or drift develops.

jumps-max-air.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1 sequence. It is supplied separately and is not created or modified here. Its exact content and duration have not been established for this curriculum. The coach must account for any jumps, loaded work or fatigue already present in it. All totals and time estimates below exclude that sequence.

jumps-max-air.title: Control & project · Stage 3A

exercises.description: Accelerate a small external load upward through coordinated knee/hip extension and heel rise. Begin tall, dumbbells beside the thighs, arms long; make a shallow dip/hinge to high-thigh level, then drive tall quickly onto the forefeet. Allow a natural shoulder rise, keep elbows long and weights close; no deliberate high elbow pull, rack catch, jump or backward lean. Lower under control over about 2 s, heels down, reset. Choose a load permitting crisp leg-driven motion; first three reps establish technique conservatively. Reduce load/intent or stop for arm hauling, lost trunk position or uncontrolled lowering.

exercises.sourceName: Dumbbell Push Press — bilateral, no flight — proposed addition
exercises.dose: 2 × 3 = 6 rapid presses with light dumbbells. 5 s after controlled lowering/reset between reps; 90 s between sets and before E6.
exercises.description: Transfer a brief vertical leg drive through an organized trunk to an upward arm finish. Begin with bells securely at the shoulders. jumps-max-air.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1 sequence. It is supplied separately and is not created or modified here. Its exact content and duration have not been established for this curriculum. The coach must account for any jumps, loaded work or fatigue already present in it. All totals and time estimates below exclude that sequence.
jumps-max-air.explosiveNotes: Six explosive exercises are integrated in alternating order: two force-absorption and rebound selections, two vertical-jump selections, and two horizontal-jump selections. Preserve each exercise’s written quality and recovery rules.

jumps-max-air.title: Rebound & redirect · Stage 10B

jumps-max-air.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1 sequence. It is supplied separately and is not created or modified here. Its exact content and duration have not been established for this curriculum. The coach must account for any jumps, loaded work or fatigue already present in it. All totals and time estimates below exclude that sequence.
jumps-max-air.explosiveNotes: Six explosive exercises are integrated in alternating order: two force-absorption and rebound selections, two vertical-jump selections, and two horizontal-jump selections. Preserve each exercise’s written quality and recovery rules.

jumps-max-air.title: Control & project · Stage 12A
jumps-max-air.effort: Integrate force absorption, vertical projection, and horizontal projection using the existing Stage 12 prescriptions. Each output and strength phase draws from all three jump tracks.
jumps-max-air.delivery: Preserve every listed dose and recovery period. Confirm total delivery time, equipment flow, and athlete readiness for this integrated class before coaching it.

exercises.description: Establish the terminal braking pattern before asking for rebounds. Use a smooth dip and arm swing, jump vertically, then let ankles, knees and hips yield together and hold 2 s. Keep pressure centered over both feet. Reduce height if the landing needs a step or the trunk folds; stop if control is not restored.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump — natural arm swing, stick landing — deliberately recurring
exercises.sourceName: Countermovement Jump — natural arm swing, stick landing — deliberately recurring
exercises.dose: 3 × 2 = 6 jumps. Set 1: two controlled execution checks; sets 2–3: up to four candidate jumps with maximum-height intent only while control/readiness permit. 30 s after landing/reset between reps; 120 s between sets and before E2.
exercises.description: Main performance task: coordinate a natural dip and arm swing into direct upward propulsion. Start stationary with the same comfortable stance, use one self-selected dip, jump upward and hold the bilateral landing 2 s. No approach, pre-hop, pause in the squat, loaded implement or rebound. Keep the declared cue/arm/stance protocol stable in sets 2–3. Reduce intent or stop for uncontrolled drift/landing; record modified work without treating it as comparable maximal output.

Two integrated sequences = six landings: four unilateral and two bilateral. No running approach; not three bilateral broad jumps.
exercises.description: Integrate same-leg reuse, opposite-leg transfer and a bilateral final reception into one defined horizontal foot sequence. From one foot, hop to the same foot, step-bound to the opposite foot, then jump from that foot to both feet; hold the final landing. Start the other set on the opposite leg. Regress/stop: Shorten each segment and slow entry intent while keeping the sequence; stop for a collapsing intermediate contact or incorrect foot order.

exercises.description: Produce upward force from a still asymmetric base and organize it into a square landing. Bring feet parallel without twisting or chasing height. The pause differs from Class 5's active-dip staggered jump; the parallel finish differs from Class 10's same-lead paused split jump. Reduce stagger/intent or replace for a re-dip, twist or unstable finish.

speed-agility.title: Push, brake & respond · Stage 1A
speed-agility.effort: Projection and controlled reversal. Connect the sprint push to a controlled planned stop or exit, then use that control to respond to a live opponent.
speed-agility.delivery: One integrated class per week. Complete Access & Prepare 1, then six explosive drills, two light resilience exercises and six primary-strength exercises. Keep each selected exercise’s dose, recovery, preparation sets and setup conditions from its source class. Confirm the combined timing and equipment flow; preserve full recovery between tasks and extend it if movement quality has not returned. Source labels identify the original exercise numbers, which may differ from today’s order.

Repeat the original doses only when readiness supports them; the class number does not authorize added volume or speed.

speed-agility.quality: Within the scheduled efforts, observe the sprint anchor’s projection or upright coordination, the planned task’s braking and exit control, and the reactive anchor’s correct read and controlled response. Projection and controlled reversal. Record execution and recovery; do not add test attempts or infer gains from unlike drills.
speed-agility.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1, supplied separately. Its content, duration and workload are unknown here. Reference it unchanged; do not create a replacement sequence. The coach must establish readiness for the listed efforts from the athlete's actual preparation and condition.
speed-agility.explosiveNotes: Two drills from each course share one purpose: produce speed, control direction, then respond to a live cue. The sprint and live-decision anchors recur across the stage’s three classes while the supporting drills vary. Each class includes a genuine reactive task; a drill’s course label alone does not make it reactive. Repeat the original doses only when readiness supports them; the class number does not authorize added volume or speed.

speed-agility.title: Coordinate, read & reaccelerate · Stage 1C
speed-agility.effort: Projection and controlled reversal. Connect running coordination to a purposeful planned exit, then choose or adapt the next action from a live cue.
speed-agility.delivery: One integrated class per week. Complete Access & Prepare 1, then six explosive drills, two light resilience exercises and six primary-strength exercises. Keep each selected exercise’s dose, recovery, preparation sets and setup conditions from its source class. Confirm the combined timing and equipment flow; preserve full recovery between tasks and extend it if movement quality has not returned. Source labels identify the original exercise numbers, which may differ from today’s order.

Keep hips down; no sudden pushes. Match resistance to 2–3 RIR, not a contest. If prone support/contact is unsuitable, use Seated Band Hamstring Curl instead, same sets/reps per side: sit on a stable bench, secure a light band at the heel with a coach holding steady forward tension, then pull the heel beneath the bench without moving the thigh. Qualify band/bench fit; no sudden release. This replaces only this slot and preserves totals. Rest 60 s between sides; 60 s before the next exercise.

speed-agility.title: Coordinate, read & reaccelerate · Stage 2C
speed-agility.effort: Low starts and lateral exits. Connect running coordination to a purposeful planned exit, then choose or adapt the next action from a live cue.

exercises.description: Main low-start task: create forward motion from a flexed lead hip/knee while bringing the rear thigh through. Front foot flat, rear knee comfortably supported on the floor and rear toes tucked; establish a modest forward torso lean without rounding, pause briefly, then push into the lane. Both legs may contribute; this is not a test of isolated lead-leg force. First pair uses controlled fast intent to establish the route; second pair uses the fastest clean intent that preserves stopping control.

speed-agility.title: Push, brake & respond · Stage 4A
speed-agility.effort: Upright support and angled responses. Connect the sprint push to a controlled planned stop or exit, then use that control to respond to a live opponent.
speed-agility.delivery: One integrated class per week. Complete Access & Prepare 1, then six explosive drills, two light resilience exercises and six primary-strength exercises. Keep each selected exercise’s dose, recovery, preparation sets and setup conditions from its source class. Confirm the combined timing and equipment flow; preserve full recovery between tasks and extend it if movement quality has not returned. Source labels identify the original exercise numbers, which may differ from today’s order.

exercises.name: Stationary A-Run — alternating high-knee exchanges
exercises.dose: 2 × 6 alternating foot contacts, 3/foot/set; 90 s between sets. Bodyweight; quick rhythm without chasing cadence. Start the sets on opposite support legs.
exercises.description: Main task: alternate a bent-knee thigh recovery and rapid support exchange while staying tall. Begin on one foot with the other knee comfortably raised; make small airborne exchanges, landing the incoming foot close to its normal standing position as the opposite thigh lifts. No extra bounce between exchanges, forced hip-height target, backward lean or deliberate clawing. Finish on contact six, stabilize, then set the other foot down. Reduce knee height/cadence for drift, reaching or loss of posture.

exercises.dose: 1 × 3 per moving leg; bodyweight. Quick floor tap/return, 1 s balanced finish; 10 s reset between reps, 45 s between legs.

exercises.name: Stationary A-Run — alternating high-knee exchanges
exercises.dose: 2 × 6 alternating foot contacts, 3/foot/set; 90 s between sets. Bodyweight; quick rhythm without chasing cadence. Start the sets on opposite support legs.
exercises.description: Main task: alternate a bent-knee thigh recovery and rapid support exchange while staying tall. Begin on one foot with the other knee comfortably raised; make small airborne exchanges, landing the incoming foot close to its normal standing position as the opposite thigh lifts. No extra bounce between exchanges, forced hip-height target, backward lean or deliberate clawing. Finish on contact six, stabilize, then set the other foot down. Reduce knee height/cadence for drift, reaching or loss of posture.

exercises.description: Practice quick opposing arm action while the torso stays organized, without adding another ankle-impact task. exercises.name: Stationary Single-Leg High-Knee Run
exercises.dose: 1 × 3 cycles per target leg; 90 s between target legs. One cycle = target-foot running contact plus opposite-foot running contact: 12 total contacts, 6/foot.
exercises.description: Main task: repeatedly recover one thigh while the other leg uses a low, compact running step. Begin supported on the opposite leg with target thigh comfortably raised. Exchange onto the target foot, then onto the opposite foot as the target heel folds beneath the hip and its thigh rises again. Repeat this asymmetric rhythm without a full cycle on the low-step leg. Use small flight, natural arms and nearby foot contacts; do not hop twice on one foot. Finish the third cycle under control. Lower knee height/speed for long backswing, drift, reaching or backward lean.

exercises.name: Stationary Single-Leg High-Knee Run
exercises.dose: 1 × 3 cycles per target leg; 90 s between target legs. One cycle = target-foot running contact plus opposite-foot running contact: 12 total contacts, 6/foot.
exercises.description: Main task: repeatedly recover one thigh while the other leg uses a low, compact running step. Begin supported on the opposite leg with target thigh comfortably raised. Exchange onto the target foot, then onto the opposite foot as the target heel folds beneath the hip and its thigh rises again. Repeat this asymmetric rhythm without a full cycle on the low-step leg. Use small flight, natural arms and nearby foot contacts; do not hop twice on one foot. Finish the third cycle under control. Lower knee height/speed for long backswing, drift, reaching or backward lean.

speed-agility.title: Push, brake & respond · Stage 6A
speed-agility.effort: Reversal, closing space and exit denial. Connect the sprint push to a controlled planned stop or exit, then use that control to respond to a live opponent.
speed-agility.delivery: One integrated class per week. Complete Access & Prepare 1, then six explosive drills, two light resilience exercises and six primary-strength exercises. Keep each selected exercise’s dose, recovery, preparation sets and setup conditions from its source class. Confirm the combined timing and equipment flow; preserve full recovery between tasks and extend it if movement quality has not returned. Source labels identify the original exercise numbers, which may differ from today’s order.

exercises.name: Falling Start — first two steps
exercises.dose: 2 × 2 starts, one with each first stepping foot per pair. Front toes at 1 m; fit the entire starting body inside 0–2 m. At most 2 driving strikes or 3 m of drive, ending by 4 m; progressively slow and stop by 9 m. 75 s between starts; 120 s between pairs.
exercises.description: Main task: turn a controlled forward whole-body lean into the first supporting push and next step. Start with feet parallel near hip width, arms relaxed; let the body tip forward from the ankles without folding at the waist. Initiate the selected stepping foot early enough to stay in control; do not wait for a near-fall or chase a maximum lean. First pair is controlled fast to establish stopping; second pair uses the fastest clean intent that preserves it. No jump into the start.

First pair is controlled-fast to establish stopping; use faster intent in the second only while control remains.

speed-agility.quality: Within the scheduled efforts, observe the sprint anchor’s projection or upright coordination, the planned task’s braking and exit control, and the reactive anchor’s correct read and controlled response. Integrated movement and adaptable decisions. Record execution and recovery; do not add test attempts or infer gains from unlike drills.
speed-agility.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1, unchanged and supplied separately. Its content, duration and workload remain unknown here. Use actual preparation/readiness to qualify today's tasks; no replacement sequence is created.
speed-agility.explosiveNotes: Two drills from each course share one purpose: produce speed, control direction, then respond to a live cue. The sprint and live-decision anchors recur across the stage’s three classes while the supporting drills vary. Each class includes a genuine reactive task; a drill’s course label alone does not make it reactive. Repeat the original doses only when readiness supports them; the class number does not authorize added volume or speed.

rotation-full-body.title: Full body · Pivot and project
rotation-full-body.effort: Foot release, hip initiation and a balanced finish. Pivot → scoop; Kick → pushing release; Support the moving limb.
rotation-full-body.extension: Establish the stage’s support and force-transfer connections using both source courses inside this class. Keep the original working doses; qualify the listed range and load before seeking more speed.

connections.title: Pivot → scoop
connections.cue: Let the support foot release with the hip turn in the grounded pivot, then retain that foot-led sequence when the hands project the ball.

connections.title: Kick → pushing release
connections.cue: Use the same freely turning support base to accelerate the thigh or the throwing hand; recover balance before resetting either task.

connections.title: Support the moving limb

rotation-full-body.delivery: Plan one integrated class per week. Complete Access & Prepare 1 → six explosive exercises → two light resilience exercises → six primary-strength exercises. In each explosive pair, complete the lower-body exercise with its prescribed recovery, clear/reset the space, then complete the connected upper-body exercise. Each exercise has its own sets and rest; this is not a superset, continuous kick/throw combination or fatigue circuit. Preserve both-side doses and the longer of the row recovery and the source class’s between-exercise recovery. Allow 10–15 s between upper-body attempts, normally 20 s between lower-body attempts and 60 s for the early-cue lower-body tasks. Extend recovery when quality requires. Primary easy loading sets are separate from working reps. Confirm combined class duration from the selected doses, rest, preparation and actual group flow; original whole-course class durations cannot simply be added or reused. Review other sport/gym/tumbling work and the source roughly 48–72 h planning allowance from comparable demanding exposures. Resume missed classes in sequence instead of doubling up.
rotation-full-body.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1 unchanged; do not recreate it or assign an assumed duration. Review its actual demands before this full-body class. Check the written setup and readiness of the selected kick, landing, handoff and implement tasks.
rotation-full-body.setup: Use the existing separate 10 m lanes. Keep waiting athletes outside the swept-leg, landing and ball paths. For released balls, verify a light grippable implement, permitted low floor target about 2–3 m beyond release, and containment of the entire flight/rebound/roll; use a throwing wall only after verification. Use a non-rebounding slam ball for slams. Clear the area between the leg drill and hand drill of each pair. Pairing is a coaching connection, not simultaneous stations or a throw immediately after a jump. Secure band/rope anchors and the landmine base. Kicks stay below hip height with a soft terminal knee, active recoil and no contact or spinning kick. Handoffs are controlled: secure the grip and wait for the feeder to release and step clear before turning. No new airborne-feed progression is added.
rotation-full-body.quality: Within the scheduled attempts, record each side’s support-foot release, hip-led initiation and controlled finish. Use today’s three connections to identify whether a miss begins at support, transfer or endpoint. Different drills are not equivalent force tests; use observed control and recovery to choose the next appropriate demand.

rotation-full-body.explosiveNotes: E1/E2 Pivot → scoop: Let the support foot release with the hip turn in the grounded pivot, then retain that foot-led sequence when the hands project the ball. E3/E4 Kick → pushing release: Use the same freely turning support base to accelerate the thigh or the throwing hand; recover balance before resetting either task. rotation-full-body.progression: Establish the stage’s support and force-transfer connections using both source courses inside this class. Keep the original working doses; qualify the listed range and load before seeking more speed. Review actual attendance, technique, loads, soreness and other training. Change one demand only after clean execution at the intended reserve and acceptable recovery; otherwise hold or regress. Each bridge connects two separately coached exercises. Complete all prescribed work and recovery for the first, then clear/reset the area for the second. Never combine a jump or kick with a simultaneous throw. Use the source’s shorter-range, supported, stationary or paused replacement inside the same slot. For handoffs, secure grip and wait for the feeder to step clear; use the existing self-held replacement when needed.
S: One upper-body/trunk and one hip/foot resilience exercise connect control at both ends of the rotational chain. Keep at least 4–5 clean repetitions or about 5 seconds of a sound hold in reserve. Preserve the row’s within-hold relaxation and use the stated side/exercise recovery.
P: Three lower-body and three upper-body/trunk lifts support the class’s force-transfer purpose. Across the first two classes of each stage, every original primary-strength prescription is included once; the additional day selects complementary full-body strength. Perform the listed easy preparation for each lift, with its recovery, before working. Keep 2–3 clean reps in reserve and the source controlled return tempo.

rotation-full-body.delivery: Plan one integrated class per week. Complete Access & Prepare 1 → six explosive exercises → two light resilience exercises → six primary-strength exercises. In each explosive pair, complete the lower-body exercise with its prescribed recovery, clear/reset the space, then complete the connected upper-body exercise. Each exercise has its own sets and rest; this is not a superset, continuous kick/throw combination or fatigue circuit. Preserve both-side doses and the longer of the row recovery and the source class’s between-exercise recovery. Allow 10–15 s between upper-body attempts, normally 20 s between lower-body attempts and 60 s for the early-cue lower-body tasks. Extend recovery when quality requires. Primary easy loading sets are separate from working reps. Confirm combined class duration from the selected doses, rest, preparation and actual group flow; original whole-course class durations cannot simply be added or reused. Review other sport/gym/tumbling work and the source roughly 48–72 h planning allowance from comparable demanding exposures. Resume missed classes in sequence instead of doubling up.
rotation-full-body.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1 unchanged; do not recreate it or assign an assumed duration. Review its actual demands before this full-body class. Check the written setup and readiness of the selected kick, landing, handoff and implement tasks.
rotation-full-body.setup: Use the existing separate 10 m lanes. Keep waiting athletes outside the swept-leg, landing and ball paths. For released balls, verify a light grippable implement, permitted low floor target about 2–3 m beyond release, and containment of the entire flight/rebound/roll; use a throwing wall only after verification. Use a non-rebounding slam ball for slams. Clear the area between the leg drill and hand drill of each pair. Pairing is a coaching connection, not simultaneous stations or a throw immediately after a jump. Secure band/rope anchors and the landmine base. Kicks stay below hip height with a soft terminal knee, active recoil and no contact or spinning kick. Handoffs are controlled: secure the grip and wait for the feeder to release and step clear before turning. No new airborne-feed progression is added.
rotation-full-body.quality: Within the scheduled attempts, record each side’s support-foot release, hip-led initiation and controlled finish. Use today’s three connections to identify whether a miss begins at support, transfer or endpoint. Different drills are not equivalent force tests; use observed control and recovery to choose the next appropriate demand.

rotation-full-body.explosiveNotes: E1/E2 Load → rotational output: Compare the single dip of the turning jump with the single compact preload of the ball throw; each load flows into one action. E3/E4 Absorb → diagonal force: Own the rotational bound landing, then use a settled base to direct the side slam. The landing and slam are separate efforts with full recovery. E5/E6 Entry → usable plant: Match the lateral entry and step-behind throw by uncrossing and settling the support foot before the pelvis and hands turn.
rotation-full-body.progression: Expand the stage to its complementary entry, direction or control demands. Transfer the support-and-finish standards from the preceding integrated class; new task demands do not authorize heavier loads. Review actual attendance, technique, loads, soreness and other training. Change one demand only after clean execution at the intended reserve and acceptable recovery; otherwise hold or regress. No athlete completion, readiness or improvement is inferred from a class number.

E: Expand the stage to its complementary entry, direction or control demands. Transfer the support-and-finish standards from the preceding integrated class; new task demands do not authorize heavier loads.

Each bridge connects two separately coached exercises. Complete all prescribed work and recovery for the first, then clear/reset the area for the second. Never combine a jump or kick with a simultaneous throw. Use the source’s shorter-range, supported, stationary or paused replacement inside the same slot. For handoffs, secure grip and wait for the feeder to step clear; use the existing self-held replacement when needed.
S: One upper-body/trunk and one hip/foot resilience exercise connect control at both ends of the rotational chain. Keep at least 4–5 clean repetitions or about 5 seconds of a sound hold in reserve. Preserve the row’s within-hold relaxation and use the stated side/exercise recovery.
P: Three lower-body and three upper-body/trunk lifts support the class’s force-transfer purpose. Across the first two classes of each stage, every original primary-strength prescription is included once; the additional day selects complementary full-body strength. Perform the listed easy preparation for each lift, with its recovery, before working. Keep 2–3 clean reps in reserve and the source controlled return tempo.

rotation-full-body.delivery: Plan one integrated class per week. Complete Access & Prepare 1 → six explosive exercises → two light resilience exercises → six primary-strength exercises. In each explosive pair, complete the lower-body exercise with its prescribed recovery, clear/reset the space, then complete the connected upper-body exercise. Each exercise has its own sets and rest; this is not a superset, continuous kick/throw combination or fatigue circuit. Preserve both-side doses and the longer of the row recovery and the source class’s between-exercise recovery. Allow 10–15 s between upper-body attempts, normally 20 s between lower-body attempts and 60 s for the early-cue lower-body tasks. Extend recovery when quality requires. Primary easy loading sets are separate from working reps. Confirm combined class duration from the selected doses, rest, preparation and actual group flow; original whole-course class durations cannot simply be added or reused. Review other sport/gym/tumbling work and the source roughly 48–72 h planning allowance from comparable demanding exposures. Resume missed classes in sequence instead of doubling up.
rotation-full-body.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1 unchanged; do not recreate it or assign an assumed duration. Review its actual demands before this full-body class. Check the written setup and readiness of the selected kick, landing, handoff and implement tasks.
rotation-full-body.setup: Use the existing separate 10 m lanes. Keep waiting athletes outside the swept-leg, landing and ball paths. For released balls, verify a light grippable implement, permitted low floor target about 2–3 m beyond release, and containment of the entire flight/rebound/roll; use a throwing wall only after verification. Use a non-rebounding slam ball for slams. Clear the area between the leg drill and hand drill of each pair. Pairing is a coaching connection, not simultaneous stations or a throw immediately after a jump. Secure band/rope anchors and the landmine base. Kicks stay below hip height with a soft terminal knee, active recoil and no contact or spinning kick. Handoffs are controlled: secure the grip and wait for the feeder to release and step clear before turning. No new airborne-feed progression is added.
rotation-full-body.quality: Within the scheduled attempts, record each side’s support-foot release, hip-led initiation and controlled finish. Use today’s three connections to identify whether a miss begins at support, transfer or endpoint. Apply one shared cue—foot, hip, finish—to the pivot/scoop and kick/shot-put pairs. Then compare turning-jump landing control with the constrained-base throw. Record these six drills in this order as the Week 36 reference; add no test attempts.

rotation-full-body.progression: Apply one shared cue—foot, hip, finish—to the pivot/scoop and kick/shot-put pairs. Then compare turning-jump landing control with the constrained-base throw. rotation-full-body.delivery: Plan one integrated class per week. Complete Access & Prepare 1 → six explosive exercises → two light resilience exercises → six primary-strength exercises. In each explosive pair, complete the lower-body exercise with its prescribed recovery, clear/reset the space, then complete the connected upper-body exercise. Each exercise has its own sets and rest; this is not a superset, continuous kick/throw combination or fatigue circuit. Preserve both-side doses and the longer of the row recovery and the source class’s between-exercise recovery. Allow 10–15 s between upper-body attempts, normally 20 s between lower-body attempts and 60 s for the early-cue lower-body tasks. Extend recovery when quality requires. Primary easy loading sets are separate from working reps. Confirm combined class duration from the selected doses, rest, preparation and actual group flow; original whole-course class durations cannot simply be added or reused. Review other sport/gym/tumbling work and the source roughly 48–72 h planning allowance from comparable demanding exposures. Resume missed classes in sequence instead of doubling up.
rotation-full-body.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1 unchanged; do not recreate it or assign an assumed duration. Review its actual demands before this full-body class. Check the written setup and readiness of the selected kick, landing, handoff and implement tasks.
rotation-full-body.setup: Use the existing separate 10 m lanes. Keep waiting athletes outside the swept-leg, landing and ball paths. For released balls, verify a light grippable implement, permitted low floor target about 2–3 m beyond release, and containment of the entire flight/rebound/roll; use a throwing wall only after verification. Use a non-rebounding slam ball for slams. Clear the area between the leg drill and hand drill of each pair. Pairing is a coaching connection, not simultaneous stations or a throw immediately after a jump. Secure band/rope anchors and the landmine base. Kicks stay below hip height with a soft terminal knee, active recoil and no contact or spinning kick. Handoffs are controlled: secure the grip and wait for the feeder to release and step clear before turning. No new airborne-feed progression is added.
rotation-full-body.quality: Within the scheduled attempts, record each side’s support-foot release, hip-led initiation and controlled finish. Use today’s three connections to identify whether a miss begins at support, transfer or endpoint. Different drills are not equivalent force tests; use observed control and recovery to choose the next appropriate demand.

Use the existing short-lever options to distinguish poor support transfer from excessive limb reach; keep the original doses. Review actual attendance, technique, loads, soreness and other training. Change one demand only after clean execution at the intended reserve and acceptable recovery; otherwise hold or regress. No athlete completion, readiness or improvement is inferred from a class number.

Each bridge connects two separately coached exercises. Complete all prescribed work and recovery for the first, then clear/reset the area for the second. Never combine a jump or kick with a simultaneous throw. Use the source’s shorter-range, supported, stationary or paused replacement inside the same slot. For handoffs, secure grip and wait for the feeder to step clear; use the existing self-held replacement when needed.
S: One upper-body/trunk and one hip/foot resilience exercise connect control at both ends of the rotational chain. Keep at least 4–5 clean repetitions or about 5 seconds of a sound hold in reserve. Preserve the row’s within-hold relaxation and use the stated side/exercise recovery.
P: Three lower-body and three upper-body/trunk lifts support the class’s force-transfer purpose. Across the first two classes of each stage, every original primary-strength prescription is included once; the additional day selects complementary full-body strength. Perform the listed easy preparation for each lift, with its recovery, before working. Keep 2–3 clean reps in reserve and the source controlled return tempo.

rotation-full-body.delivery: Plan one integrated class per week. Complete Access & Prepare 1 → six explosive exercises → two light resilience exercises → six primary-strength exercises. In each explosive pair, complete the lower-body exercise with its prescribed recovery, clear/reset the space, then complete the connected upper-body exercise. Each exercise has its own sets and rest; this is not a superset, continuous kick/throw combination or fatigue circuit. Preserve both-side doses and the longer of the row recovery and the source class’s between-exercise recovery. Allow 10–15 s between upper-body attempts, normally 20 s between lower-body attempts and 60 s for the early-cue lower-body tasks. Extend recovery when quality requires. Primary easy loading sets are separate from working reps. Confirm combined class duration from the selected doses, rest, preparation and actual group flow; original whole-course class durations cannot simply be added or reused. Review other sport/gym/tumbling work and the source roughly 48–72 h planning allowance from comparable demanding exposures. Resume missed classes in sequence instead of doubling up.
rotation-full-body.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1 unchanged; do not recreate it or assign an assumed duration. Review its actual demands before this full-body class. Check the written setup and readiness of the selected kick, landing, handoff and implement tasks.
rotation-full-body.setup: Use the existing separate 10 m lanes. Keep waiting athletes outside the swept-leg, landing and ball paths. For released balls, verify a light grippable implement, permitted low floor target about 2–3 m beyond release, and containment of the entire flight/rebound/roll; use a throwing wall only after verification. Use a non-rebounding slam ball for slams. Clear the area between the leg drill and hand drill of each pair. Pairing is a coaching connection, not simultaneous stations or a throw immediately after a jump. Secure band/rope anchors and the landmine base. Kicks stay below hip height with a soft terminal knee, active recoil and no contact or spinning kick. Handoffs are controlled: secure the grip and wait for the feeder to release and step clear before turning. No new airborne-feed progression is added.
rotation-full-body.quality: Within the scheduled attempts, record each side’s support-foot release, hip-led initiation and controlled finish. Use today’s three connections to identify whether a miss begins at support, transfer or endpoint. Different drills are not equivalent force tests; use observed control and recovery to choose the next appropriate demand.

rotation-full-body.progression: Establish the stage’s support and force-transfer connections using both source courses inside this class. Keep the original working doses; qualify the listed range and load before seeking more speed. Review actual attendance, technique, loads, soreness and other training. Change one demand only after clean execution at the intended reserve and acceptable recovery; otherwise hold or regress. Each bridge connects two separately coached exercises. Complete all prescribed work and recovery for the first, then clear/reset the area for the second. Never combine a jump or kick with a simultaneous throw. Use the source’s shorter-range, supported, stationary or paused replacement inside the same slot. For handoffs, secure grip and wait for the feeder to step clear; use the existing self-held replacement when needed.
S: One upper-body/trunk and one hip/foot resilience exercise connect control at both ends of the rotational chain. Keep at least 4–5 clean repetitions or about 5 seconds of a sound hold in reserve. Preserve the row’s within-hold relaxation and use the stated side/exercise recovery.
P: Three lower-body and three upper-body/trunk lifts support the class’s force-transfer purpose. Across the first two classes of each stage, every original primary-strength prescription is included once; the additional day selects complementary full-body strength. Perform the listed easy preparation for each lift, with its recovery, before working. Keep 2–3 clean reps in reserve and the source controlled return tempo.

rotation-full-body.delivery: Plan one integrated class per week. Complete Access & Prepare 1 → six explosive exercises → two light resilience exercises → six primary-strength exercises. In each explosive pair, complete the lower-body exercise with its prescribed recovery, clear/reset the space, then complete the connected upper-body exercise. Each exercise has its own sets and rest; this is not a superset, continuous kick/throw combination or fatigue circuit. Preserve both-side doses and the longer of the row recovery and the source class’s between-exercise recovery. Allow 10–15 s between upper-body attempts, normally 20 s between lower-body attempts and 60 s for the early-cue lower-body tasks. Extend recovery when quality requires. Primary easy loading sets are separate from working reps. Confirm combined class duration from the selected doses, rest, preparation and actual group flow; original whole-course class durations cannot simply be added or reused. Review other sport/gym/tumbling work and the source roughly 48–72 h planning allowance from comparable demanding exposures. Resume missed classes in sequence instead of doubling up.
rotation-full-body.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1 unchanged; do not recreate it or assign an assumed duration. Review its actual demands before this full-body class. Check the written setup and readiness of the selected kick, landing, handoff and implement tasks.
rotation-full-body.setup: Use the existing separate 10 m lanes. Keep waiting athletes outside the swept-leg, landing and ball paths. For released balls, verify a light grippable implement, permitted low floor target about 2–3 m beyond release, and containment of the entire flight/rebound/roll; use a throwing wall only after verification. Use a non-rebounding slam ball for slams. Clear the area between the leg drill and hand drill of each pair. Pairing is a coaching connection, not simultaneous stations or a throw immediately after a jump. Secure band/rope anchors and the landmine base. Kicks stay below hip height with a soft terminal knee, active recoil and no contact or spinning kick. Handoffs are controlled: secure the grip and wait for the feeder to release and step clear before turning. No new airborne-feed progression is added.
rotation-full-body.quality: Within the scheduled attempts, record each side’s support-foot release, hip-led initiation and controlled finish. Use today’s three connections to identify whether a miss begins at support, transfer or endpoint. Different drills are not equivalent force tests; use observed control and recovery to choose the next appropriate demand.

rotation-full-body.explosiveNotes: E1/E2 Lateral catch → outward release: Establish a balanced split-to-parallel landing, then keep a stable base as the backhand hand path moves outward. E3/E4 Knee drive → rising hand path: Keep the hovering-leg drive and uppercut connected to a tall trunk without substituting a back arch for limb acceleration. E5/E6 Release step → diagonal pull: Push out of the held split stance, then use a settled stance to send rotational force down the rope diagonal.
rotation-full-body.progression: Expand the stage to its complementary entry, direction or control demands. Transfer the support-and-finish standards from the preceding integrated class; new task demands do not authorize heavier loads. Review actual attendance, technique, loads, soreness and other training. Change one demand only after clean execution at the intended reserve and acceptable recovery; otherwise hold or regress. No athlete completion, readiness or improvement is inferred from a class number.

E: Expand the stage to its complementary entry, direction or control demands. Transfer the support-and-finish standards from the preceding integrated class; new task demands do not authorize heavier loads.

Each bridge connects two separately coached exercises. Complete all prescribed work and recovery for the first, then clear/reset the area for the second. Never combine a jump or kick with a simultaneous throw. Use the source’s shorter-range, supported, stationary or paused replacement inside the same slot. For handoffs, secure grip and wait for the feeder to step clear; use the existing self-held replacement when needed.
S: One upper-body/trunk and one hip/foot resilience exercise connect control at both ends of the rotational chain. Keep at least 4–5 clean repetitions or about 5 seconds of a sound hold in reserve. Preserve the row’s within-hold relaxation and use the stated side/exercise recovery.
P: Three lower-body and three upper-body/trunk lifts support the class’s force-transfer purpose. Across the first two classes of each stage, every original primary-strength prescription is included once; the additional day selects complementary full-body strength. Perform the listed easy preparation for each lift, with its recovery, before working. Keep 2–3 clean reps in reserve and the source controlled return tempo.

rotation-full-body.delivery: Plan one integrated class per week. Complete Access & Prepare 1 → six explosive exercises → two light resilience exercises → six primary-strength exercises. In each explosive pair, complete the lower-body exercise with its prescribed recovery, clear/reset the space, then complete the connected upper-body exercise. Each exercise has its own sets and rest; this is not a superset, continuous kick/throw combination or fatigue circuit. Preserve both-side doses and the longer of the row recovery and the source class’s between-exercise recovery. Allow 10–15 s between upper-body attempts, normally 20 s between lower-body attempts and 60 s for the early-cue lower-body tasks. Extend recovery when quality requires. Primary easy loading sets are separate from working reps. Confirm combined class duration from the selected doses, rest, preparation and actual group flow; original whole-course class durations cannot simply be added or reused. Review other sport/gym/tumbling work and the source roughly 48–72 h planning allowance from comparable demanding exposures. Resume missed classes in sequence instead of doubling up.
rotation-full-body.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1 unchanged; do not recreate it or assign an assumed duration. Review its actual demands before this full-body class. Check the written setup and readiness of the selected kick, landing, handoff and implement tasks.
rotation-full-body.setup: Use the existing separate 10 m lanes. Keep waiting athletes outside the swept-leg, landing and ball paths. For released balls, verify a light grippable implement, permitted low floor target about 2–3 m beyond release, and containment of the entire flight/rebound/roll; use a throwing wall only after verification. Use a non-rebounding slam ball for slams. Clear the area between the leg drill and hand drill of each pair. Pairing is a coaching connection, not simultaneous stations or a throw immediately after a jump. Secure band/rope anchors and the landmine base. Kicks stay below hip height with a soft terminal knee, active recoil and no contact or spinning kick. Handoffs are controlled: secure the grip and wait for the feeder to release and step clear before turning. No new airborne-feed progression is added.
rotation-full-body.quality: Within the scheduled attempts, record each side’s support-foot release, hip-led initiation and controlled finish. Use today’s three connections to identify whether a miss begins at support, transfer or endpoint. Contrast a held lower-body start with a permitted upper-body preload, then apply the same tall-trunk control to an upward hand finish. Classify each scheduled attempt as held, preloaded or an unintended redip; use that observation to choose the next appropriate start.

rotation-full-body.explosiveNotes: E1/E2 Support → output: Keep the paused jump truly still and the scoop reversal continuous; do not blend the start rules. E3/E4 Accelerate → control: Carry the controlled held-kick initiation into a compact uppercut without adding a preparatory bounce. E5/E6 Recover → redirect: Use isolated hip rotation to rehearse the torque contribution before the whole-chain speed row.
rotation-full-body.progression: Contrast a held lower-body start with a permitted upper-body preload, then apply the same tall-trunk control to an upward hand finish. Classify each scheduled attempt as held, preloaded or an unintended redip; use that observation to choose the next appropriate start. Each bridge connects two separately coached exercises. Complete all prescribed work and recovery for the first, then clear/reset the area for the second. Never combine a jump or kick with a simultaneous throw. Use the source’s shorter-range, supported, stationary or paused replacement inside the same slot. For handoffs, secure grip and wait for the feeder to step clear; use the existing self-held replacement when needed.
S: One upper-body/trunk and one hip/foot resilience exercise connect control at both ends of the rotational chain. Keep at least 4–5 clean repetitions or about 5 seconds of a sound hold in reserve. Preserve the row’s within-hold relaxation and use the stated side/exercise recovery.
P: Three lower-body and three upper-body/trunk lifts support the class’s force-transfer purpose. Across the first two classes of each stage, every original primary-strength prescription is included once; the additional day selects complementary full-body strength. Perform the listed easy preparation for each lift, with its recovery, before working. Keep 2–3 clean reps in reserve and the source controlled return tempo.

connections.title: Chamber → upward hand drive
connections.cue: Keep the supported chamber and band uppercut low enough to preserve a stacked trunk while the limb rises.

connections.title: Recoil → planted release

rotation-full-body.delivery: Plan one integrated class per week. Complete Access & Prepare 1 → six explosive exercises → two light resilience exercises → six primary-strength exercises. In each explosive pair, complete the lower-body exercise with its prescribed recovery, clear/reset the space, then complete the connected upper-body exercise. Each exercise has its own sets and rest; this is not a superset, continuous kick/throw combination or fatigue circuit. Preserve both-side doses and the longer of the row recovery and the source class’s between-exercise recovery. Allow 10–15 s between upper-body attempts, normally 20 s between lower-body attempts and 60 s for the early-cue lower-body tasks. Extend recovery when quality requires. Primary easy loading sets are separate from working reps. Confirm combined class duration from the selected doses, rest, preparation and actual group flow; original whole-course class durations cannot simply be added or reused. Review other sport/gym/tumbling work and the source roughly 48–72 h planning allowance from comparable demanding exposures. Resume missed classes in sequence instead of doubling up.
rotation-full-body.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1 unchanged; do not recreate it or assign an assumed duration. Review its actual demands before this full-body class. Check the written setup and readiness of the selected kick, landing, handoff and implement tasks.
rotation-full-body.setup: Use the existing separate 10 m lanes. Keep waiting athletes outside the swept-leg, landing and ball paths. For released balls, verify a light grippable implement, permitted low floor target about 2–3 m beyond release, and containment of the entire flight/rebound/roll; use a throwing wall only after verification. Use a non-rebounding slam ball for slams. Clear the area between the leg drill and hand drill of each pair. Pairing is a coaching connection, not simultaneous stations or a throw immediately after a jump. Secure band/rope anchors and the landmine base. Kicks stay below hip height with a soft terminal knee, active recoil and no contact or spinning kick. Handoffs are controlled: secure the grip and wait for the feeder to release and step clear before turning. No new airborne-feed progression is added.
rotation-full-body.quality: Within the scheduled attempts, record each side’s support-foot release, hip-led initiation and controlled finish. Use today’s three connections to identify whether a miss begins at support, transfer or endpoint. Different drills are not equivalent force tests; use observed control and recovery to choose the next appropriate demand.

rotation-full-body.explosiveNotes: E1/E2 Support → output: Settle the plant, express force and own the finish in both the kick and shot-put. E3/E4 Accelerate → control: Compare inward leg recovery with the compact hand hook: neither arc should pull the torso off its base. E5/E6 Recover → redirect: Connect active knee folding and the band uppercut through a quiet pelvis and controlled limb return.
rotation-full-body.progression: Apply the same finish-and-return standard to the step-in release, kick re-chamber, inward leg sweep and short hand paths. Use the shorter source extension or stationary entry when return control deteriorates, retaining the remaining scheduled attempts only. Review actual attendance, technique, loads, soreness and other training. Change one demand only after clean execution at the intended reserve and acceptable recovery; otherwise hold or regress. No athlete completion, readiness or improvement is inferred from a class number.

E: Apply the same finish-and-return standard to the step-in release, kick re-chamber, inward leg sweep and short hand paths. Use the shorter source extension or stationary entry when return control deteriorates, retaining the remaining scheduled attempts only.

Each bridge connects two separately coached exercises. Complete all prescribed work and recovery for the first, then clear/reset the area for the second. Never combine a jump or kick with a simultaneous throw. Use the source’s shorter-range, supported, stationary or paused replacement inside the same slot. For handoffs, secure grip and wait for the feeder to step clear; use the existing self-held replacement when needed.
S: One upper-body/trunk and one hip/foot resilience exercise connect control at both ends of the rotational chain. Keep at least 4–5 clean repetitions or about 5 seconds of a sound hold in reserve. Preserve the row’s within-hold relaxation and use the stated side/exercise recovery.
P: Three lower-body and three upper-body/trunk lifts support the class’s force-transfer purpose. Across the first two classes of each stage, every original primary-strength prescription is included once; the additional day selects complementary full-body strength. Perform the listed easy preparation for each lift, with its recovery, before working. Keep 2–3 clean reps in reserve and the source controlled return tempo.

rotation-full-body.title: Full body · Lateral arrival into leg and hand force
rotation-full-body.effort: Accept lateral arrival and redirect it through the body. Shuffle → kick and throw; Uncross → rotational output; Lateral catch → retained cross.
rotation-full-body.extension: Establish the stage’s support and force-transfer connections using both source courses inside this class. Keep the original working doses; qualify the listed range and load before seeking more speed.

connections.title: Shuffle → kick and throw
connections.cue: Use one short shuffle and a usable plant before either the kicking thigh or the hands accelerate.

connections.title: Uncross → rotational output
connections.cue: Finish the crossover chamber and step-behind slam entries with uncrossed feet before turning; retain each source travel limit.

connections.title: Lateral catch → retained cross
connections.cue: Own the bound-to-split catch before applying the same support alignment to the planted band cross.

rotation-full-body.delivery: Plan one integrated class per week. Complete Access & Prepare 1 → six explosive exercises → two light resilience exercises → six primary-strength exercises. In each explosive pair, complete the lower-body exercise with its prescribed recovery, clear/reset the space, then complete the connected upper-body exercise. Each exercise has its own sets and rest; this is not a superset, continuous kick/throw combination or fatigue circuit. Preserve both-side doses and the longer of the row recovery and the source class’s between-exercise recovery. Allow 10–15 s between upper-body attempts, normally 20 s between lower-body attempts and 60 s for the early-cue lower-body tasks. Extend recovery when quality requires. Primary easy loading sets are separate from working reps. Confirm combined class duration from the selected doses, rest, preparation and actual group flow; original whole-course class durations cannot simply be added or reused. Review other sport/gym/tumbling work and the source roughly 48–72 h planning allowance from comparable demanding exposures. Resume missed classes in sequence instead of doubling up.
rotation-full-body.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1 unchanged; do not recreate it or assign an assumed duration. Review its actual demands before this full-body class. Check the written setup and readiness of the selected kick, landing, handoff and implement tasks.
rotation-full-body.setup: Use the existing separate 10 m lanes. Keep waiting athletes outside the swept-leg, landing and ball paths. For released balls, verify a light grippable implement, permitted low floor target about 2–3 m beyond release, and containment of the entire flight/rebound/roll; use a throwing wall only after verification. Use a non-rebounding slam ball for slams. Clear the area between the leg drill and hand drill of each pair. Pairing is a coaching connection, not simultaneous stations or a throw immediately after a jump. Secure band/rope anchors and the landmine base. Kicks stay below hip height with a soft terminal knee, active recoil and no contact or spinning kick. Handoffs are controlled: secure the grip and wait for the feeder to release and step clear before turning. No new airborne-feed progression is added.
rotation-full-body.quality: Within the scheduled attempts, record each side’s support-foot release, hip-led initiation and controlled finish. Use today’s three connections to identify whether a miss begins at support, transfer or endpoint. Different drills are not equivalent force tests; use observed control and recovery to choose the next appropriate demand.

E3/E4 Uncross → rotational output: Finish the crossover chamber and step-behind slam entries with uncrossed feet before turning; retain each source travel limit. rotation-full-body.progression: Establish the stage’s support and force-transfer connections using both source courses inside this class. Keep the original working doses; qualify the listed range and load before seeking more speed. Review actual attendance, technique, loads, soreness and other training. Change one demand only after clean execution at the intended reserve and acceptable recovery; otherwise hold or regress. No athlete completion, readiness or improvement is inferred from a class number.

Each bridge connects two separately coached exercises. Complete all prescribed work and recovery for the first, then clear/reset the area for the second. Never combine a jump or kick with a simultaneous throw. Use the source’s shorter-range, supported, stationary or paused replacement inside the same slot. For handoffs, secure grip and wait for the feeder to step clear; use the existing self-held replacement when needed.
S: One upper-body/trunk and one hip/foot resilience exercise connect control at both ends of the rotational chain. Keep at least 4–5 clean repetitions or about 5 seconds of a sound hold in reserve. Preserve the row’s within-hold relaxation and use the stated side/exercise recovery.
P: Three lower-body and three upper-body/trunk lifts support the class’s force-transfer purpose. Across the first two classes of each stage, every original primary-strength prescription is included once; the additional day selects complementary full-body strength. Perform the listed easy preparation for each lift, with its recovery, before working. Keep 2–3 clean reps in reserve and the source controlled return tempo.

rotation-full-body.title: Full body · Reload, brake and recover
rotation-full-body.effort: Accept lateral arrival and redirect it through the body. Step-behind push → hip reload; Adductor contribution → lateral hand pulse; Return base → stop the implement.
rotation-full-body.extension: Expand the stage to its complementary entry, direction or control demands. Transfer the support-and-finish standards from the preceding integrated class; new task demands do not authorize heavier loads.

connections.title: Step-behind push → hip reload
connections.cue: Use the step-behind bound to organize lateral push-off, then control the smaller drop-step reload before the scoop release.

connections.title: Adductor contribution → lateral hand pulse

rotation-full-body.delivery: Plan one integrated class per week. Complete Access & Prepare 1 → six explosive exercises → two light resilience exercises → six primary-strength exercises. In each explosive pair, complete the lower-body exercise with its prescribed recovery, clear/reset the space, then complete the connected upper-body exercise. Each exercise has its own sets and rest; this is not a superset, continuous kick/throw combination or fatigue circuit. Preserve both-side doses and the longer of the row recovery and the source class’s between-exercise recovery. Allow 10–15 s between upper-body attempts, normally 20 s between lower-body attempts and 60 s for the early-cue lower-body tasks. Extend recovery when quality requires. Primary easy loading sets are separate from working reps. Confirm combined class duration from the selected doses, rest, preparation and actual group flow; original whole-course class durations cannot simply be added or reused. Review other sport/gym/tumbling work and the source roughly 48–72 h planning allowance from comparable demanding exposures. Resume missed classes in sequence instead of doubling up.
rotation-full-body.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1 unchanged; do not recreate it or assign an assumed duration. Review its actual demands before this full-body class. Check the written setup and readiness of the selected kick, landing, handoff and implement tasks.
rotation-full-body.setup: Use the existing separate 10 m lanes. Keep waiting athletes outside the swept-leg, landing and ball paths. For released balls, verify a light grippable implement, permitted low floor target about 2–3 m beyond release, and containment of the entire flight/rebound/roll; use a throwing wall only after verification. Use a non-rebounding slam ball for slams. Clear the area between the leg drill and hand drill of each pair. Pairing is a coaching connection, not simultaneous stations or a throw immediately after a jump. Secure band/rope anchors and the landmine base. Kicks stay below hip height with a soft terminal knee, active recoil and no contact or spinning kick. Handoffs are controlled: secure the grip and wait for the feeder to release and step clear before turning. No new airborne-feed progression is added.
rotation-full-body.quality: Within the scheduled attempts, record each side’s support-foot release, hip-led initiation and controlled finish. Use today’s three connections to identify whether a miss begins at support, transfer or endpoint. Different drills are not equivalent force tests; use observed control and recovery to choose the next appropriate demand.

Each bridge connects two separately coached exercises. Complete all prescribed work and recovery for the first, then clear/reset the area for the second. Never combine a jump or kick with a simultaneous throw. Use the source’s shorter-range, supported, stationary or paused replacement inside the same slot. rotation-full-body.delivery: Plan one integrated class per week. Complete Access & Prepare 1 → six explosive exercises → two light resilience exercises → six primary-strength exercises. In each explosive pair, complete the lower-body exercise with its prescribed recovery, clear/reset the space, then complete the connected upper-body exercise. Each exercise has its own sets and rest; this is not a superset, continuous kick/throw combination or fatigue circuit. Preserve both-side doses and the longer of the row recovery and the source class’s between-exercise recovery. Allow 10–15 s between upper-body attempts, normally 20 s between lower-body attempts and 60 s for the early-cue lower-body tasks. Extend recovery when quality requires. Primary easy loading sets are separate from working reps. Confirm combined class duration from the selected doses, rest, preparation and actual group flow; original whole-course class durations cannot simply be added or reused. Review other sport/gym/tumbling work and the source roughly 48–72 h planning allowance from comparable demanding exposures. Resume missed classes in sequence instead of doubling up.
rotation-full-body.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1 unchanged; do not recreate it or assign an assumed duration. Review its actual demands before this full-body class. Check the written setup and readiness of the selected kick, landing, handoff and implement tasks.
rotation-full-body.setup: Use the existing separate 10 m lanes. Keep waiting athletes outside the swept-leg, landing and ball paths. For released balls, verify a light grippable implement, permitted low floor target about 2–3 m beyond release, and containment of the entire flight/rebound/roll; use a throwing wall only after verification. Use a non-rebounding slam ball for slams. Clear the area between the leg drill and hand drill of each pair. Pairing is a coaching connection, not simultaneous stations or a throw immediately after a jump. Secure band/rope anchors and the landmine base. Kicks stay below hip height with a soft terminal knee, active recoil and no contact or spinning kick. Handoffs are controlled: secure the grip and wait for the feeder to release and step clear before turning. No new airborne-feed progression is added.
rotation-full-body.quality: Within the scheduled attempts, record each side’s support-foot release, hip-led initiation and controlled finish. Use today’s three connections to identify whether a miss begins at support, transfer or endpoint. Apply the same plant-and-stop cue to a lateral kick/throw pair, a bound-to-catch/ball-stop pair and a crossover-chamber/band-cross pair. Log entry length and rescue steps so the next progression changes control or entry demand before adding load.

rotation-full-body.progression: Apply the same plant-and-stop cue to a lateral kick/throw pair, a bound-to-catch/ball-stop pair and a crossover-chamber/band-cross pair. Log entry length and rescue steps so the next progression changes control or entry demand before adding load. Review actual attendance, technique, loads, soreness and other training. Change one demand only after clean execution at the intended reserve and acceptable recovery; otherwise hold or regress. No athlete completion, readiness or improvement is inferred from a class number.

Each bridge connects two separately coached exercises. Complete all prescribed work and recovery for the first, then clear/reset the area for the second. Never combine a jump or kick with a simultaneous throw. Use the source’s shorter-range, supported, stationary or paused replacement inside the same slot. For handoffs, secure grip and wait for the feeder to step clear; use the existing self-held replacement when needed.
S: One upper-body/trunk and one hip/foot resilience exercise connect control at both ends of the rotational chain. Keep at least 4–5 clean repetitions or about 5 seconds of a sound hold in reserve. Preserve the row’s within-hold relaxation and use the stated side/exercise recovery.
P: Three lower-body and three upper-body/trunk lifts support the class’s force-transfer purpose. Across the first two classes of each stage, every original primary-strength prescription is included once; the additional day selects complementary full-body strength. Perform the listed easy preparation for each lift, with its recovery, before working. Keep 2–3 clean reps in reserve and the source controlled return tempo.

rotation-full-body.delivery: Plan one integrated class per week. Complete Access & Prepare 1 → six explosive exercises → two light resilience exercises → six primary-strength exercises. In each explosive pair, complete the lower-body exercise with its prescribed recovery, clear/reset the space, then complete the connected upper-body exercise. Each exercise has its own sets and rest; this is not a superset, continuous kick/throw combination or fatigue circuit. Preserve both-side doses and the longer of the row recovery and the source class’s between-exercise recovery. Allow 10–15 s between upper-body attempts, normally 20 s between lower-body attempts and 60 s for the early-cue lower-body tasks. Extend recovery when quality requires. Primary easy loading sets are separate from working reps. Confirm combined class duration from the selected doses, rest, preparation and actual group flow; original whole-course class durations cannot simply be added or reused. Review other sport/gym/tumbling work and the source roughly 48–72 h planning allowance from comparable demanding exposures. Resume missed classes in sequence instead of doubling up.
rotation-full-body.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1 unchanged; do not recreate it or assign an assumed duration. Review its actual demands before this full-body class. Check the written setup and readiness of the selected kick, landing, handoff and implement tasks.
rotation-full-body.setup: Use the existing separate 10 m lanes. Keep waiting athletes outside the swept-leg, landing and ball paths. For released balls, verify a light grippable implement, permitted low floor target about 2–3 m beyond release, and containment of the entire flight/rebound/roll; use a throwing wall only after verification. Use a non-rebounding slam ball for slams. Clear the area between the leg drill and hand drill of each pair. Pairing is a coaching connection, not simultaneous stations or a throw immediately after a jump. Secure band/rope anchors and the landmine base. Kicks stay below hip height with a soft terminal knee, active recoil and no contact or spinning kick. Handoffs are controlled: secure the grip and wait for the feeder to release and step clear before turning. No new airborne-feed progression is added.
rotation-full-body.quality: Within the scheduled attempts, record each side’s support-foot release, hip-led initiation and controlled finish. Use today’s three connections to identify whether a miss begins at support, transfer or endpoint. Different drills are not equivalent force tests; use observed control and recovery to choose the next appropriate demand.
