exercises.preparation: One easy set of 3 per side with bodyweight or lighter resistance before this lift, separate from working reps. Allow 30–45 s between preparation sides where applicable and 60–90 s before working. Add and record any further ramps and their time. Keep 2–3 clean repetitions in reserve during working sets; qualify each athlete’s current load rather than automatically increasing it.

rotation-full-body.explosiveNotes: E1/E2 Heel release → rising impulse: Keep the calf-pop grounded, then use a free foot/hip turn to produce one modest upward rope pulse. E3/E4 Neutral support → constrained push: Organize the parallel-stance kick base, then retain trunk control when the kneeling shot-put reduces leg propulsion. E5/E6 Retreat plant → body-and-ball stop: Own the small retreat plant and then the compact retained-ball endpoint; neither task should drift into another turn.
rotation-full-body.progression: Establish the stage’s support and force-transfer connections using both source courses inside this class. Keep the original working doses; qualify the listed range and load before seeking more speed. Review actual attendance, technique, loads, soreness and other training. Change one demand only after clean execution at the intended reserve and acceptable recovery; otherwise hold or regress. No athlete completion, readiness or improvement is inferred from a class number.

E: Establish the stage’s support and force-transfer connections using both source courses inside this class. Keep the original working doses; qualify the listed range and load before seeking more speed.

Each bridge connects two separately coached exercises. Complete all prescribed work and recovery for the first, then clear/reset the area for the second. Never combine a jump or kick with a simultaneous throw. Use the source’s shorter-range, supported, stationary or paused replacement inside the same slot. For handoffs, secure grip and wait for the feeder to step clear; use the existing self-held replacement when needed.
S: One upper-body/trunk and one hip/foot resilience exercise connect control at both ends of the rotational chain. Keep at least 4–5 clean repetitions or about 5 seconds of a sound hold in reserve. Preserve the row’s within-hold relaxation and use the stated side/exercise recovery.
P: Three lower-body and three upper-body/trunk lifts support the class’s force-transfer purpose. Across the first two classes of each stage, every original primary-strength prescription is included once; the additional day selects complementary full-body strength. Perform the listed easy preparation for each lift, with its recovery, before working. Keep 2–3 clean reps in reserve and the source controlled return tempo.

rotation-full-body.title: Full body · Control both ends of the turn
rotation-full-body.effort: Consolidate compact rotation with reduced workload. Leg-driven turn → outward hand force; Outward leg arc → downward hand arc; Isolated hip return → pulling turn.
rotation-full-body.extension: Expand the stage to its complementary entry, direction or control demands. Transfer the support-and-finish standards from the preceding integrated class; new task demands do not authorize heavier loads.

connections.title: Leg-driven turn → outward hand force
connections.cue: Keep hands on hips for the turning jump, then allow a short backhand path from a controlled grounded base.

connections.title: Outward leg arc → downward hand arc

connections.title: Isolated hip return → pulling turn

rotation-full-body.delivery: Plan one integrated class per week. Complete Access & Prepare 1 → six explosive exercises → two light resilience exercises → six primary-strength exercises. In each explosive pair, complete the lower-body exercise with its prescribed recovery, clear/reset the space, then complete the connected upper-body exercise. Each exercise has its own sets and rest; this is not a superset, continuous kick/throw combination or fatigue circuit. Preserve both-side doses and the longer of the row recovery and the source class’s between-exercise recovery. Allow 10–15 s between upper-body attempts, normally 20 s between lower-body attempts and 60 s for the early-cue lower-body tasks. Extend recovery when quality requires. Primary easy loading sets are separate from working reps. Confirm combined class duration from the selected doses, rest, preparation and actual group flow; original whole-course class durations cannot simply be added or reused. Review other sport/gym/tumbling work and the source roughly 48–72 h planning allowance from comparable demanding exposures. Resume missed classes in sequence instead of doubling up.
rotation-full-body.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1 unchanged; do not recreate it or assign an assumed duration. Review its actual demands before this full-body class. Check the written setup and readiness of the selected kick, landing, handoff and implement tasks.
rotation-full-body.setup: Use the existing separate 10 m lanes. Keep waiting athletes outside the swept-leg, landing and ball paths. For released balls, verify a light grippable implement, permitted low floor target about 2–3 m beyond release, and containment of the entire flight/rebound/roll; use a throwing wall only after verification. Use a non-rebounding slam ball for slams. Clear the area between the leg drill and hand drill of each pair. Pairing is a coaching connection, not simultaneous stations or a throw immediately after a jump. Secure band/rope anchors and the landmine base. Kicks stay below hip height with a soft terminal knee, active recoil and no contact or spinning kick. Handoffs are controlled: secure the grip and wait for the feeder to release and step clear before turning. No new airborne-feed progression is added.
rotation-full-body.quality: Within the scheduled attempts, record each side’s support-foot release, hip-led initiation and controlled finish. Use today’s three connections to identify whether a miss begins at support, transfer or endpoint. Different drills are not equivalent force tests; use observed control and recovery to choose the next appropriate demand.

Rest 20 s between attempts, 60 s between sides/directions, then 90 s before the next entry/section.

Each bridge connects two separately coached exercises. Complete all prescribed work and recovery for the first, then clear/reset the area for the second. Each bridge connects two separately coached exercises. Complete all prescribed work and recovery for the first, then clear/reset the area for the second. Never combine a jump or kick with a simultaneous throw. Use the source’s shorter-range, supported, stationary or paused replacement inside the same slot. For handoffs, secure grip and wait for the feeder to step clear; use the existing self-held replacement when needed.
S: One upper-body/trunk and one hip/foot resilience exercise connect control at both ends of the rotational chain. Keep at least 4–5 clean repetitions or about 5 seconds of a sound hold in reserve. Preserve the row’s within-hold relaxation and use the stated side/exercise recovery.
P: Three lower-body and three upper-body/trunk lifts support the class’s force-transfer purpose. Across the first two classes of each stage, every original primary-strength prescription is included once; the additional day selects complementary full-body strength. Perform the listed easy preparation for each lift, with its recovery, before working. Keep 2–3 clean reps in reserve and the source controlled return tempo.

rotation-full-body.delivery: Plan one integrated class per week. Complete Access & Prepare 1 → six explosive exercises → two light resilience exercises → six primary-strength exercises. In each explosive pair, complete the lower-body exercise with its prescribed recovery, clear/reset the space, then complete the connected upper-body exercise. Each exercise has its own sets and rest; this is not a superset, continuous kick/throw combination or fatigue circuit. Preserve both-side doses and the longer of the row recovery and the source class’s between-exercise recovery. Allow 10–15 s between upper-body attempts, normally 20 s between lower-body attempts and 60 s for the early-cue lower-body tasks. Extend recovery when quality requires. Primary easy loading sets are separate from working reps. Confirm combined class duration from the selected doses, rest, preparation and actual group flow; original whole-course class durations cannot simply be added or reused. Review other sport/gym/tumbling work and the source roughly 48–72 h planning allowance from comparable demanding exposures. Resume missed classes in sequence instead of doubling up.
rotation-full-body.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1 unchanged; do not recreate it or assign an assumed duration. Review its actual demands before this full-body class. Check the written setup and readiness of the selected kick, landing, handoff and implement tasks.
rotation-full-body.setup: Use the existing separate 10 m lanes. Keep waiting athletes outside the swept-leg, landing and ball paths. For released balls, verify a light grippable implement, permitted low floor target about 2–3 m beyond release, and containment of the entire flight/rebound/roll; use a throwing wall only after verification. Use a non-rebounding slam ball for slams. Clear the area between the leg drill and hand drill of each pair. Pairing is a coaching connection, not simultaneous stations or a throw immediately after a jump. Secure band/rope anchors and the landmine base. Kicks stay below hip height with a soft terminal knee, active recoil and no contact or spinning kick. Handoffs are controlled: secure the grip and wait for the feeder to release and step clear before turning. No new airborne-feed progression is added.
rotation-full-body.quality: Within the scheduled attempts, record each side’s support-foot release, hip-led initiation and controlled finish. Use today’s three connections to identify whether a miss begins at support, transfer or endpoint. Different drills are not equivalent force tests; use observed control and recovery to choose the next appropriate demand.

rotation-full-body.delivery: Plan one integrated class per week. Complete Access & Prepare 1 → six explosive exercises → two light resilience exercises → six primary-strength exercises. In each explosive pair, complete the lower-body exercise with its prescribed recovery, clear/reset the space, then complete the connected upper-body exercise. Each exercise has its own sets and rest; this is not a superset, continuous kick/throw combination or fatigue circuit. Preserve both-side doses and the longer of the row recovery and the source class’s between-exercise recovery. Allow 10–15 s between upper-body attempts, normally 20 s between lower-body attempts and 60 s for the early-cue lower-body tasks. Extend recovery when quality requires. Primary easy loading sets are separate from working reps. Confirm combined class duration from the selected doses, rest, preparation and actual group flow; original whole-course class durations cannot simply be added or reused. Review other sport/gym/tumbling work and the source roughly 48–72 h planning allowance from comparable demanding exposures. Resume missed classes in sequence instead of doubling up.
rotation-full-body.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1 unchanged; do not recreate it or assign an assumed duration. Review its actual demands before this full-body class. Check the written setup and readiness of the selected kick, landing, handoff and implement tasks.
rotation-full-body.setup: Use the existing separate 10 m lanes. Keep waiting athletes outside the swept-leg, landing and ball paths. For released balls, verify a light grippable implement, permitted low floor target about 2–3 m beyond release, and containment of the entire flight/rebound/roll; use a throwing wall only after verification. Use a non-rebounding slam ball for slams. Clear the area between the leg drill and hand drill of each pair. Pairing is a coaching connection, not simultaneous stations or a throw immediately after a jump. Secure band/rope anchors and the landmine base. Kicks stay below hip height with a soft terminal knee, active recoil and no contact or spinning kick. Handoffs are controlled: secure the grip and wait for the feeder to release and step clear before turning. No new airborne-feed progression is added.
rotation-full-body.quality: Within the scheduled attempts, record each side’s support-foot release, hip-led initiation and controlled finish. Use today’s three connections to identify whether a miss begins at support, transfer or endpoint. Integrate the receiving lesson with three grounded leg actions, removing rebound landings from this application day. Use controlled handoffs only. Preserve the support-before-turn sequence when switching from externally supplied release to retained-ball stopping and band sweeping.

rotation-full-body.explosiveNotes: E1/E2 Support → output: Organize the hip load and the supplied ball before initiating either turn. rotation-full-body.progression: Integrate the receiving lesson with three grounded leg actions, removing rebound landings from this application day. Use controlled handoffs only. Review actual attendance, technique, loads, soreness and other training. Change one demand only after clean execution at the intended reserve and acceptable recovery; otherwise hold or regress. No athlete completion, readiness or improvement is inferred from a class number.

Each bridge connects two separately coached exercises. Complete all prescribed work and recovery for the first, then clear/reset the area for the second. Never combine a jump or kick with a simultaneous throw. Use the source’s shorter-range, supported, stationary or paused replacement inside the same slot. For handoffs, secure grip and wait for the feeder to step clear; use the existing self-held replacement when needed.
S: One upper-body/trunk and one hip/foot resilience exercise connect control at both ends of the rotational chain. Keep at least 4–5 clean repetitions or about 5 seconds of a sound hold in reserve. Preserve the row’s within-hold relaxation and use the stated side/exercise recovery.
P: Three lower-body and three upper-body/trunk lifts support the class’s force-transfer purpose. Across the first two classes of each stage, every original primary-strength prescription is included once; the additional day selects complementary full-body strength. Perform the listed easy preparation for each lift, with its recovery, before working. Keep 2–3 clean reps in reserve and the source controlled return tempo.

rotation-full-body.delivery: Plan one integrated class per week. Complete Access & Prepare 1 → six explosive exercises → two light resilience exercises → six primary-strength exercises. In each explosive pair, complete the lower-body exercise with its prescribed recovery, clear/reset the space, then complete the connected upper-body exercise. Each exercise has its own sets and rest; this is not a superset, continuous kick/throw combination or fatigue circuit. Preserve both-side doses and the longer of the row recovery and the source class’s between-exercise recovery. Allow 10–15 s between upper-body attempts, normally 20 s between lower-body attempts and 60 s for the early-cue lower-body tasks. Extend recovery when quality requires. Primary easy loading sets are separate from working reps. Confirm combined class duration from the selected doses, rest, preparation and actual group flow; original whole-course class durations cannot simply be added or reused. Review other sport/gym/tumbling work and the source roughly 48–72 h planning allowance from comparable demanding exposures. Resume missed classes in sequence instead of doubling up.
rotation-full-body.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1 unchanged; do not recreate it or assign an assumed duration. Review its actual demands before this full-body class. Check the written setup and readiness of the selected kick, landing, handoff and implement tasks.
rotation-full-body.setup: Use the existing separate 10 m lanes. Keep waiting athletes outside the swept-leg, landing and ball paths. For released balls, verify a light grippable implement, permitted low floor target about 2–3 m beyond release, and containment of the entire flight/rebound/roll; use a throwing wall only after verification. Use a non-rebounding slam ball for slams. Clear the area between the leg drill and hand drill of each pair. Pairing is a coaching connection, not simultaneous stations or a throw immediately after a jump. Secure band/rope anchors and the landmine base. Kicks stay below hip height with a soft terminal knee, active recoil and no contact or spinning kick. Handoffs are controlled: secure the grip and wait for the feeder to release and step clear before turning. No new airborne-feed progression is added.
rotation-full-body.quality: Within the scheduled attempts, record each side’s support-foot release, hip-led initiation and controlled finish. Use today’s three connections to identify whether a miss begins at support, transfer or endpoint. Different drills are not equivalent force tests; use observed control and recovery to choose the next appropriate demand.

rotation-full-body.delivery: Plan one integrated class per week. Complete Access & Prepare 1 → six explosive exercises → two light resilience exercises → six primary-strength exercises. In each explosive pair, complete the lower-body exercise with its prescribed recovery, clear/reset the space, then complete the connected upper-body exercise. Each exercise has its own sets and rest; this is not a superset, continuous kick/throw combination or fatigue circuit. Preserve both-side doses and the longer of the row recovery and the source class’s between-exercise recovery. Allow 10–15 s between upper-body attempts, normally 20 s between lower-body attempts and 60 s for the early-cue lower-body tasks. Extend recovery when quality requires. Primary easy loading sets are separate from working reps. Confirm combined class duration from the selected doses, rest, preparation and actual group flow; original whole-course class durations cannot simply be added or reused. Review other sport/gym/tumbling work and the source roughly 48–72 h planning allowance from comparable demanding exposures. Resume missed classes in sequence instead of doubling up.
rotation-full-body.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1 unchanged; do not recreate it or assign an assumed duration. Review its actual demands before this full-body class. Check the written setup and readiness of the selected kick, landing, handoff and implement tasks.
rotation-full-body.setup: Use the existing separate 10 m lanes. Keep waiting athletes outside the swept-leg, landing and ball paths. For released balls, verify a light grippable implement, permitted low floor target about 2–3 m beyond release, and containment of the entire flight/rebound/roll; use a throwing wall only after verification. Use a non-rebounding slam ball for slams. Clear the area between the leg drill and hand drill of each pair. Pairing is a coaching connection, not simultaneous stations or a throw immediately after a jump. Secure band/rope anchors and the landmine base. Kicks stay below hip height with a soft terminal knee, active recoil and no contact or spinning kick. Handoffs are controlled: secure the grip and wait for the feeder to release and step clear before turning. No new airborne-feed progression is added.
rotation-full-body.quality: Within the scheduled attempts, record each side’s support-foot release, hip-led initiation and controlled finish. Use today’s three connections to identify whether a miss begins at support, transfer or endpoint. Different drills are not equivalent force tests; use observed control and recovery to choose the next appropriate demand.

Each bridge connects two separately coached exercises. Complete all prescribed work and recovery for the first, then clear/reset the area for the second. Never combine a jump or kick with a simultaneous throw. Use the source’s shorter-range, supported, stationary or paused replacement inside the same slot. For handoffs, secure grip and wait for the feeder to step clear; use the existing self-held replacement when needed.
S: One upper-body/trunk and one hip/foot resilience exercise connect control at both ends of the rotational chain. Keep at least 4–5 clean repetitions or about 5 seconds of a sound hold in reserve. Preserve the row’s within-hold relaxation and use the stated side/exercise recovery.
P: Three lower-body and three upper-body/trunk lifts support the class’s force-transfer purpose. Across the first two classes of each stage, every original primary-strength prescription is included once; the additional day selects complementary full-body strength. Perform the listed easy preparation for each lift, with its recovery, before working. Keep 2–3 clean reps in reserve and the source controlled return tempo.

rotation-full-body.title: Full body · Catch the reload without losing orientation
rotation-full-body.effort: Stop incoming travel, redirect the turn and recover a base. Drop-step takeoff → forward diagonal; Lateral return → rising hand path; Backward catch → constrained projection.
rotation-full-body.extension: Expand the stage to its complementary entry, direction or control demands. Transfer the support-and-finish standards from the preceding integrated class; new task demands do not authorize heavier loads.

rotation-full-body.delivery: Plan one integrated class per week. Complete Access & Prepare 1 → six explosive exercises → two light resilience exercises → six primary-strength exercises. In each explosive pair, complete the lower-body exercise with its prescribed recovery, clear/reset the space, then complete the connected upper-body exercise. Each exercise has its own sets and rest; this is not a superset, continuous kick/throw combination or fatigue circuit. Preserve both-side doses and the longer of the row recovery and the source class’s between-exercise recovery. Allow 10–15 s between upper-body attempts, normally 20 s between lower-body attempts and 60 s for the early-cue lower-body tasks. Extend recovery when quality requires. Primary easy loading sets are separate from working reps. Confirm combined class duration from the selected doses, rest, preparation and actual group flow; original whole-course class durations cannot simply be added or reused. Review other sport/gym/tumbling work and the source roughly 48–72 h planning allowance from comparable demanding exposures. Resume missed classes in sequence instead of doubling up.
rotation-full-body.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1 unchanged; do not recreate it or assign an assumed duration. Review its actual demands before this full-body class. Check the written setup and readiness of the selected kick, landing, handoff and implement tasks.
rotation-full-body.setup: Use the existing separate 10 m lanes. Keep waiting athletes outside the swept-leg, landing and ball paths. For released balls, verify a light grippable implement, permitted low floor target about 2–3 m beyond release, and containment of the entire flight/rebound/roll; use a throwing wall only after verification. Use a non-rebounding slam ball for slams. Clear the area between the leg drill and hand drill of each pair. Pairing is a coaching connection, not simultaneous stations or a throw immediately after a jump. Secure band/rope anchors and the landmine base. Kicks stay below hip height with a soft terminal knee, active recoil and no contact or spinning kick. Handoffs are controlled: secure the grip and wait for the feeder to release and step clear before turning. No new airborne-feed progression is added.
rotation-full-body.quality: Within the scheduled attempts, record each side’s support-foot release, hip-led initiation and controlled finish. Use today’s three connections to identify whether a miss begins at support, transfer or endpoint. Different drills are not equivalent force tests; use observed control and recovery to choose the next appropriate demand.

Each bridge connects two separately coached exercises. Complete all prescribed work and recovery for the first, then clear/reset the area for the second. Never combine a jump or kick with a simultaneous throw. Use the source’s shorter-range, supported, stationary or paused replacement inside the same slot. For handoffs, secure grip and wait for the feeder to step clear; use the existing self-held replacement when needed.
S: One upper-body/trunk and one hip/foot resilience exercise connect control at both ends of the rotational chain. Keep at least 4–5 clean repetitions or about 5 seconds of a sound hold in reserve. Preserve the row’s within-hold relaxation and use the stated side/exercise recovery.
P: Three lower-body and three upper-body/trunk lifts support the class’s force-transfer purpose. Across the first two classes of each stage, every original primary-strength prescription is included once; the additional day selects complementary full-body strength. Perform the listed easy preparation for each lift, with its recovery, before working. Keep 2–3 clean reps in reserve and the source controlled return tempo.

rotation-full-body.delivery: Plan one integrated class per week. Complete Access & Prepare 1 → six explosive exercises → two light resilience exercises → six primary-strength exercises. In each explosive pair, complete the lower-body exercise with its prescribed recovery, clear/reset the space, then complete the connected upper-body exercise. Each exercise has its own sets and rest; this is not a superset, continuous kick/throw combination or fatigue circuit. Preserve both-side doses and the longer of the row recovery and the source class’s between-exercise recovery. Allow 10–15 s between upper-body attempts, normally 20 s between lower-body attempts and 60 s for the early-cue lower-body tasks. Extend recovery when quality requires. Primary easy loading sets are separate from working reps. Confirm combined class duration from the selected doses, rest, preparation and actual group flow; original whole-course class durations cannot simply be added or reused. Review other sport/gym/tumbling work and the source roughly 48–72 h planning allowance from comparable demanding exposures. Resume missed classes in sequence instead of doubling up.
rotation-full-body.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1 unchanged; do not recreate it or assign an assumed duration. Review its actual demands before this full-body class. Check the written setup and readiness of the selected kick, landing, handoff and implement tasks.
rotation-full-body.setup: Use the existing separate 10 m lanes. Keep waiting athletes outside the swept-leg, landing and ball paths. For released balls, verify a light grippable implement, permitted low floor target about 2–3 m beyond release, and containment of the entire flight/rebound/roll; use a throwing wall only after verification. Use a non-rebounding slam ball for slams. Clear the area between the leg drill and hand drill of each pair. Pairing is a coaching connection, not simultaneous stations or a throw immediately after a jump. Secure band/rope anchors and the landmine base. Kicks stay below hip height with a soft terminal knee, active recoil and no contact or spinning kick. Handoffs are controlled: secure the grip and wait for the feeder to release and step clear before turning. No new airborne-feed progression is added.
rotation-full-body.quality: Within the scheduled attempts, record each side’s support-foot release, hip-led initiation and controlled finish. Use today’s three connections to identify whether a miss begins at support, transfer or endpoint. Apply one braking standard across retreat, unwind and inward recovery, then alternate outward release, pushing release and a rising resisted hand path. Bring the second lesson’s uppercut into the first lesson’s recovery tasks. Use the existing settled-plant alternatives when travel persists.

rotation-full-body.explosiveNotes: E1/E2 Support → output: Stop drift before the retreat kick and before the lateral-entry backhand release. E3/E4 Accelerate → control: Rebuild stance after the hip unwind and before the drop-step pressing release. E5/E6 Recover → redirect: Recover the inward leg sweep under a controlled pelvis, then preserve that base through the rising band uppercut without leaning back.
rotation-full-body.progression: Apply one braking standard across retreat, unwind and inward recovery, then alternate outward release, pushing release and a rising resisted hand path. Bring the second lesson’s uppercut into the first lesson’s recovery tasks. Use the existing settled-plant alternatives when travel persists. Review actual attendance, technique, loads, soreness and other training. Change one demand only after clean execution at the intended reserve and acceptable recovery; otherwise hold or regress. No athlete completion, readiness or improvement is inferred from a class number.

E: Apply one braking standard across retreat, unwind and inward recovery, then alternate outward release, pushing release and a rising resisted hand path. Bring the second lesson’s uppercut into the first lesson’s recovery tasks. Use the existing settled-plant alternatives when travel persists.

Each bridge connects two separately coached exercises. Complete all prescribed work and recovery for the first, then clear/reset the area for the second. Never combine a jump or kick with a simultaneous throw. Use the source’s shorter-range, supported, stationary or paused replacement inside the same slot. For handoffs, secure grip and wait for the feeder to step clear; use the existing self-held replacement when needed.
S: One upper-body/trunk and one hip/foot resilience exercise connect control at both ends of the rotational chain. Keep at least 4–5 clean repetitions or about 5 seconds of a sound hold in reserve. Preserve the row’s within-hold relaxation and use the stated side/exercise recovery.
P: Three lower-body and three upper-body/trunk lifts support the class’s force-transfer purpose. Across the first two classes of each stage, every original primary-strength prescription is included once; the additional day selects complementary full-body strength. Perform the listed easy preparation for each lift, with its recovery, before working. Keep 2–3 clean reps in reserve and the source controlled return tempo.

rotation-full-body.delivery: Plan one integrated class per week. Complete Access & Prepare 1 → six explosive exercises → two light resilience exercises → six primary-strength exercises. In each explosive pair, complete the lower-body exercise with its prescribed recovery, clear/reset the space, then complete the connected upper-body exercise. Each exercise has its own sets and rest; this is not a superset, continuous kick/throw combination or fatigue circuit. Preserve both-side doses and the longer of the row recovery and the source class’s between-exercise recovery. Allow 10–15 s between upper-body attempts, normally 20 s between lower-body attempts and 60 s for the early-cue lower-body tasks. Extend recovery when quality requires. Primary easy loading sets are separate from working reps. Confirm combined class duration from the selected doses, rest, preparation and actual group flow; original whole-course class durations cannot simply be added or reused. Review other sport/gym/tumbling work and the source roughly 48–72 h planning allowance from comparable demanding exposures. Resume missed classes in sequence instead of doubling up.
rotation-full-body.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1 unchanged; do not recreate it or assign an assumed duration. Review its actual demands before this full-body class. Check the written setup and readiness of the selected kick, landing, handoff and implement tasks.
rotation-full-body.setup: Use the existing separate 10 m lanes. Keep waiting athletes outside the swept-leg, landing and ball paths. For released balls, verify a light grippable implement, permitted low floor target about 2–3 m beyond release, and containment of the entire flight/rebound/roll; use a throwing wall only after verification. Use a non-rebounding slam ball for slams. Clear the area between the leg drill and hand drill of each pair. Pairing is a coaching connection, not simultaneous stations or a throw immediately after a jump. Secure band/rope anchors and the landmine base. Kicks stay below hip height with a soft terminal knee, active recoil and no contact or spinning kick. Handoffs are controlled: secure the grip and wait for the feeder to release and step clear before turning. No new airborne-feed progression is added.
rotation-full-body.quality: Within the scheduled attempts, record each side’s support-foot release, hip-led initiation and controlled finish. Use today’s three connections to identify whether a miss begins at support, transfer or endpoint. Different drills are not equivalent force tests; use observed control and recovery to choose the next appropriate demand.

rotation-full-body.delivery: Plan one integrated class per week. Complete Access & Prepare 1 → six explosive exercises → two light resilience exercises → six primary-strength exercises. In each explosive pair, complete the lower-body exercise with its prescribed recovery, clear/reset the space, then complete the connected upper-body exercise. Each exercise has its own sets and rest; this is not a superset, continuous kick/throw combination or fatigue circuit. Preserve both-side doses and the longer of the row recovery and the source class’s between-exercise recovery. Allow 10–15 s between upper-body attempts, normally 20 s between lower-body attempts and 60 s for the early-cue lower-body tasks. Extend recovery when quality requires. Primary easy loading sets are separate from working reps. Confirm combined class duration from the selected doses, rest, preparation and actual group flow; original whole-course class durations cannot simply be added or reused. Review other sport/gym/tumbling work and the source roughly 48–72 h planning allowance from comparable demanding exposures. Resume missed classes in sequence instead of doubling up.
rotation-full-body.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1 unchanged; do not recreate it or assign an assumed duration. Review its actual demands before this full-body class. Check the written setup and readiness of the selected kick, landing, handoff and implement tasks.
rotation-full-body.setup: Use the existing separate 10 m lanes. Keep waiting athletes outside the swept-leg, landing and ball paths. For released balls, verify a light grippable implement, permitted low floor target about 2–3 m beyond release, and containment of the entire flight/rebound/roll; use a throwing wall only after verification. Use a non-rebounding slam ball for slams. Clear the area between the leg drill and hand drill of each pair. Pairing is a coaching connection, not simultaneous stations or a throw immediately after a jump. Secure band/rope anchors and the landmine base. Kicks stay below hip height with a soft terminal knee, active recoil and no contact or spinning kick. Handoffs are controlled: secure the grip and wait for the feeder to release and step clear before turning. No new airborne-feed progression is added.
rotation-full-body.quality: Within the scheduled attempts, record each side’s support-foot release, hip-led initiation and controlled finish. Use today’s three connections to identify whether a miss begins at support, transfer or endpoint. Different drills are not equivalent force tests; use observed control and recovery to choose the next appropriate demand.

rotation-full-body.progression: Establish the stage’s support and force-transfer connections using both source courses inside this class. Keep the original working doses; qualify the listed range and load before seeking more speed. Review actual attendance, technique, loads, soreness and other training. Each bridge connects two separately coached exercises. Complete all prescribed work and recovery for the first, then clear/reset the area for the second. Never combine a jump or kick with a simultaneous throw. Use the source’s shorter-range, supported, stationary or paused replacement inside the same slot. For handoffs, secure grip and wait for the feeder to step clear; use the existing self-held replacement when needed.
S: One upper-body/trunk and one hip/foot resilience exercise connect control at both ends of the rotational chain. Keep at least 4–5 clean repetitions or about 5 seconds of a sound hold in reserve. Preserve the row’s within-hold relaxation and use the stated side/exercise recovery.
P: Three lower-body and three upper-body/trunk lifts support the class’s force-transfer purpose. Across the first two classes of each stage, every original primary-strength prescription is included once; the additional day selects complementary full-body strength. Perform the listed easy preparation for each lift, with its recovery, before working. Keep 2–3 clean reps in reserve and the source controlled return tempo.

rotation-full-body.title: Full body · Place the base and control supplied force
rotation-full-body.effort: Preserve the output line and recover a repeatable endpoint. Landing gate → one-hand return; Single-leg orientation → constrained handoff; Recovery base → transverse impulse.
rotation-full-body.extension: Expand the stage to its complementary entry, direction or control demands. Transfer the support-and-finish standards from the preceding integrated class; new task demands do not authorize heavier loads.

connections.title: Landing gate → one-hand return
connections.cue: Own the offset stance gate, then use a settled base for the supplied underhand return; reduce the one-hand demand when grip is insecure.

connections.title: Single-leg orientation → constrained handoff

rotation-full-body.delivery: Plan one integrated class per week. Complete Access & Prepare 1 → six explosive exercises → two light resilience exercises → six primary-strength exercises. In each explosive pair, complete the lower-body exercise with its prescribed recovery, clear/reset the space, then complete the connected upper-body exercise. Each exercise has its own sets and rest; this is not a superset, continuous kick/throw combination or fatigue circuit. Preserve both-side doses and the longer of the row recovery and the source class’s between-exercise recovery. Allow 10–15 s between upper-body attempts, normally 20 s between lower-body attempts and 60 s for the early-cue lower-body tasks. Extend recovery when quality requires. Primary easy loading sets are separate from working reps. Confirm combined class duration from the selected doses, rest, preparation and actual group flow; original whole-course class durations cannot simply be added or reused. Review other sport/gym/tumbling work and the source roughly 48–72 h planning allowance from comparable demanding exposures. Resume missed classes in sequence instead of doubling up.
rotation-full-body.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1 unchanged; do not recreate it or assign an assumed duration. Review its actual demands before this full-body class. Check the written setup and readiness of the selected kick, landing, handoff and implement tasks.
rotation-full-body.setup: Use the existing separate 10 m lanes. Keep waiting athletes outside the swept-leg, landing and ball paths. For released balls, verify a light grippable implement, permitted low floor target about 2–3 m beyond release, and containment of the entire flight/rebound/roll; use a throwing wall only after verification. Use a non-rebounding slam ball for slams. Clear the area between the leg drill and hand drill of each pair. Pairing is a coaching connection, not simultaneous stations or a throw immediately after a jump. Secure band/rope anchors and the landmine base. Kicks stay below hip height with a soft terminal knee, active recoil and no contact or spinning kick. Handoffs are controlled: secure the grip and wait for the feeder to release and step clear before turning. No new airborne-feed progression is added.
rotation-full-body.quality: Within the scheduled attempts, record each side’s support-foot release, hip-led initiation and controlled finish. Use today’s three connections to identify whether a miss begins at support, transfer or endpoint. Different drills are not equivalent force tests; use observed control and recovery to choose the next appropriate demand.

Transfer the support-and-finish standards from the preceding integrated class; new task demands do not authorize heavier loads. Each bridge connects two separately coached exercises. Complete all prescribed work and recovery for the first, then clear/reset the area for the second. Never combine a jump or kick with a simultaneous throw. Use the source’s shorter-range, supported, stationary or paused replacement inside the same slot. For handoffs, secure grip and wait for the feeder to step clear; use the existing self-held replacement when needed.
S: One upper-body/trunk and one hip/foot resilience exercise connect control at both ends of the rotational chain. Keep at least 4–5 clean repetitions or about 5 seconds of a sound hold in reserve. Preserve the row’s within-hold relaxation and use the stated side/exercise recovery.
P: Three lower-body and three upper-body/trunk lifts support the class’s force-transfer purpose. Across the first two classes of each stage, every original primary-strength prescription is included once; the additional day selects complementary full-body strength. Perform the listed easy preparation for each lift, with its recovery, before working. Keep 2–3 clean reps in reserve and the source controlled return tempo.

rotation-full-body.delivery: Plan one integrated class per week. Complete Access & Prepare 1 → six explosive exercises → two light resilience exercises → six primary-strength exercises. In each explosive pair, complete the lower-body exercise with its prescribed recovery, clear/reset the space, then complete the connected upper-body exercise. Each exercise has its own sets and rest; this is not a superset, continuous kick/throw combination or fatigue circuit. Preserve both-side doses and the longer of the row recovery and the source class’s between-exercise recovery. Allow 10–15 s between upper-body attempts, normally 20 s between lower-body attempts and 60 s for the early-cue lower-body tasks. Extend recovery when quality requires. Primary easy loading sets are separate from working reps. Confirm combined class duration from the selected doses, rest, preparation and actual group flow; original whole-course class durations cannot simply be added or reused. Review other sport/gym/tumbling work and the source roughly 48–72 h planning allowance from comparable demanding exposures. Resume missed classes in sequence instead of doubling up.
rotation-full-body.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1 unchanged; do not recreate it or assign an assumed duration. Review its actual demands before this full-body class. Check the written setup and readiness of the selected kick, landing, handoff and implement tasks.
rotation-full-body.setup: Use the existing separate 10 m lanes. Keep waiting athletes outside the swept-leg, landing and ball paths. For released balls, verify a light grippable implement, permitted low floor target about 2–3 m beyond release, and containment of the entire flight/rebound/roll; use a throwing wall only after verification. Use a non-rebounding slam ball for slams. Clear the area between the leg drill and hand drill of each pair. Pairing is a coaching connection, not simultaneous stations or a throw immediately after a jump. Secure band/rope anchors and the landmine base. Kicks stay below hip height with a soft terminal knee, active recoil and no contact or spinning kick. Handoffs are controlled: secure the grip and wait for the feeder to release and step clear before turning. No new airborne-feed progression is added.
rotation-full-body.quality: Within the scheduled attempts, record each side’s support-foot release, hip-led initiation and controlled finish. Use today’s three connections to identify whether a miss begins at support, transfer or endpoint. Bring line, endpoint and support recovery together at restrained strength volume. Use a planned kick/throw line, matched chamber/hand stops and a recovery-base/handoff pair. Keep handoffs predictable and every primary lift at one working set before the reference stage.

rotation-full-body.progression: Bring line, endpoint and support recovery together at restrained strength volume. Use a planned kick/throw line, matched chamber/hand stops and a recovery-base/handoff pair. Keep handoffs predictable and every primary lift at one working set before the reference stage. Review actual attendance, technique, loads, soreness and other training. Change one demand only after clean execution at the intended reserve and acceptable recovery; otherwise hold or regress. No athlete completion, readiness or improvement is inferred from a class number.

E: Bring line, endpoint and support recovery together at restrained strength volume. Use a planned kick/throw line, matched chamber/hand stops and a recovery-base/handoff pair. Keep handoffs predictable and every primary lift at one working set before the reference stage.

Each bridge connects two separately coached exercises. Complete all prescribed work and recovery for the first, then clear/reset the area for the second. Never combine a jump or kick with a simultaneous throw. Use the source’s shorter-range, supported, stationary or paused replacement inside the same slot. For handoffs, secure grip and wait for the feeder to step clear; use the existing self-held replacement when needed.
S: One upper-body/trunk and one hip/foot resilience exercise connect control at both ends of the rotational chain. Keep at least 4–5 clean repetitions or about 5 seconds of a sound hold in reserve. Preserve the row’s within-hold relaxation and use the stated side/exercise recovery.
P: Three lower-body and three upper-body/trunk lifts support the class’s force-transfer purpose. Across the first two classes of each stage, every original primary-strength prescription is included once; the additional day selects complementary full-body strength. Perform the listed easy preparation for each lift, with its recovery, before working. Keep 2–3 clean reps in reserve and the source controlled return tempo.

rotation-full-body.delivery: Plan one integrated class per week. Complete Access & Prepare 1 → six explosive exercises → two light resilience exercises → six primary-strength exercises. In each explosive pair, complete the lower-body exercise with its prescribed recovery, clear/reset the space, then complete the connected upper-body exercise. Each exercise has its own sets and rest; this is not a superset, continuous kick/throw combination or fatigue circuit. Preserve both-side doses and the longer of the row recovery and the source class’s between-exercise recovery. Allow 10–15 s between upper-body attempts, normally 20 s between lower-body attempts and 60 s for the early-cue lower-body tasks. Extend recovery when quality requires. Primary easy loading sets are separate from working reps. Confirm combined class duration from the selected doses, rest, preparation and actual group flow; original whole-course class durations cannot simply be added or reused. Review other sport/gym/tumbling work and the source roughly 48–72 h planning allowance from comparable demanding exposures. Resume missed classes in sequence instead of doubling up.
rotation-full-body.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1 unchanged; do not recreate it or assign an assumed duration. Review its actual demands before this full-body class. Check the written setup and readiness of the selected kick, landing, handoff and implement tasks.
rotation-full-body.setup: Use the existing separate 10 m lanes. Keep waiting athletes outside the swept-leg, landing and ball paths. For released balls, verify a light grippable implement, permitted low floor target about 2–3 m beyond release, and containment of the entire flight/rebound/roll; use a throwing wall only after verification. Use a non-rebounding slam ball for slams. Clear the area between the leg drill and hand drill of each pair. Pairing is a coaching connection, not simultaneous stations or a throw immediately after a jump. Secure band/rope anchors and the landmine base. Kicks stay below hip height with a soft terminal knee, active recoil and no contact or spinning kick. Handoffs are controlled: secure the grip and wait for the feeder to release and step clear before turning. No new airborne-feed progression is added.
rotation-full-body.quality: Within the scheduled attempts, record each side’s support-foot release, hip-led initiation and controlled finish. Use today’s three connections to identify whether a miss begins at support, transfer or endpoint. Different drills are not equivalent force tests; use observed control and recovery to choose the next appropriate demand.

rotation-full-body.explosiveNotes: E1/E2 Pivot → paused projection review: Review the original grounded pivot and paused scoop conditions within their scheduled attempts; record the actual setup and finish quality. E3/E4 Kick recovery → pressing finish review: Review low roundhouse recoil and rotational shot-put balance with matched task conditions where possible. rotation-full-body.progression: Establish the stage’s support and force-transfer connections using both source courses inside this class. Keep the original working doses; qualify the listed range and load before seeking more speed. Review actual attendance, technique, loads, soreness and other training. Change one demand only after clean execution at the intended reserve and acceptable recovery; otherwise hold or regress. No athlete completion, readiness or improvement is inferred from a class number.

Each bridge connects two separately coached exercises. Complete all prescribed work and recovery for the first, then clear/reset the area for the second. Never combine a jump or kick with a simultaneous throw. Use the source’s shorter-range, supported, stationary or paused replacement inside the same slot. For handoffs, secure grip and wait for the feeder to step clear; use the existing self-held replacement when needed.
S: One upper-body/trunk and one hip/foot resilience exercise connect control at both ends of the rotational chain. Keep at least 4–5 clean repetitions or about 5 seconds of a sound hold in reserve. Preserve the row’s within-hold relaxation and use the stated side/exercise recovery.
P: Three lower-body and three upper-body/trunk lifts support the class’s force-transfer purpose. Across the first two classes of each stage, every original primary-strength prescription is included once; the additional day selects complementary full-body strength. Perform the listed easy preparation for each lift, with its recovery, before working. Keep 2–3 clean reps in reserve and the source controlled return tempo.

rotation-full-body.title: Full body · Apply the turn after entry and recovery

rotation-full-body.extension: Expand the stage to its complementary entry, direction or control demands. Transfer the support-and-finish standards from the preceding integrated class; new task demands do not authorize heavier loads.

connections.title: Gathered entry → supplied lateral entry

rotation-full-body.delivery: Plan one integrated class per week. Complete Access & Prepare 1 → six explosive exercises → two light resilience exercises → six primary-strength exercises. In each explosive pair, complete the lower-body exercise with its prescribed recovery, clear/reset the space, then complete the connected upper-body exercise. Each exercise has its own sets and rest; this is not a superset, continuous kick/throw combination or fatigue circuit. Preserve both-side doses and the longer of the row recovery and the source class’s between-exercise recovery. Allow 10–15 s between upper-body attempts, normally 20 s between lower-body attempts and 60 s for the early-cue lower-body tasks. Extend recovery when quality requires. Primary easy loading sets are separate from working reps. Confirm combined class duration from the selected doses, rest, preparation and actual group flow; original whole-course class durations cannot simply be added or reused. Review other sport/gym/tumbling work and the source roughly 48–72 h planning allowance from comparable demanding exposures. Resume missed classes in sequence instead of doubling up.
rotation-full-body.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1 unchanged; do not recreate it or assign an assumed duration. Review its actual demands before this full-body class. Check the written setup and readiness of the selected kick, landing, handoff and implement tasks.
rotation-full-body.setup: Use the existing separate 10 m lanes. Keep waiting athletes outside the swept-leg, landing and ball paths. For released balls, verify a light grippable implement, permitted low floor target about 2–3 m beyond release, and containment of the entire flight/rebound/roll; use a throwing wall only after verification. Use a non-rebounding slam ball for slams. Clear the area between the leg drill and hand drill of each pair. Pairing is a coaching connection, not simultaneous stations or a throw immediately after a jump. Secure band/rope anchors and the landmine base. Kicks stay below hip height with a soft terminal knee, active recoil and no contact or spinning kick. Handoffs are controlled: secure the grip and wait for the feeder to release and step clear before turning. No new airborne-feed progression is added.
rotation-full-body.quality: Within the scheduled attempts, record each side’s support-foot release, hip-led initiation and controlled finish. Use today’s three connections to identify whether a miss begins at support, transfer or endpoint. Different drills are not equivalent force tests; use observed control and recovery to choose the next appropriate demand.

rotation-full-body.delivery: Plan one integrated class per week. Complete Access & Prepare 1 → six explosive exercises → two light resilience exercises → six primary-strength exercises. In each explosive pair, complete the lower-body exercise with its prescribed recovery, clear/reset the space, then complete the connected upper-body exercise. Each exercise has its own sets and rest; this is not a superset, continuous kick/throw combination or fatigue circuit. Preserve both-side doses and the longer of the row recovery and the source class’s between-exercise recovery. Allow 10–15 s between upper-body attempts, normally 20 s between lower-body attempts and 60 s for the early-cue lower-body tasks. Extend recovery when quality requires. Primary easy loading sets are separate from working reps. Confirm combined class duration from the selected doses, rest, preparation and actual group flow; original whole-course class durations cannot simply be added or reused. Review other sport/gym/tumbling work and the source roughly 48–72 h planning allowance from comparable demanding exposures. Resume missed classes in sequence instead of doubling up.
rotation-full-body.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1 unchanged; do not recreate it or assign an assumed duration. rotation-full-body.setup: Use the existing separate 10 m lanes. Keep waiting athletes outside the swept-leg, landing and ball paths. For released balls, verify a light grippable implement, permitted low floor target about 2–3 m beyond release, and containment of the entire flight/rebound/roll; use a throwing wall only after verification. Use a non-rebounding slam ball for slams. Clear the area between the leg drill and hand drill of each pair. Pairing is a coaching connection, not simultaneous stations or a throw immediately after a jump. Secure band/rope anchors and the landmine base. Kicks stay below hip height with a soft terminal knee, active recoil and no contact or spinning kick. Handoffs are controlled: secure the grip and wait for the feeder to release and step clear before turning. No new airborne-feed progression is added.
rotation-full-body.quality: Compare with Week 3 only when equipment, ball mass, target, stance, turn range, pair order, doses and recovery match. Observe scheduled attempts only. full-body-force.delivery: Estimate 67–73 minutes after Access & Prepare 1 with prompt equipment access. Includes selected work, resets, side/set recovery, new-order transitions, same-lift preparation and 12–18 minutes extra instruction/setup. Additional recovery, queues or load finding add actual time. Existing preparation and complete booking duration remain unresolved. Never shorten needed recovery to fit a clock. Class numbers specify 36 ordered exposures, not consecutive days or a fixed 36-week calendar. Review actual sport, lifting, throwing, kicking, running, jumping and separate tumbling before scheduling. Roughly 48–72 hours between comparably demanding exposures is an initial planning allowance, adjusted to actual recovery. Do not also perform the standalone source workouts or double up missed classes. No athlete completion or readiness is inferred from a saved class.
full-body-force.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1, unchanged and supplied separately. Its exercises, duration and workload are not recreated or assumed. Review its actual demands before this full-body class.
full-body-force.setup: Inspect all loads, stable supports, band/landmine attachments, surfaces and athlete fit. Use the three separate 10 m lanes with complete setup, action and receiving/stopping envelopes inside the available space; do not combine them into a 30 m runway. Clear waiting/return paths outside active ball and swept-leg areas. Ball flight, impact, bounce and roll containment require a separately verified area; no throwing wall or rebound behavior is assumed. Low kicks are noncontact and below hip height, with active recoil and no knee snap or spin; qualify kicking competence during the prescribed first attempts. For a handoff, secure the ball and let the feeder release and step clear before turning; no airborne feed is added. Finish each exercise and its recovery, then clear/reset the area before the next. Mechanical connections do not authorize simultaneous jump/kick/throw combinations or supersets. Before multiple substitutions, check that they do not duplicate another slot; otherwise stop the affected work and record a modified/incomplete delivery for revision. Only tasks that explicitly prescribe a feed or receiving action include it; all other releases are no-catch. Retrieve only after the ball stops and the coach clears entry into the area.
full-body-force.quality: Main observation: Squat Jump — settled quarter-squat start. Within its listed attempts, record the declared starting position, side, movement/receiving control and a stable finish. Also record the partner task in the first connection under its own criteria; do not treat unlike drills as equivalent force tests. A miss consumes the attempt; no additional testing slots or retries are added.
full-body-force.explosiveNotes: Open with Squat Jump — settled quarter-squat start as the controlled lower-body force anchor. Start a decisive upward leg push before a still-base forward release.
full-body-force.progression:
Squat Jump — settled quarter-squat start establishes the still-start vertical-force reference, paired with Medicine Ball Chest Pass — stationary, paused for a still-base forward release. The grounded hip pivot and paused rotational scoop add turn initiation without a kick or additional foot reception. Prescribed baseline: 13 ball releases, 6 bilateral foot-landing events, 0 bilateral hand-receiving events. Before delivery, review actual recent loading and recovery; require the held squat start without a second dip, a controlled two-foot finish and a quiet-trunk chest release. If flight cannot be controlled, use the listed fast nonflight squat rise for only the remaining E1 attempts and record removed landings; keep full resets and add no test attempts.

This is the first combined prescription; the source courses are written references, not evidence that these athletes completed them. Original force doses/within-task recovery and same-lift preparation are retained; rotational additions are separately reduced. Advance only after actual controlled execution at the target reserve and satisfactory recovery. Hold, reduce or revise if feedback or first-attempt quality does not support the new constraint.

E: Six separate explosive tasks: two upper force, two lower force, one upper rotation and one lower rotation. The opener is today’s main quality observation; every other task has a specific supporting job. Use bodyweight/light resistance and rapid intent with controlled execution, preserving the written reset and side/set recovery. Extend rest to 2–3 minutes when needed. A miss consumes the attempt; no bonus test or make-up reps.

Stop for pain, unsafe implement path, trapped support knee, uncontrolled reception, lost alignment or clear slowing. Regress only remaining work when control returns; otherwise log the stopped slot. Source alternative doses are capped by the remaining combined dose. No new flight is added by the rotational selections.
S: Exactly two light strengthening tasks, one for each region. Keep at least 5 technical reps/cycles in reserve; do not chase burn or fatigue. Preserve the source tempo and any counted hold/relaxation. Stop or reduce range/load if control fades.
P: Six challenging primary-strength tasks: two from each force course plus one upper and one lower rotational support. Use about 2–3 technical reps/cycles in reserve with controlled lowering/range. No forced reps, failure/max testing or breathless circuit. Same-lift preparation is separate from working sets; extra load finding adds actual work/time.

The original force-course doses and preparation stay with their source exercises. Added rotational support uses the clearly stated smaller combined dose and its own easy preparation. A new class or changed position in the sequence does not justify a load increase. Judge late-session technical reserve and record reductions rather than forcing nominal completion.

connections.title: Settled force onset
connections.cue: Squat Jump — settled quarter-squat start and Medicine Ball Chest Pass — stationary, paused: Settle the body and load before accelerating; use the same clear start discipline for upward leg projection and forward hand release.

connections.title: Force through a stable finish
connections.cue: Calf Raise — rapid supported rise, no flight and Band Row — seated, fast pull: Keep the support base organized while force builds toward the ankle-rise or arm-draw finish; reset without rocking the torso.

connections.title: Hip initiation into hand force
connections.cue: Split-stance explosive hip pivot and Med Ball Rotational Scoop Toss — paused standing start; floor-target adaptation: Settled rotational projection beside an isolated grounded hip/foot initiation.

exercises.rest: 90 s between complete set rounds; 10 s between individual reps; 90 s before the next exercise/section
exercises.purpose: Main knee/hip force from a still start, expressed vertically. Hold a comfortable quarter squat 2 s with hands at hips; jump vertically without another dip, land on both feet with yielding knees and hold 2 s. Keep jump height within a controlled reception. Use instead: a smaller same-start jump; if flight cannot be controlled, a fast nonflight squat rise at the same dose and zero landings. exercises.name: Split-stance explosive hip pivot
exercises.dose: 1 × 2 per side/direction
exercises.prescription: 1 × 2 per side/direction
exercises.rest: 60 s between side/direction bouts; 4 total reps; 20 s between individual reps; 90 s before the next exercise/section
exercises.purpose: Isolate the support-foot release and rapid hip-turn initiation before adding a swinging leg. Start in a short split stance. Rapidly shift toward the lead leg and turn feet and pelvis together through a comfortable arc of about 45 degrees or less. Both forefeet remain grounded as the heels may release. Finish still for 2 seconds. Mirror stance and direction for the other side; no kick or jump. Let the support foot or both feet turn freely with the pelvis; never force rotation through a trapped knee. Remain grounded. Use instead: Reduce the turn size if a foot sticks, knee twists or the trunk leads. Stop the task if the surface does not permit a controlled foot-and-hip pivot. Apply this change only to the same remaining combined dose and recovery; it replaces the original execution and adds no extra task or make-up attempts. This replacement uses only the remaining combined dose/rest unless explicitly stated; log changed support, event type, load and added time.

exercises.name: Med Ball Rotational Scoop Toss — paused standing start; floor-target adaptation
exercises.sourceName: Med Ball Rotational Scoop Toss — paused standing start; floor-target adaptation
exercises.dose: 1 × 2 per side/direction
exercises.prescription: 1 × 2 per side/direction
exercises.rest: 90 s between side/direction bouts; 4 total reps; 15 s between individual reps; 90 s before the next exercise/section
exercises.purpose: Generate rotational projection from a settled load. Stand side-on at comfortable athletic width with a light ball beside the rear hip. Pause 2 seconds, pivot the rear foot, turn hips and trunk, then sweep both hands into the low forward target. No bounce, countermovement or step. Hold the balanced finish for 2 seconds. Use a light grippable ball and a verified low target in a permitted, fully contained release area; keep the entire flight, rebound and roll clear of people. Stay grounded, and do not receive a rebound. Use instead: Reduce ball mass or turn range for arm-first movement or loss of balance; retain the paused grounded scoop. If the release area cannot be qualified, stop and re-audit this slot rather than throw into an unsafe area. Apply this change only to the same remaining combined dose and recovery; it replaces the original execution and adds no extra task or make-up attempts. exercises.name: Scapular Push-Up — quadruped, dynamic
exercises.rest: 45 s before the next exercise/section
exercises.purpose: Keep this light support at ≥5 technical RIR. Strengthen controlled shoulder-blade travel against light bodyweight so the chest-pass finish and push-up support do not depend on elbow bending or trunk sag. Hands and knees remain down; keep elbows straight, let the chest settle slightly, then push the floor away. Use 2 seconds inward, 2 seconds outward and a 2-second finish hold. Stop for shrugging, elbow bend or lumbar movement. Use instead: a smaller controlled shoulder-blade excursion at the same easy dose; do not turn it into an elbow-bending push-up. This replacement uses only the remaining combined dose/rest unless explicitly stated; log changed support, event type, load and added time.

exercises.name: Seated band hip internal rotation
exercises.dose: 1 × 5 per side/direction
exercises.prescription: 1 × 5 per side/direction
exercises.rest: 60 s between side bouts; 10 total reps; 90 s before the next lift preparation
exercises.purpose: Keep the working load at 2–3 technical reps/cycles in reserve. Load controlled internal-rotation torque directly at the hip, complementing the larger leg push used to organise the selected grounded lower turn. full-body-force.title: Grounded hip drive and fast traction
full-body-force.effort: Drive the hips sharply while expressing a quick arm pull and controlled hand push-off.
full-body-force.delivery: Estimate 68–75 minutes after Access & Prepare 1 with prompt equipment access. Includes selected work, resets, side/set recovery, new-order transitions, same-lift preparation and 12–18 minutes extra instruction/setup. Additional recovery, queues or load finding add actual time. Existing preparation and complete booking duration remain unresolved. Never shorten needed recovery to fit a clock. Class numbers specify 36 ordered exposures, not consecutive days or a fixed 36-week calendar. Review actual sport, lifting, throwing, kicking, running, jumping and separate tumbling before scheduling. Roughly 48–72 hours between comparably demanding exposures is an initial planning allowance, adjusted to actual recovery. Do not also perform the standalone source workouts or double up missed classes. No athlete completion or readiness is inferred from a saved class.
full-body-force.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1, unchanged and supplied separately. Its exercises, duration and workload are not recreated or assumed. Review its actual demands before this full-body class.
full-body-force.setup: Inspect all loads, stable supports, band/landmine attachments, surfaces and athlete fit. Use the three separate 10 m lanes with complete setup, action and receiving/stopping envelopes inside the available space; do not combine them into a 30 m runway. Clear waiting/return paths outside active ball and swept-leg areas. Ball flight, impact, bounce and roll containment require a separately verified area; no throwing wall or rebound behavior is assumed. Only tasks that explicitly prescribe a feed or receiving action include it; all other releases are no-catch. Retrieve only after the ball stops and the coach clears entry into the area. Low kicks are noncontact and below hip height, with active recoil and no knee snap or spin; qualify kicking competence during the prescribed first attempts. For a handoff, secure the ball and let the feeder release and step clear before turning; no airborne feed is added. Finish each exercise and its recovery, then clear/reset the area before the next. Mechanical connections do not authorize simultaneous jump/kick/throw combinations or supersets. Before multiple substitutions, check that they do not duplicate another slot; otherwise stop the affected work and record a modified/incomplete delivery for revision.
full-body-force.quality: Main observation: Two-Hand Landmine Bent-Over Row — fast pull from a pause. Within its listed attempts, record the declared starting position, side, movement/receiving control and a stable finish. Also record the partner task in the first connection under its own criteria; do not treat unlike drills as equivalent force tests. A miss consumes the attempt; no additional testing slots or retries are added.
full-body-force.explosiveNotes: Open with Two-Hand Landmine Bent-Over Row — fast pull from a pause as the controlled upper-body force anchor. Drive the hips sharply while expressing a quick arm pull and controlled hand push-off.
full-body-force.progression:
Two-Hand Landmine Bent-Over Row — fast pull from a pause moves the observation to rapid traction from a settled load; Kettlebell Swing — dead-stop two-hand repetitions supplies deliberate hip acceleration from a parked bell. This separates trunk-still arm force from hip-driven force, while Plyo Push-Up — hands elevated introduces a small hand-receiving dose and the lower rotation slot introduces a low actively recoiled kick. Compared with Class 1, prescribed ball releases change from 13 to 7, bilateral foot-landing events change from 6 to 0, bilateral hand-receiving events change from 0 to 3. With actual recovery reviewed, require a steady row hinge, a controlled bell park and soft hand reception before another effort. If the landmine load or grip is unsuitable, use the listed seated bilateral band row with its settled start for remaining row attempts; if hand reception is unqualified, use the listed nonflight incline push-up for remaining E3 work and log zero hand receptions.

Previous combined Class 1 prescribed 9 primary bouts and 56 conventional/traverse reps plus 0 cycles; this class prescribes 12 bouts, 64 reps and 3 cycles. This is a redistributed task dose, not an earned load increase. Original force doses/within-task recovery and same-lift preparation are retained; rotational additions are separately reduced. Advance only after actual controlled execution at the target reserve and satisfactory recovery. Hold, reduce or revise if feedback or first-attempt quality does not support the new constraint.

E: Six separate explosive tasks: two upper force, two lower force, one upper rotation and one lower rotation. The opener is today’s main quality observation; every other task has a specific supporting job. Use bodyweight/light resistance and rapid intent with controlled execution, preserving the written reset and side/set recovery. Extend rest to 2–3 minutes when needed. A miss consumes the attempt; no bonus test or make-up reps.

Stop for pain, unsafe implement path, trapped support knee, uncontrolled reception, lost alignment or clear slowing. Regress only remaining work when control returns; otherwise log the stopped slot. Source alternative doses are capped by the remaining combined dose. No new flight is added by the rotational selections.
S: Exactly two light strengthening tasks, one for each region. Keep at least 5 technical reps/cycles in reserve; do not chase burn or fatigue. Preserve the source tempo and any counted hold/relaxation. Stop or reduce range/load if control fades.
P: Six challenging primary-strength tasks: two from each force course plus one upper and one lower rotational support. Use about 2–3 technical reps/cycles in reserve with controlled lowering/range. No forced reps, failure/max testing or breathless circuit. Same-lift preparation is separate from working sets; extra load finding adds actual work/time.

The original force-course doses and preparation stay with their source exercises. Added rotational support uses the clearly stated smaller combined dose and its own easy preparation. A new class or changed position in the sequence does not justify a load increase. Judge late-session technical reserve and record reductions rather than forcing nominal completion.
