full-body-force.title: Cued arm force and grounded leg reversal
full-body-force.effort: Express force from a clear cue or controlled reversal while retaining grounded support.
full-body-force.delivery: Estimate 64–71 minutes after Access & Prepare 1 with prompt equipment access. Includes selected work, resets, side/set recovery, new-order transitions, same-lift preparation and 12–18 minutes extra instruction/setup. Additional recovery, queues or load finding add actual time. Existing preparation and complete booking duration remain unresolved. Never shorten needed recovery to fit a clock. Class numbers specify 36 ordered exposures, not consecutive days or a fixed 36-week calendar. Review actual sport, lifting, throwing, kicking, running, jumping and separate tumbling before scheduling. Roughly 48–72 hours between comparably demanding exposures is an initial planning allowance, adjusted to actual recovery. Do not also perform the standalone source workouts or double up missed classes. No athlete completion or readiness is inferred from a saved class.
full-body-force.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1, unchanged and supplied separately. Its exercises, duration and workload are not recreated or assumed. Review its actual demands before this full-body class.
full-body-force.setup: Inspect all loads, stable supports, band/landmine attachments, surfaces and athlete fit. Use the three separate 10 m lanes with complete setup, action and receiving/stopping envelopes inside the available space; do not combine them into a 30 m runway. Clear waiting/return paths outside active ball and swept-leg areas. Ball flight, impact, bounce and roll containment require a separately verified area; no throwing wall or rebound behavior is assumed. Only tasks that explicitly prescribe a feed or receiving action include it; all other releases are no-catch. Retrieve only after the ball stops and the coach clears entry into the area. Low kicks are noncontact and below hip height, with active recoil and no knee snap or spin; qualify kicking competence during the prescribed first attempts. For a handoff, secure the ball and let the feeder release and step clear before turning; no airborne feed is added. Finish each exercise and its recovery, then clear/reset the area before the next. Mechanical connections do not authorize simultaneous jump/kick/throw combinations or supersets. Before multiple substitutions, check that they do not duplicate another slot; otherwise stop the affected work and record a modified/incomplete delivery for revision.
full-body-force.quality: Main observation: Single-Arm Band Chest Press — still start on a spoken cue. Within its listed attempts, record the declared starting position, side, movement/receiving control and a stable finish. Also record the partner task in the first connection under its own criteria; do not treat unlike drills as equivalent force tests. A miss consumes the attempt; no additional testing slots or retries are added.
full-body-force.explosiveNotes: Open with Single-Arm Band Chest Press — still start on a spoken cue as the controlled upper-body force anchor. Express force from a clear cue or controlled reversal while retaining grounded support.
full-body-force.progression:
Single-Arm Band Chest Press — still start on a spoken cue applies the spoken start cue to one independent arm with a fixed trunk; Step-Down to Step-Up — quick grounded reversal retains the grounded step reversal at one repetition per leg. The familiar body-assisted row and bridge preserve hip-force support, while the short drop-step kick changes how support is loaded before the lower turn and the resisted cross stays familiar. Compared with Class 31, prescribed ball releases change from 8 to 0, bilateral foot-landing events change from 4 to 0, airborne feed catches change from 4 to 0, secure handoffs change from 4 to 0. Require actual recovery, a cue wait that preserves band tension and posture, and a grounded reversal without bouncing from the floor foot. Use a self-initiated single-arm band press for remaining E1 attempts if cue timing disrupts posture; use the listed shallow supported single-leg lower-and-rise for remaining E2 attempts if step geometry is unsuitable. Shorten remaining drop steps when needed and do not increase their speed and length together.

Previous combined Class 31 prescribed 9 primary bouts and 51 conventional/traverse reps plus 0 cycles; this class prescribes 11 bouts, 55 reps and 2 cycles. This is a redistributed task dose, not an earned load increase. Original force doses/within-task recovery and same-lift preparation are retained; rotational additions are separately reduced. Advance only after actual controlled execution at the target reserve and satisfactory recovery. Hold, reduce or revise if feedback or first-attempt quality does not support the new constraint.

E: Six separate explosive tasks: two upper force, two lower force, one upper rotation and one lower rotation. The opener is today’s main quality observation; every other task has a specific supporting job. Use bodyweight/light resistance and rapid intent with controlled execution, preserving the written reset and side/set recovery. Extend rest to 2–3 minutes when needed. A miss consumes the attempt; no bonus test or make-up reps.

Stop for pain, unsafe implement path, trapped support knee, uncontrolled reception, lost alignment or clear slowing. Regress only remaining work when control returns; otherwise log the stopped slot. Source alternative doses are capped by the remaining combined dose. No new flight is added by the rotational selections.
S: Exactly two light strengthening tasks, one for each region. Keep at least 5 technical reps/cycles in reserve; do not chase burn or fatigue. Preserve the source tempo and any counted hold/relaxation. Stop or reduce range/load if control fades.
P: Six challenging primary-strength tasks: two from each force course plus one upper and one lower rotational support. Use about 2–3 technical reps/cycles in reserve with controlled lowering/range. No forced reps, failure/max testing or breathless circuit. Same-lift preparation is separate from working sets; extra load finding adds actual work/time.

The original force-course doses and preparation stay with their source exercises. Added rotational support uses the clearly stated smaller combined dose and its own easy preparation. A new class or changed position in the sequence does not justify a load increase. Judge late-session technical reserve and record reductions rather than forcing nominal completion.

full-body-force.delivery: Estimate 57–64 minutes after Access & Prepare 1 with prompt equipment access. Includes selected work, resets, side/set recovery, new-order transitions, same-lift preparation and 12–18 minutes extra instruction/setup. Additional recovery, queues or load finding add actual time. Existing preparation and complete booking duration remain unresolved. Never shorten needed recovery to fit a clock. Class numbers specify 36 ordered exposures, not consecutive days or a fixed 36-week calendar. Review actual sport, lifting, throwing, kicking, running, jumping and separate tumbling before scheduling. Roughly 48–72 hours between comparably demanding exposures is an initial planning allowance, adjusted to actual recovery. Do not also perform the standalone source workouts or double up missed classes. No athlete completion or readiness is inferred from a saved class.
full-body-force.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1, unchanged and supplied separately. Its exercises, duration and workload are not recreated or assumed. Review its actual demands before this full-body class.
full-body-force.setup: Inspect all loads, stable supports, band/landmine attachments, surfaces and athlete fit. Use the three separate 10 m lanes with complete setup, action and receiving/stopping envelopes inside the available space; do not combine them into a 30 m runway. Clear waiting/return paths outside active ball and swept-leg areas. Ball flight, impact, bounce and roll containment require a separately verified area; no throwing wall or rebound behavior is assumed. Only tasks that explicitly prescribe a feed or receiving action include it; all other releases are no-catch. Retrieve only after the ball stops and the coach clears entry into the area. Low kicks are noncontact and below hip height, with active recoil and no knee snap or spin; qualify kicking competence during the prescribed first attempts. For a handoff, secure the ball and let the feeder release and step clear before turning; no airborne feed is added. Finish each exercise and its recovery, then clear/reset the area before the next. Mechanical connections do not authorize simultaneous jump/kick/throw combinations or supersets. Before multiple substitutions, check that they do not duplicate another slot; otherwise stop the affected work and record a modified/incomplete delivery for revision.
full-body-force.quality: Main observation: Crossover recovery to a marked kick base. Within its listed attempts, record the declared starting position, side, movement/receiving control and a stable finish. Also record the partner task in the first connection under its own criteria; do not treat unlike drills as equivalent force tests. A miss consumes the attempt; no additional testing slots or retries are added.

full-body-force.progression:
Crossover recovery to a marked kick base emphasizes uncrossing into a marked rotational base; Step-in rotational medicine-ball shot-put retains a self-held step-to-press release instead of adding another supplied-ball sequence. The closing contact pair combines four low pogo receptions in two reset pairs with three separately reset hand receptions, so foot and hand receiving remain separate doses. Compared with Class 32, prescribed ball releases change from 0 to 9, bilateral foot-landing events change from 0 to 4, bilateral hand-receiving events change from 0 to 3. Use the listed isolated supported calf rises for remaining E5 attempts if rhythm fails, and nonflight incline push-ups for remaining E6 attempts if hand reception is unqualified; record each removed event type and preserve the specified resets.

full-body-force.title: Review still-start force
full-body-force.effort: Review the combined program's opening lower and upper still-start tasks under recorded matching conditions.
full-body-force.delivery: Estimate 63–70 minutes after Access & Prepare 1 with prompt equipment access. Includes selected work, resets, side/set recovery, new-order transitions, same-lift preparation and 12–18 minutes extra instruction/setup. Additional recovery, queues or load finding add actual time. Existing preparation and complete booking duration remain unresolved. Never shorten needed recovery to fit a clock. Class numbers specify 36 ordered exposures, not consecutive days or a fixed 36-week calendar. Review actual sport, lifting, throwing, kicking, running, jumping and separate tumbling before scheduling. Roughly 48–72 hours between comparably demanding exposures is an initial planning allowance, adjusted to actual recovery. Do not also perform the standalone source workouts or double up missed classes. No athlete completion or readiness is inferred from a saved class.
full-body-force.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1, unchanged and supplied separately. Its exercises, duration and workload are not recreated or assumed. Review its actual demands before this full-body class.
full-body-force.setup: Inspect all loads, stable supports, band/landmine attachments, surfaces and athlete fit. Use the three separate 10 m lanes with complete setup, action and receiving/stopping envelopes inside the available space; do not combine them into a 30 m runway. Clear waiting/return paths outside active ball and swept-leg areas. Ball flight, impact, bounce and roll containment require a separately verified area; no throwing wall or rebound behavior is assumed. Only tasks that explicitly prescribe a feed or receiving action include it; all other releases are no-catch. Retrieve only after the ball stops and the coach clears entry into the area. Low kicks are noncontact and below hip height, with active recoil and no knee snap or spin; qualify kicking competence during the prescribed first attempts. For a handoff, secure the ball and let the feeder release and step clear before turning; no airborne feed is added. Finish each exercise and its recovery, then clear/reset the area before the next. Mechanical connections do not authorize simultaneous jump/kick/throw combinations or supersets. Before multiple substitutions, check that they do not duplicate another slot; otherwise stop the affected work and record a modified/incomplete delivery for revision.
full-body-force.quality: Main observation: Squat Jump — settled quarter-squat start. Within its listed attempts, record the declared starting position, side, movement/receiving control and a stable finish. Also record the partner task in the first connection under its own criteria; do not treat unlike drills as equivalent force tests. For a repeated source reference, compare only an actually recorded earlier combined occurrence with matching dose, actual equipment, stance, arm strategy, range, reset, side/set rest, preparation and order. An unmatched or missing baseline is not zero or improvement. E1 matches the prescribed execution/dose in combined Class 1; E2 matches the prescribed execution/dose in combined Class 1; E3 matches the prescribed execution/dose in combined Class 16; E5 matches the prescribed execution/dose in combined Class 1; E6 matches the prescribed execution/dose in combined Class 1. A miss consumes the attempt; no additional testing slots or retries are added.
full-body-force.explosiveNotes: Open with Squat Jump — settled quarter-squat start as the controlled lower-body force anchor. Review the combined program's opening lower and upper still-start tasks under recorded matching conditions. Review current quality under matched recorded conditions where available; do not infer improvement from absent baseline data.
full-body-force.progression:
Squat Jump — settled quarter-squat start and Medicine Ball Chest Pass — stationary, paused restore the combined opening class's first two tasks, order and anchor doses: six settled-start jumps and nine stationary chest releases. The small hip pivot and paused rotational scoop are familiar support references; their preceding accessory work differs from Class 1, so they do not by themselves form a controlled before/after test. Compared with Class 33, prescribed ball releases change from 9 to 13, bilateral foot-landing events change from 4 to 6, bilateral hand-receiving events change from 3 to 0. Delivery requires actual recovery and matched recorded setup, surface, ball, technique, preparation and rest before comparing the opening anchors. If those earlier observations do not exist, record current quality only. Use the listed smaller jump or nonflight rise for remaining E1 attempts and the secured bilateral band chest press for remaining E2 attempts when release containment fails; mark changed comparison conditions and add no test attempts.

Previous combined Class 33 prescribed 9 primary bouts and 48 conventional/traverse reps plus 0 cycles; this class prescribes 8 bouts, 47 reps and 0 cycles. This is a redistributed task dose, not an earned load increase. Original force doses/within-task recovery and same-lift preparation are retained; rotational additions are separately reduced. Advance only after actual controlled execution at the target reserve and satisfactory recovery. Hold, reduce or revise if feedback or first-attempt quality does not support the new constraint.

E: Six separate explosive tasks: two upper force, two lower force, one upper rotation and one lower rotation. The opener is today’s main quality observation; every other task has a specific supporting job. Use bodyweight/light resistance and rapid intent with controlled execution, preserving the written reset and side/set recovery. Extend rest to 2–3 minutes when needed. A miss consumes the attempt; no bonus test or make-up reps.

Stop for pain, unsafe implement path, trapped support knee, uncontrolled reception, lost alignment or clear slowing. Regress only remaining work when control returns; otherwise log the stopped slot. Source alternative doses are capped by the remaining combined dose. No new flight is added by the rotational selections.
S: Exactly two light strengthening tasks, one for each region. Keep at least 5 technical reps/cycles in reserve; do not chase burn or fatigue. Preserve the source tempo and any counted hold/relaxation. Stop or reduce range/load if control fades.
P: Six challenging primary-strength tasks: two from each force course plus one upper and one lower rotational support. Use about 2–3 technical reps/cycles in reserve with controlled lowering/range. No forced reps, failure/max testing or breathless circuit. Same-lift preparation is separate from working sets; extra load finding adds actual work/time.

full-body-force.title: Review fixed-base independent force
full-body-force.effort: Review independent arm force and a grounded hip-driven projection with controlled starts.
full-body-force.delivery: Estimate 63–70 minutes after Access & Prepare 1 with prompt equipment access. Includes selected work, resets, side/set recovery, new-order transitions, same-lift preparation and 12–18 minutes extra instruction/setup. Additional recovery, queues or load finding add actual time. Existing preparation and complete booking duration remain unresolved. Never shorten needed recovery to fit a clock. Class numbers specify 36 ordered exposures, not consecutive days or a fixed 36-week calendar. Review actual sport, lifting, throwing, kicking, running, jumping and separate tumbling before scheduling. Roughly 48–72 hours between comparably demanding exposures is an initial planning allowance, adjusted to actual recovery. Do not also perform the standalone source workouts or double up missed classes. No athlete completion or readiness is inferred from a saved class.
full-body-force.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1, unchanged and supplied separately. Its exercises, duration and workload are not recreated or assumed. Review its actual demands before this full-body class.
full-body-force.setup: Inspect all loads, stable supports, band/landmine attachments, surfaces and athlete fit. Use the three separate 10 m lanes with complete setup, action and receiving/stopping envelopes inside the available space; do not combine them into a 30 m runway. Clear waiting/return paths outside active ball and swept-leg areas. Ball flight, impact, bounce and roll containment require a separately verified area; no throwing wall or rebound behavior is assumed. Only tasks that explicitly prescribe a feed or receiving action include it; all other releases are no-catch. Retrieve only after the ball stops and the coach clears entry into the area. Low kicks are noncontact and below hip height, with active recoil and no knee snap or spin; qualify kicking competence during the prescribed first attempts. For a handoff, secure the ball and let the feeder release and step clear before turning; no airborne feed is added. Finish each exercise and its recovery, then clear/reset the area before the next. Mechanical connections do not authorize simultaneous jump/kick/throw combinations or supersets. Before multiple substitutions, check that they do not duplicate another slot; otherwise stop the affected work and record a modified/incomplete delivery for revision.
full-body-force.quality: Main observation: Single-Arm Band Chest Press — still start on a spoken cue. Within its listed attempts, record the declared starting position, side, movement/receiving control and a stable finish. Also record the partner task in the first connection under its own criteria; do not treat unlike drills as equivalent force tests. For a repeated source reference, compare only an actually recorded earlier combined occurrence with matching dose, actual equipment, stance, arm strategy, range, reset, side/set rest, preparation and order. An unmatched or missing baseline is not zero or improvement. E1 matches the prescribed execution/dose in combined Class 32; E2 matches the prescribed execution/dose in combined Class 11; E5 matches the prescribed execution/dose in combined Class 2. A miss consumes the attempt; no additional testing slots or retries are added.
full-body-force.explosiveNotes: Open with Single-Arm Band Chest Press — still start on a spoken cue as the controlled upper-body force anchor. Review independent arm force and a grounded hip-driven projection with controlled starts. Review current quality under matched recorded conditions where available; do not infer improvement from absent baseline data.
full-body-force.progression:
Single-Arm Band Chest Press — still start on a spoken cue retains the cued independent press from Class 32, while One-Arm Row — supported mid-range pause into fast finish adds a supported held-mid-range start to the final arm draw. The parked hip impulse and small forward scoop retain familiar force routes; the returning low roundhouse uses a familiar task and dose, but preceding work differs from its earlier prescription. Compared with Class 34, prescribed ball releases change from 13 to 6, bilateral foot-landing events change from 6 to 0, kick actions change from 0 to 4. Review actual recovery, require the held row without shoulder roll and the kick to recoil into a balanced stance, and compare only fully documented like conditions. Use a self-initiated press for remaining E1 attempts if the cue disrupts control, a full-range supported speed row for remaining E3 attempts if the partial start is strained, and a shorter kick arc for remaining E5 attempts when needed. Log those as changed executions, not matched improvement.

Previous combined Class 34 prescribed 8 primary bouts and 47 conventional/traverse reps plus 0 cycles; this class prescribes 11 bouts, 57 reps and 2 cycles. This is a redistributed task dose, not an earned load increase. Original force doses/within-task recovery and same-lift preparation are retained; rotational additions are separately reduced. Advance only after actual controlled execution at the target reserve and satisfactory recovery. Hold, reduce or revise if feedback or first-attempt quality does not support the new constraint.

E: Six separate explosive tasks: two upper force, two lower force, one upper rotation and one lower rotation. The opener is today’s main quality observation; every other task has a specific supporting job. Use bodyweight/light resistance and rapid intent with controlled execution, preserving the written reset and side/set recovery. Extend rest to 2–3 minutes when needed. A miss consumes the attempt; no bonus test or make-up reps.

Stop for pain, unsafe implement path, trapped support knee, uncontrolled reception, lost alignment or clear slowing. Regress only remaining work when control returns; otherwise log the stopped slot. Source alternative doses are capped by the remaining combined dose. No new flight is added by the rotational selections.
S: Exactly two light strengthening tasks, one for each region. Keep at least 5 technical reps/cycles in reserve; do not chase burn or fatigue. Preserve the source tempo and any counted hold/relaxation. Stop or reduce range/load if control fades.
P: Six challenging primary-strength tasks: two from each force course plus one upper and one lower rotational support. Use about 2–3 technical reps/cycles in reserve with controlled lowering/range. No forced reps, failure/max testing or breathless circuit. Same-lift preparation is separate from working sets; extra load finding adds actual work/time.

The original force-course doses and preparation stay with their source exercises. Added rotational support uses the clearly stated smaller combined dose and its own easy preparation. A new class or changed position in the sequence does not justify a load increase. Judge late-session technical reserve and record reductions rather than forcing nominal completion.

full-body-force.title: Review lead-leg and arm sequence
full-body-force.effort: Review a low hip-led rotational kick with lateral recovery and a retained upper-body rotational pull. Supported lead-leg work and alternating or independent forward arm actions provide small linear-force support; no improvement is inferred without matched actual records.
full-body-force.delivery: Estimate 55–62 minutes after Access & Prepare 1 with prompt equipment access. Includes selected work, resets, side/set recovery, new-order transitions, same-lift preparation and 12–18 minutes extra instruction/setup. Additional recovery, queues or load finding add actual time. Existing preparation and complete booking duration remain unresolved. Never shorten needed recovery to fit a clock. Class numbers specify 36 ordered exposures, not consecutive days or a fixed 36-week calendar. Review actual sport, lifting, throwing, kicking, running, jumping and separate tumbling before scheduling. Roughly 48–72 hours between comparably demanding exposures is an initial planning allowance, adjusted to actual recovery. Do not also perform the standalone source workouts or double up missed classes. No athlete completion or readiness is inferred from a saved class.
full-body-force.preparation: Complete the existing predetermined Access & Prepare 1, unchanged and supplied separately. Its exercises, duration and workload are not recreated or assumed. Review its actual demands before this full-body class.
full-body-force.setup: Inspect all loads, stable supports, band/landmine attachments, surfaces and athlete fit. Use the three separate 10 m lanes with complete setup, action and receiving/stopping envelopes inside the available space; do not combine them into a 30 m runway. Clear waiting/return paths outside active ball and swept-leg areas. Ball flight, impact, bounce and roll containment require a separately verified area; no throwing wall or rebound behavior is assumed. Only tasks that explicitly prescribe a feed or receiving action include it; all other releases are no-catch. Retrieve only after the ball stops and the coach clears entry into the area. Low kicks are noncontact and below hip height, with active recoil and no knee snap or spin; qualify kicking competence during the prescribed first attempts. For a handoff, secure the ball and let the feeder release and step clear before turning; no airborne feed is added. Finish each exercise and its recovery, then clear/reset the area before the next. Mechanical connections do not authorize simultaneous jump/kick/throw combinations or supersets. Before multiple substitutions, check that they do not duplicate another slot; otherwise stop the affected work and record a modified/incomplete delivery for revision.
full-body-force.quality: Main observation: Low roundhouse with lateral recovery placement. Within its listed attempts, record the declared starting position, side, movement/receiving control and a stable finish. Also record the partner task in the first connection under its own criteria; do not treat unlike drills as equivalent force tests. For a repeated source reference, compare only an actually recorded earlier combined occurrence with matching dose, actual equipment, stance, arm strategy, range, reset, side/set rest, preparation and order. An unmatched or missing baseline is not zero or improvement. E2 matches the prescribed execution/dose in combined Class 8; E3 matches the prescribed execution/dose in combined Class 18; E6 matches the prescribed execution/dose in combined Class 3. A miss consumes the attempt; no additional testing slots or retries are added.
full-body-force.explosiveNotes: Open with Low roundhouse with lateral recovery placement as the grounded rotational force anchor. Control the return leg when restoring a base slightly off the original line after rotational output. Review current quality under matched recorded conditions where available; do not infer improvement from absent baseline data.
full-body-force.progression:
Low roundhouse with lateral recovery placement changes the final low kick's recovery to a short lateral placement and is capped at one attempt per side, while Rotational band row speed drive keeps the rotational pull familiar. The supported leg tasks remain small and grounded; Floor Press — alternating light speed presses, opposite arm parked adds four alternating presses total, two per arm, with the opposite load parked rather than adding simultaneous pressing volume. Compared with Class 35, prescribed ball releases change from 6 to 4, kick actions change from 4 to 2, explosive set/side bouts change from 10 to 11. Before final delivery, check actual recovery and require the recovery foot to finish clear of the support knee without continued spinning, plus stable control of the parked dumbbell. Shorten only remaining kick arcs or recovery widths if necessary. If alternating press control fails, apply the listed bilateral conversion only to remaining equivalent arm work: two unperformed alternating presses become one bilateral cycle. Preserve recovery, record changed counting and use actual observations to set the next cycle; no make-up work or improvement claim is added. Stop and log an unmatched single-arm remainder instead of rounding it up to another bilateral cycle.

Previous combined Class 35 prescribed 11 primary bouts and 57 conventional/traverse reps plus 2 cycles; this class prescribes 8 bouts, 46 reps and 0 cycles. This is a redistributed task dose, not an earned load increase. This third lesson completes stage coverage and repeats the selected light supports for the stated shoulder/hip/foot jobs. Original force doses/within-task recovery and same-lift preparation are retained; rotational additions are separately reduced. Advance only after actual controlled execution at the target reserve and satisfactory recovery. Hold, reduce or revise if feedback or first-attempt quality does not support the new constraint.

E: Six separate explosive tasks: two upper force, two lower force, one upper rotation and one lower rotation. The opener is today’s main quality observation; every other task has a specific supporting job. Use bodyweight/light resistance and rapid intent with controlled execution, preserving the written reset and side/set recovery. Extend rest to 2–3 minutes when needed. A miss consumes the attempt; no bonus test or make-up reps.

Stop for pain, unsafe implement path, trapped support knee, uncontrolled reception, lost alignment or clear slowing. Regress only remaining work when control returns; otherwise log the stopped slot. Source alternative doses are capped by the remaining combined dose. No new flight is added by the rotational selections.
S: Exactly two light strengthening tasks, one for each region. Keep at least 5 technical reps/cycles in reserve; do not chase burn or fatigue. Preserve the source tempo and any counted hold/relaxation. Stop or reduce range/load if control fades.
P: Six challenging primary-strength tasks: two from each force course plus one upper and one lower rotational support. Use about 2–3 technical reps/cycles in reserve with controlled lowering/range. No forced reps, failure/max testing or breathless circuit. Same-lift preparation is separate from working sets; extra load finding adds actual work/time.

The original force-course doses and preparation stay with their source exercises. Added rotational support uses the clearly stated smaller combined dose and its own easy preparation. A new class or changed position in the sequence does not justify a load increase. Judge late-session technical reserve and record reductions rather than forcing nominal completion.

Load the turning arc and controlled endpoints that transmit lower-body force into the selected upper rotational action. Secure the landmine and qualify the bar, grip and minimum load. Hold the sleeve or suitable grip in both hands with elbows softly bent. Turn the feet and hips with a modest side-to-side loaded arc while keeping ribs over pelvis. Each one-way traverse is one rep; the return is the next counted rep. Take about 2 seconds per traverse and settle briefly at each endpoint. Avoid trunk lean, a trapped knee or an uncontrolled finish. Use instead: Reduce the load or arc for loss of alignment. If a secured, manageable landmine setup cannot be qualified, use a standing two-hand band rotation with a verified side anchor and the same one-way traverse counting instead; log the changed setup.
